players.name: O. Benbot
players.note: He retired from the national team, then changed his mind when an injury crisis thinned out Algeria's goalkeeping options. The home-based USM Alger man is back, slightly to his own surprise.

players.name: M. Mastil
players.note: France-born and on loan in the Swiss second tier, he had hernia surgery that left his tournament in doubt. A long way from the spotlight for a man hoping to make a World Cup squad.

players.name: L. Zidane
players.note: Yes, that Zidane: Zinedine's son, a goalkeeper who has chosen Algeria over France. He carries the most famous surname in the squad and quietly minds the goal for Granada.

players.name: A. Abada
players.note: A no-frills defender who made his name in the Algerian league with Chlef and earned a domestic move on the back of it. One of the few in the squad who has never left home.

players.name: R. Aït-Nouri
players.note: After five seasons quietly impressing at Wolves, the attacking left-back earned a big-money move to Manchester City in 2025. He likes to bomb forward, which is half the fun of watching him.

players.name: Z. Belaïd
players.note: A centre-back who signed for storied home club JS Kabylie in 2025. He is one of the squad's locally-based options, plying his trade in front of Algeria's own crowds rather than Europe's.

players.name: R. Belghali
players.note: A right-back who became one of Verona's standouts and got bigger Italian clubs taking notice. Injuries kept interrupting his breakout, but the talent is not in question.

players.name: R. Bensebaïni
players.note: A left-sided defender who chips in goals more than most, though back trouble has him scrapping for a starting place at Dortmund. Useful from the penalty spot when Algeria need it.

players.name: S. Chergui
players.note: A defender at the recently risen Paris FC, the capital's quieter, less-glamorous club. He is one of the squad's understated options rather than a household name.

players.name: J. Hadjam
players.note: A France-born left-back who picked Algeria and scored his first international goals during the qualifying run. At 22, he is the youthful alternative down that flank to Aït-Nouri.

players.name: A. Mandi
players.note: Algeria's most-capped player ever and a survivor of the 2014 World Cup, now the calm elder of the back line at Lille. If anyone in this squad has seen it all before, it is him.

players.name: M. Tougai
players.note: An Algiers-born centre-back who plays his club football next door in Tunisia with continental heavyweights Espérance. He even chips in the odd goal from the back.

players.name: H. Aouar
players.note: Once a Lyon prodigy, he switched to Algeria and is now enjoying the most prolific scoring of his career in Saudi Arabia. A creative midfielder who has finally found his goal touch.

players.name: N. Bentaleb
players.note: He suffered a cardiac arrest in 2024 and was told he might never play again, then returned eight months later and scored on his Lille comeback. The most remarkable story in the squad, no contest.

players.name: H. Boudaoui
players.note: A tireless central midfielder now in his seventh season at Nice, the kind of player teammates rate more than headlines do. He does the unglamorous running so others can shine.

players.name: I. Maza
players.note: Germany capped him at youth level, but Petkovic persuaded the 18-year-old to choose Algeria instead. Now 20 and a breakout name at Leverkusen, he is the squad's most exciting young creator.

players.name: Y. Titraoui
players.note: A Paradou academy graduate who has become one of Belgium's steadier midfielders at Charleroi, with English clubs circling. At 22, this is his big audition.

players.name: R. Zerrouki
players.note: A holding midfielder who returned on loan to Twente, the Dutch club he started at, after a Feyenoord move never quite clicked. He is the squad's screen in front of the back four.

players.name: F. Chaïbi
players.note: A French-Algerian playmaker who has become a key creator at Frankfurt, racking up assists from a deeper role or as a number 10. Watch him for the clever pass nobody else saw.

players.name: M. Amoura
players.note: Algeria's qualifying top scorer, who led the line with goals to spare and grabbed his first international hat-trick along the way. A quick, sharp Bundesliga finisher who is the team's main goal threat.

players.name: A. Benbouali
players.note: A Paradou-trained striker who has banged in goals by the bucketload in Hungary's top flight, earning a late look from Petkovic. Proof that the goals count wherever you score them.

players.name: A. Boulbina
players.note: A left winger who exploded at Paradou before cashing in with a move to Qatar's Al-Duhail. At 22 he carries plenty of trickery, even if the league switch is a quieter stage.

players.name: F. Ghedjemis
players.note: A winger who turned down richer offers to fire Frosinone to promotion as their top scorer, and credits Mahrez as his inspiration. Loyalty and ambition in roughly equal measure.

players.name: A. Gouiri
players.note: France's top scorer at a youth Euros who chose to play for Algeria, then hit double figures in half a season after a big move to Marseille. A versatile forward at home leading the line or drifting wide.

players.name: A. Hadj-Moussa
players.note: A winger who lit up the last AFCON and stunned Manchester City in the Champions League, with Chelsea among those now sniffing around. Direct, fearless, and the squad's most likely breakout.

players.name: R. Mahrez
players.note: The captain and the star: a Leicester title-winner, Manchester City treble champion, and the man whose free-kick won Algeria the 2019 AFCON. At 34 in Saudi Arabia, this is likely his last World Cup, and that left foot still does the talking.

players.name: E. Martínez
players.note: Argentina's undisputed No. 1 and a genuine folk hero at home after the penalty heroics that won the 2022 final and the shootouts of two Copa Americas. Loud, theatrical and very good at getting inside opponents' heads, he is the one keeper Scaloni never has to think twice about.

players.name: J. Musso
players.note: A reliable, low-drama goalkeeper now at Atletico Madrid who is here as a steady third pair of hands rather than a starter. The kind of squad member who trains hard, says little and would only see the pitch if something went badly wrong ahead of him.

players.name: G. Rulli
players.note: The likely backup keeper, an experienced campaigner at Marseille who has knocked about the game in Spain and France for years. He has a knack for the dramatic, having once saved a penalty in the final seconds to win Argentina an Olympic gold, so he is calmer than most when it matters.

players.name: L. Balerdi
players.note: Marseille's captain and a centre-back who turned a rocky early career into one of the steadier defensive seasons in France. He is the next man up behind Argentina's first-choice pairing, which at a tournament this long is far from a quiet job.

players.name: Lisandro Martínez
players.note: Half of Argentina's first-choice centre-back duo, a left-footed defender who plays like he has a personal grudge against the ball. Small for the position but ferociously aggressive, he is one of those defenders forwards quietly dread spending ninety minutes against.

players.name: F. Medina
players.note: A Marseille defender comfortable at centre-back or left-back, which is exactly the kind of two-in-one flexibility Scaloni likes to pack into a 26-man squad. He arrived from Lens in a sizeable move and gives Argentina cover across the whole left side of the back line.

players.name: N. Molina
players.note: A galloping right-back at Atletico Madrid who loves nothing more than bombing forward, best remembered for setting up Argentina's opener in the 2022 final. Quick and direct going forward, occasionally caught out coming back, which is the eternal trade-off with attacking full-backs.

players.name: G. Montiel
players.note: A right-back back home at River Plate after a spell in Europe, and the man who calmly tucked away the winning penalty in the 2022 World Cup final shootout. Whatever else happens in his career, he will always be the one who kicked the trophy home.

players.name: N. Otamendi
players.note: At 37, the elder statesman of the back line and a one-man link to nearly every Argentina campaign of the last decade. Still tough as old boots at Benfica, he is the experienced voice Scaloni leans on when the pairing in front of him needs a rest.

players.name: C. Romero
players.note: Known to everyone as 'Cuti,' the Tottenham centre-back is the other half of Argentina's preferred defensive pairing and not a man who shies away from a battle. He shrugged off a knee scare in the build-up and brings the kind of front-foot aggression that sets the tone for the whole team.

players.name: N. Tagliafico
players.note: A left-back with stacks of international miles on the clock, now at Lyon and heading to another World Cup. Reliable and uncomplicated, he is the sort of full-back who quietly does his job for the full ninety while the headlines go to others.

players.name: V. Barco
players.note: A 21-year-old known as 'Colo,' an adventurous left-back at Strasbourg who treats overlapping runs as a personal calling. One of Argentina's brightest young defensive prospects, he plays like he is permanently set to fast-forward while everyone else moves at normal speed.

players.name: E. Fernández
players.note: Argentina's midfield engine at just 24, a Chelsea man who was named the best young player of the 2022 World Cup he helped win. He covers enormous ground and breaks up play, the kind of all-action presence that lets the creative types ahead of him do the fun stuff.

players.name: G. Lo Celso
players.note: A creative midfielder at Real Betis who, when fit, supplies the clever passing and set-piece quality that loosens stubborn defences. Injuries have interrupted his career more than once, so a healthy spell at the right moment makes him a useful card to have.

players.name: A. Mac Allister
players.note: A Liverpool midfielder who does a bit of everything and rarely gives the ball away, one of the steadier members of the 2022-winning core. Tidy, intelligent and a good runner, he is the type who makes the job look easier than it is.

players.name: E. Palacios
players.note: A combative central midfielder at Bayer Leverkusen who can both protect the defence and step into a tackle without flinching. He chipped in with important goals during Leverkusen's recent rise, so he is more than just a destroyer when the moment calls for it.

players.name: L. Paredes
players.note: A deep-lying playmaker now back home at Boca Juniors, the man who dictates tempo from the base of midfield and floats in dangerous set-pieces. A veteran of the 2022 triumph, he is the metronome the rest of the side plays around.

players.name: N. González
players.note: A versatile attacking midfielder at Atletico Madrid who can fill in across the front and supply goals and assists from wide or central areas. He missed the cut for Qatar 2022 at the very last moment, so this tournament is something of a long-awaited second chance.

players.name: R. De Paul
players.note: Messi's self-appointed bodyguard on the pitch and now his clubmate again at Inter Miami, having reunited with his captain in 2025. A relentless, talkative midfielder whose job is partly to run and partly to make sure nobody gets near the No. 10.

players.name: T. Almada
players.note: A creative attacker now at Atletico Madrid with a left foot built for through balls and a fondness for spectacular goals. He was a surprise late call-up to the winning Qatar squad as a youngster, so a tournament has a way of putting him in the right place.

players.name: J. Álvarez
players.note: A relentless, do-everything forward at Atletico Madrid who scored four times in Argentina's 2022 triumph despite barely starting the campaign. Happy to play through the middle, out wide or as a chasing nuisance, he is the kind of striker managers build whole game plans around.

players.name: N. Paz
players.note: At 21, the squad's most exciting young playmaker, a classic No. 10 at Como who lit up Serie A and dragged his club into Europe for the first time. Born in Spain to Argentine football roots, he shook off a late knee scare to make Messi's final World Cup squad.

players.name: J. López
players.note: A tall striker nicknamed 'Flaco' who earns his living at Palmeiras in Brazil, one of the least-capped names in the squad. He impressed Scaloni enough in recent call-ups to leapfrog more familiar faces, which tells you something about the form he is in.

players.name: Lautaro Martínez
players.note: Inter Milan's prolific striker and the man wearing the goals burden when Messi drops deeper, fresh off being top scorer at the last Copa America and scoring the winner in the final. A ruthless, instinctive finisher who is now firmly Argentina's No. 9.

players.name: L. Messi
players.note: The captain, the 38-year-old who has won everything and is set for a record sixth World Cup, almost certainly his last. Three goals short of the all-time tournament scoring record, he plays a little deeper these days but still bends games to his will when it counts.

players.name: G. Simeone
players.note: A tireless winger at Atletico Madrid and, yes, the son of his manager there, Diego Simeone. He earned his place on hard running and relentless pressing rather than the family name, the sort of player who chases lost causes until they stop being lost.

players.name: P. Beach
players.note: At 22 he's the kid keeper of the group, here off the back of helping Melbourne City lift the 2024/25 A-League title. First major tournament, so don't expect minutes, but he's the one quietly learning from Ryan.

players.name: P. Izzo
players.note: A late bloomer who waited years for his shot and finally debuted at 30, keeping a clean sheet against New Zealand. The patient understudy who took the long way round, via Melbourne Victory and now Denmark.

players.name: M. Ryan
players.note: The captain and the heartbeat, north of 100 caps and heading to a fourth World Cup, which ties the Australian record held by Cahill and Milligan. Saved a penalty on his 100th cap to help send the team to this tournament, so the big moments don't faze him.

players.name: A. Behich
players.note: At 35 he's one of the most capped Socceroos ever, a left-back who debuted back in 2012 and has barely missed a tournament since. The dependable old hand who came home to Melbourne and is still doing the unglamorous defensive shift.

players.name: J. Bos
players.note: An attacking left-back who earned a move to Feyenoord and promptly chipped in with goals and assists from defence. One of the genuine bright sparks of this squad, the kind of full-back who treats the touchline as a runway.

players.name: C. Burgess
players.note: A Scotland-born centre-back who plays his club football in the Championship with Swansea and helped see Australia through qualifying. Steady rather than flashy, the sort of defender you only notice when he's not there.

players.name: A. Circati
players.note: A 22-year-old centre-back holding down a Serie A starting spot at Parma, and after a month of pre-tournament camp he looks set to partner Souttar. Young, composed, and answering every question asked of him at exactly the right time.

players.name: J. Geria
players.note: A right-back and Melbourne Victory club legend who'd been out of the national setup for eight years before Popovic called him back in. Proof it's never quite over, even at 32 with 200-odd A-League games behind you.

players.name: L. Herrington
players.note: At 18 he's the youngest in the squad, a Brisbane Roar academy product who made his pro debut only in late 2024 and then materialised on a World Cup roster almost out of nowhere. A genuine bolt-from-the-blue selection who'll be soaking it all in.

players.name: H. Souttar
players.note: All 6ft 6in of him anchors the back line, and his older brother John plays the same position for Scotland, the country Harry left to play for Australia. A set-piece threat at both ends, which is what happens when you put the tallest man on the pitch in the box.

players.name: M. Degenek
players.note: Serbian-born and refreshingly blunt off the pitch, he's heading to his third World Cup with grit to spare. His club career has wandered from Germany to Japan to Serbia, and he brings that well-travelled steel to the back three.

players.name: J. Italiano
players.note: A Perth-raised defender who spent five years in Borussia Monchengladbach's reserves before finding regular first-team football in Austria. He once scored a hat-trick from defence with a couple of screamers, which is not the usual full-back job description.

players.name: K. Trewin
players.note: A ball-playing defender who swept Melbourne City's individual awards during their title season and only debuted for Australia in late 2025. The versatile type who can slot in almost anywhere across the back, which is exactly why he's here.

players.name: J. Irvine
players.note: Captain at St Pauli and one of Australia's most important midfielders, the engine who can both break things up and play. The Guardian's pick of the squad, though he's had to fight his way back from foot surgery to make it, which tells you how much this means to him.

players.name: C. Devlin
players.note: A defensive midfielder making a living in the Scottish Premiership with Hearts, the one who does the tackling so the more eye-catching names don't have to. Cut his teeth in New Zealand and Sydney before the move to Edinburgh.

players.name: A. O Neill
players.note: A defensive midfielder who swapped Belgium for New York City in early 2025 and gives the side a calm presence at the base. The kind of player whose value shows up in the spaces he closes rather than the highlight reel.

players.name: Paul Okon-Engstler
players.note: The son of former Socceroos captain Paul Okon, and now part of dad's old assistant-coach setup as a 20-year-old in his own right. Schooled at Club Brugge and Benfica's academies, he's the next-generation name to keep an eye on.

players.name: C. Metcalfe
players.note: Shares a Bundesliga dressing room with captain Irvine at St Pauli, a box-to-box midfielder who keeps things ticking. A Melbourne City product who's quietly built a solid career in Germany.

players.name: A. Hrustic
players.note: An attacking midfielder with a lovely left foot, now plying his trade in the Eredivisie with Heracles after spells at bigger German clubs. Wears the number 10 and carries the set-piece responsibility that tends to come with it.

players.name: C. Volpato
players.note: A Sydney-raised attacker who came up through Italy's youth ranks and switched his allegiance to Australia at the eleventh hour, landing in the squad days later. A Serie A creator with something to prove, and the most last-minute story in the group.

players.name: N. Irankunda
players.note: Born in a refugee camp after his family fled Burundi, raised in Adelaide, and once clocked as one of the fastest players to grace the Bundesliga. A genuine speed merchant now at Watford, and there's talk Popovic may even use him through the middle.

players.name: M. Leckie
players.note: The man who scored the goal that sent Australia past Denmark and into the last 16 in 2022, a moment that still gets replayed on loop back home. At 34 he's the experienced forward who knows exactly what these nights are worth.

players.name: A. Mabil
players.note: Born in Kenya's Kakuma refugee camp, raised in Adelaide, and later named Young Australian of the Year for his charity work with refugees. He scored one of the penalties that booked the 2022 World Cup spot, so the pressure moments are familiar territory.

players.name: T. Yengi
players.note: An uncapped striker until this squad, he forced his way in on the back of a loan spell in Japan that took Machida Zelvia to a continental final. The physical, out-of-nowhere bolter, and he spent years in his brother Kusini's shadow before this.

players.name: M. Touré
players.note: Born a refugee in Guinea, he became the youngest goalscorer in A-League history at 15 and now wears the number 9 in Denmark. Comes from a footballing family, with both brothers having played alongside him at Adelaide, and may well lead the line here.

players.name: N. Velupillay
players.note: A Melbourne Victory winger who scored on his international debut against China within minutes of coming off the bench, the dream way to introduce yourself. A quick, direct option off the flank who's earned his place through A-League form.

players.name: P. Pentz
players.note: A keeper who once held down Austria's number one shirt and has since taken his trade to Denmark with Brondby. He's the experienced cover in this squad rather than the first name on the teamsheet.

players.name: A. Schlager
players.note: The Salzburg goalkeeper who looks set to wear the number one shirt in North America, wearing it on his back here too. A steady, unfussy presence who has worked his way up to being Rangnick's trusted pick.

players.name: F. Wiegele
players.note: The youngest of the three keepers, now plying his trade in the Czech league with Plzen. He's third in the pecking order, so a tournament here is more about learning the ropes than expecting to play.

players.name: D. Affengruber
players.note: A centre-back who made his name at Sturm Graz before taking the leap to Spain with Elche. He's part of the newer crop in defence, the sort of player who has to earn his minutes around the established names.

players.name: D. Alaba
players.note: The captain and by some distance the biggest name Austria has, a Real Madrid defender with four Champions League winner's medals split between Madrid and Bayern. At 33 this is almost certainly his one shot at a World Cup, and the whole team is built around getting him there.

players.name: K. Danso
players.note: Austria's Premier League centre-back, now at Tottenham, and the sort of strong, no-nonsense defender you want alongside the ageing captain. Quick across the ground and happy to do the unglamorous work that keeps a back line honest.

players.name: M. Friedl
players.note: Captain of Werder Bremen and comfortable at either centre-back or left-back, which makes him exactly the kind of flexible body a coach loves to have. He carries the quiet authority of someone used to leading a Bundesliga dressing room.

players.name: P. Lienhart
players.note: A long-serving Freiburg centre-back who has spent years as one of the more reliable defenders in the Bundesliga without ever shouting about it. Dependable rather than flashy, which is its own kind of compliment for a defender.

players.name: P. Mwene
players.note: A Vienna-born full-back at Mainz who took the long way to the national team, having once been eligible for Kenya through his father. The kind of steady wide defender who keeps his shirt by rarely putting a foot wrong.

players.name: S. Posch
players.note: A Mainz defender who can fill in at right-back or centre-back depending on what the day asks for, which is handy in a tournament squad. That versatility means he's rarely far from a game, even if he's not always the first pick.

players.name: M. Svoboda
players.note: A defender plying his trade in Italy with Venezia, and one of the less familiar faces in this back line. He's squad depth here, the sort of name that surprises a few fans when it's read out.

players.name: C. Baumgartner
players.note: A Leipzig attacking midfielder who was Austrian Footballer of the Year in 2024 and chips in with goals from the space between the lines. He chimed in during qualifying too, including a share of the spoils in a 10-0 romp over San Marino.

players.name: C. Chukwuemeka
players.note: Born in Vienna but raised in England, the Dortmund midfielder won youth titles in an England shirt before Rangnick talked him into switching to Austria early in 2026. He marked his decision in the best possible way, scoring on his debut against Ghana.

players.name: F. Grillitsch
players.note: A deep-lying midfielder with more than fifty caps, now in Portugal with Braga after spells at Hoffenheim and a brief stop at Ajax. The calm one who breaks up play and starts moves from the back, the type you only notice when he's missing.

players.name: K. Laimer
players.note: The Bayern Munich midfielder and reigning Austrian Footballer of the Year, the engine who covers every blade of grass so others don't have to. The Guardian's pick as the team's standout, and the kind of relentless runner Rangnick's pressing game is built on.

players.name: A. Prass
players.note: A wing-back who broke through at Sturm Graz before earning his Bundesliga move to Hoffenheim. He gives Austria energy and width down the flank, the legs to get up and down all afternoon.

players.name: M. Sabitzer
players.note: A Dortmund midfielder with a CV that takes in Bayern, Leipzig and Manchester United, and one of the more experienced heads in the middle of the park. He carries a thumping shot and the kind of box-to-box engine that suits a high-pressing side.

players.name: X. Schlager
players.note: A combative central midfielder at Leipzig who shares both a surname and a club with goalkeeper Alexander, though the two aren't related. He's the ball-winner of the side, all bite and tackles in front of the back four.

players.name: R. Schmid
players.note: A creative midfielder at Werder Bremen, where he lines up alongside captain Marco Friedl for club and country alike. He's one of the lighter, more inventive options in the middle, good for a clever pass when the game needs unlocking.

players.name: A. Schöpf
players.note: A midfielder who spent his best years in the Bundesliga with Schalke before coming home to play for Wolfsberger in the Austrian top flight. A late call-up at 31, the experienced squad man rewarded for finding his form again back in his own league.

players.name: N. Seiwald
players.note: A Leipzig midfielder who followed the well-trodden Salzburg-to-Leipzig pipeline and is one of the squad's listed key players despite still being only 24. A tidy, hard-running passer who keeps the team ticking over without much fuss.

players.name: P. Wanner
players.note: At 20, the baby of the squad, a Bayern Munich talent spending the season on loan at PSV to get regular minutes. He came through Germany's youth ranks but threw his lot in with Austria in 2025, and Rangnick fast-tracked him in.

players.name: P. Wimmer
players.note: A tricky wide forward at Wolfsburg who likes to run at defenders and cut inside off the flank. He gives Rangnick a different kind of threat out wide, more dribble than muscle.

players.name: M. Arnautovic
players.note: At 36, Austria's most-capped player and all-time leading scorer, now playing at Red Star Belgrade after years in the Premier League and Serie A. He top-scored in qualifying with eight goals, proof the old gunslinger still fancies the big stage.

players.name: M. Gregoritsch
players.note: The Augsburg striker who provided the moment that mattered most, a late equaliser against Bosnia that sealed top spot and the ticket to North America. Austria's second-top scorer in qualifying, the unsung foil to Arnautovic up front.

players.name: S. Kalajdzic
players.note: A two-metre target man whose career was nearly ended by three separate cruciate ligament tears that cost him close to a thousand days. A loan to LASK to rebuild rescued him, and this call-up is the happy ending to a long, grim road back.

players.name: T. Courtois
players.note: Real Madrid's giant goalkeeper sat out Belgium for nearly two years after falling out with the old manager, then came back under Rudi Garcia with one goal in mind: the World Cup. Tall enough to fill a goal on his own, and one of the best in the world at doing exactly that.

players.name: S. Lammens
players.note: A penalty-saving specialist who left Antwerp for Manchester United on deadline day and quickly won over a tough crowd, earning a Premier League transfer-of-the-season nod. Here he's the understudy keeping Courtois honest in training.

players.name: M. Penders
players.note: One of the youngest names in the squad, a Chelsea-owned keeper learning the trade on loan in France. He won't play a minute unless something goes very wrong, but being here at all is the reward for a precocious debut season at Genk — Owned by Chelsea, on a season-long loan at Strasbourg.

players.name: T. Castagne
players.note: The kind of dependable full-back every team needs, equally happy down the right or the left, with an FA Cup from his Leicester days in the cupboard. After ankle surgery cut short last season at Fulham, this is his fourth major tournament for Belgium.

players.name: M. De Cuyper
players.note: An attacking left-back who racked up titles at Club Brugge before a big-money move to Brighton last summer. He likes to push forward and create, so think of him as a winger who also defends.

players.name: K. De Winter
players.note: A versatile defender who came through Juventus's academy, made his name at Genoa, then sealed a 'dream' move to AC Milan. He can slot in anywhere across the back line, which is exactly why managers love him.

players.name: Z. Debast
players.note: An Anderlecht graduate who moved to Sporting in Portugal and announced himself by scoring against Lille on his Champions League debut. Comfortable as a centre-back or sitting in midfield, he's one of the young faces Belgium is building around.

players.name: B. Mechele
players.note: A true one-club man who joined Club Brugge at the age of six and has since racked up more than 500 appearances and a stack of league titles. The kind of steady, no-fuss defender who only gets noticed when he's not there.

players.name: T. Meunier
players.note: The squad's old hand at right-back, with PSG and Borussia Dortmund behind him and now a steadying presence at Lille. Plenty of caps, plenty of tournaments, and still chipping in the odd goal at 34.

players.name: N. Ngoy
players.note: A Brussels-born centre-back who left Standard Liege for Lille and impressed with his reading of the game more than brute strength. Injuries slowed his start, but he's now seen as one of Belgium's brightest defensive prospects.

players.name: J. Seys
players.note: A flying full-back who shot up from Club Brugge's reserves to the first team in a matter of months and was named the league's best young player. Quick and tidy on the ball, he's already got the big Premier League clubs taking notes.

players.name: A. Theate
players.note: A left-footed defender who once became the most expensive Belgian defender ever when Rennes signed him, and now anchors the back line at Eintracht Frankfurt. Equally at home in the middle or out on the left.

players.name: K. De Bruyne
players.note: After a decade and a trophy cabinet's worth of medals at Manchester City, Belgium's finest passer moved to Napoli on a free and reunited with old pal Lukaku. At 34 this is almost certainly his last World Cup, and that vision and right foot are still the team's beating heart.

players.name: A. Onana
players.note: Born in Senegal and raised in Belgium, this towering midfielder is the muscle in front of the defence and an Europa League winner with Aston Villa. He finally got off the mark for his country with a goal against the USA earlier this year.

players.name: N. Raskin
players.note: A combative, all-action midfielder who has become Rangers' engine room in Scotland, chipping in goals and assists from deep. He only made his Belgium debut last year and is now pushing hard for a starting spot.

players.name: A. Saelemaekers
players.note: A tireless wide player who had a strong loan spell at Roma before settling back in at AC Milan, where he'll do a shift anywhere down the right. The sort of selfless runner whose work often goes unsung.

players.name: Y. Tielemans
players.note: Belgium's captain and a calm, smart midfielder who orchestrates things from the centre for Aston Villa, voted their player of the season and an Europa League winner. He inherited the armband from De Bruyne in 2025 and now sets the tone for this team.

players.name: D. Moreira
players.note: A Liege-born winger-turned-wing-back who came through Benfica and Chelsea before thriving at Strasbourg, and who only switched his allegiance to Belgium last year. Fast, fearless and a nightmare to mark when he gets the ball at his feet.

players.name: H. Vanaken
players.note: A three-time Belgian Footballer of the Year and the brain of Club Brugge's midfield, prized for his vision and an eye for goal. A bit of a throwback to an old-school playmaker, and proof you don't have to leave the home league to be brilliant.

players.name: A. Witsel
players.note: The elder statesman of the squad, a composed deep-lying midfielder now playing in Spain for Girona after years at the top with Atletico and Dortmund. He scored against Barcelona this season just to remind everyone he's still got it.

players.name: J. Doku
players.note: Manchester City's electric winger and arguably the player most likely to win Belgium a game on his own, thanks to dribbling that ties defenders in knots. After a season where his end product finally caught up with the flair, he's the one to watch.

players.name: M. Fernandez-Pardo
players.note: A Brussels-born forward who briefly switched to Spain before changing his mind and committing to Belgium, with much of Europe's elite now circling his Lille form. At 20 he's the squad's wildcard, full of pace and goals across the front line.

players.name: R. Lukaku
players.note: Belgium's all-time top scorer arrives at his fourth World Cup, but a muscle injury wrecked his Napoli season and the manager has already said he won't start the opener. A big, powerful number nine racing the clock to be fit when it matters.

players.name: D. Lukebakio
players.note: A quick, direct right-winger who was Sevilla's top scorer before joining Benfica, with a knack for both finishing and setting others up. Useful change-of-pace option off the bench when defences need stretching.

players.name: C. De Ketelaere
players.note: A tall, graceful forward whose pricey move to AC Milan flopped badly, only for Atalanta to revive his career with goals and assists by the dozen. A reminder that sometimes a player just needs the right home to come good.

players.name: L. Trossard
players.note: Arsenal's clever forward who pops up with big goals whether he starts or comes off the bench, the definition of a useful man to have around. Left foot, sharp brain, and a habit of scoring in the matches that matter.

players.name: M. Jurkas
players.note: The third keeper, here to train hard and carry the bibs rather than expect minutes. If you see him on the pitch in the group stage, something has gone very wrong for the two in front of him.

players.name: N. Vasilj
players.note: The number one, who spent five seasons at St. Pauli and got promoted to the Bundesliga with them. He's the calm pair of hands Bosnia will lean on when the bigger names come knocking.

players.name: M. Zlomislic
players.note: The backup keeper who quietly does his job at Rijeka, where he's kept a clean sheet in roughly a quarter of his league games this season. Born in Posusje, he's the sort of steady deputy every squad needs and few notice.

players.name: N. Celik
players.note: At 19 he's already a Ligue 1 regular, having left Sarajevo for Lens in a record fee for a Bosnian league player. A towering centre-back who decided his future was in France before most teenagers have finished growing into one.

players.name: A. Dedic
players.note: An attacking right-back who left Salzburg for Benfica in a big-money move and has been chipping in goals and assists in Lisbon. One of the names on Barbarez's keep-an-eye-on list, and the kind of full-back who treats defending as the dull part of the job.

players.name: D. Hadzikadunic
players.note: A tall, right-footed centre-back born in Sweden who chose Bosnia over the country he came up through. His career has wandered from Malmo to Italy, and he's currently holding the line for Sampdoria in Serie B.

players.name: N. Katic
players.note: Once a Rangers favourite who scored a derby winner against Celtic before a bad injury derailed things, he's rebuilt at Schalke and switched his allegiance from Croatia to Bosnia. He admitted to tears after the win that booked this World Cup.

players.name: S. Kolasinac
players.note: The squad's other survivor from the 2014 World Cup alongside Dzeko, with an FA Cup at Arsenal and a Europa League at Atalanta behind him. Twelve years on he's still here, doing the unglamorous defensive shifts so the youngsters can go forward.

players.name: T. Muharemovic
players.note: A 22-year-old centre-back who's become one of Serie A's more talked-about defenders, with the bigger Italian clubs reportedly circling. He helped knock Italy out in the play-off and then said he felt a bit sorry about it, which tells you the sort of player he is.

players.name: N. Mujakic
players.note: A ball-playing defender who's spent his career mostly in Turkey and is on loan at Eyupspor. He grabbed his first international goal in a qualifier against San Marino, the sort of milestone a centre-back tucks away for the grandkids.

players.name: S. Radeljic
players.note: A centre-back who took the scenic route through Stuttgart's reserves, Osijek and a spell in Moldova before winning the Croatian title with Rijeka. A late bloomer who's earned his place rather than been handed it.

players.name: I. Basic
players.note: A midfielder who started out at Zrinjski Mostar and has since taken his trade to Russia and now Kazakhstan with Astana. Plays his club football a long way from the spotlight, which makes a World Cup squad spot all the sweeter.

players.name: A. Gigovic
players.note: A central midfielder born in Sweden who switched to Bosnia and moved to Young Boys, where he marked his European debut for the club with a brace. Energetic in the middle, he's the legs that let the older heads conserve theirs.

players.name: A. Hadziahmetovic
players.note: A defensive midfielder born in Denmark who came up through Zeljeznicar and now anchors things on loan at Hull City. The kind of player who breaks up play and lets the flair merchants take the applause.

players.name: Ermin Mahmic
players.note: A 20-year-old attacking midfielder having a productive season in the Czech league, with goals and assists to his name. His switch from Austria to Bosnia was only cleared by FIFA weeks before the squad was named, so he's a very new face.

players.name: I. Sunjic
players.note: A holding midfielder whose pricey Birmingham City spell never quite clicked, so he reinvented himself in Cyprus and won the title in his first season at Pafos. A reminder that the right move matters more than the biggest one.

players.name: B. Tahirovic
players.note: A deep-lying midfielder who passed through Roma and Ajax before settling at Brondby in Denmark. Still only 22, he played nearly every qualifier and even chipped in a goal, so the rebuild is being built partly around him.

players.name: A. Memic
players.note: Filed as a midfielder but really an attacking creator, he's been one of Plzen's brighter sparks with a healthy haul of goals and assists. Reportedly being eyed by bigger clubs, which usually means a busy summer ahead.

players.name: D. Burnic
players.note: A central midfielder who came through Borussia Dortmund's academy and won the DFB-Pokal there before settling into steady work at Karlsruhe. A former Germany youth player who threw his lot in with Bosnia, and he collects yellow cards like souvenirs.

players.name: Kerim-Sam Alajbegovic
players.note: At 18 he's the squad's baby, a Cologne-born winger who openly dreams of Real Madrid and already has a Europa League wonder goal on his highlight reel. He scored the clinching penalty in the play-off shootout, which is a lot of nerve for someone barely out of school.

players.name: E. Bajraktarevic
players.note: The Appleton, Wisconsin kid nicknamed the "Milwaukee Messi," who came up through the New England Revolution, switched from the US to Bosnia, and now plays for PSV. He set up Dzeko's crucial play-off equaliser, so the American detour worked out rather well for everyone.

players.name: S. Bazdar
players.note: A forward born in Serbia who once represented them before switching to Bosnia in 2024, currently on loan in Poland with Jagiellonia. Young and still finding his level, he's one for the future more than the starting eleven.

players.name: E. Demirovic
players.note: Bosnia's most reliable goal threat after Dzeko, a Stuttgart forward who hits double figures in the Bundesliga and won the German Cup. He's the natural heir to the number nine shirt once the captain finally hangs his up.

players.name: E. Dzeko
players.note: The 39-year-old captain, all-time top scorer and most-capped player, still finding the net and still the focal point of everything Bosnia do going forward. He's the last man standing from the 2014 squad, refusing to let his record-breaking story end before North America.

players.name: J. Lukic
players.note: A late-blooming forward who became the Romanian top flight's leading scorer and player of the season at Universitatea Cluj, the best year of his career by a distance. Proof that the call-up sometimes goes to the man simply scoring the most goals, wherever he happens to play.

players.name: H. Tabakovic
players.note: A near-two-metre target man who flopped at Hoffenheim, then revived his career on loan at Gladbach by climbing the Bundesliga scoring charts behind the likes of Harry Kane. Big, late to bloom, and exactly the sort of aerial nuisance Bosnia can throw on when chasing a game.

players.name: Alisson Becker
players.note: Brazil's first-choice keeper and one of the calmest in the game, equally happy making a point-blank save or starting an attack with a pass off his feet. He has spent years as a Liverpool mainstay, so a packed stadium is nothing new to him.

players.name: Ederson
players.note: The backup keeper famous for treating goal kicks like passing drills, so confident on the ball he sometimes dribbles past forwards inside his own box. After eight trophy-filled years at Manchester City he moved to Turkey with Fenerbahçe in 2025.

players.name: Weverton
players.note: At 38, the elder statesman of the squad and almost certainly here as the third keeper rather than to play. He won Olympic gold with Brazil back in 2016 and has been a steady fixture in goal for Palmeiras for years.

players.name: Alex Sandro
players.note: A vastly experienced left-back who spent the best part of a decade winning league titles at Juventus before heading home to Flamengo. At 34 he leans on positioning and know-how rather than raw pace these days.

players.name: Bremer
players.note: A powerful, no-nonsense centre-back who became Juventus's defensive anchor, though a serious knee injury in late 2024 cost him a long chunk of football. The big question is whether he has fully rediscovered his old sharpness in time.

players.name: Gabriel Magalhães
players.note: Arsenal's commanding left-sided centre-back, the kind of defender who throws himself in front of shots and is a genuine threat from corners at the other end. A knee problem picked up late in the club season is the worry hanging over his tournament.

players.name: Ibañez
players.note: A comfortable, ball-playing centre-back who made his name at Roma before a big-money move to Saudi Arabia's Al-Ahli. He won a European trophy with Roma, so he is no stranger to the big nights.

players.name: Léo Pereira
players.note: A tall, left-footed centre-back who has built his reputation at home with Flamengo rather than chasing a move to Europe. His left foot gives Ancelotti useful balance alongside the more familiar right-footers.

players.name: Marquinhos
players.note: The captain and defensive heartbeat, a long-serving Paris Saint-Germain centre-back who reads the game a step ahead of everyone else. The armband sits naturally on a player this calm under pressure.

players.name: Douglas Santos
players.note: A left-back who has quietly racked up the trophies with Zenit in Russia, which keeps him a little out of the everyday spotlight back home. He offers Ancelotti a tidy, dependable option down the left flank.

players.name: Wesley
players.note: An attacking right-back with a remarkable backstory, having reportedly not kicked a ball seriously until 17 before a Flamengo breakthrough earned him a move to Roma. At 22 he is one of the youngest in the squad and loves bombing forward.

players.name: Danilo
players.note: A do-everything defender who can fill in at right-back or centre-back, and who captained Juventus before bringing all that experience home to Flamengo. That versatility is exactly the sort of insurance a manager wants on the bench.

players.name: Bruno Guimarães
players.note: Newcastle's elegant midfield conductor, the player who keeps the ball moving and ties the defence to the attack. If you only watch the goalscorers you will miss why Brazil's midfield ticks, and the answer is usually him.

players.name: Casemiro
players.note: The squad's serial winner, a holding midfielder who lifted five Champions League titles at Real Madrid and exists to break up the other team's attacks. He is set to leave Manchester United at the end of the season, so this could be a fitting last big stage.

players.name: Fabinho
players.note: A holding midfielder who shielded the back four during Liverpool's best years before moving to the Saudi league with Al-Ittihad. He does the unglamorous screening work that lets the flashier players shine.

players.name: Lucas Paquetá
players.note: West Ham's creative midfielder, all silky touches and clever passes from the centre of the pitch. He spent a long stretch under the cloud of an FA betting investigation before being cleared of the most serious charges, so a clean run at a World Cup is a welcome change.

players.name: Danilo Santos
players.note: A 24-year-old midfielder who stayed in Brazil with Botafogo and earned his call-up through consistently strong domestic form. He is one of the less familiar names here, very much a player making the most of his moment.

players.name: Matheus Cunha
players.note: A restless, skilful forward who can lead the line or drift wide, signed by Manchester United for a hefty fee in 2025. He plays with a bit of needle and never seems to stand still.

players.name: Endrick
players.note: The teenage striker once hyped as the next big thing, who found minutes hard to come by at Real Madrid and went to Lyon on loan to actually play football. At 19 he is the baby of the attack, with everything still in front of him.

players.name: Luiz Henrique
players.note: A direct, dribbling winger who shone for Botafogo before a big move to Zenit in Russia early in 2025. He gives Ancelotti pace and trickery off the bench when a game needs unlocking.

players.name: Gabriel Martinelli
players.note: Arsenal's flying left winger, blessed with the kind of acceleration that turns a half-chance into a goal in a couple of strides. His job off the bench is simple, run tiring defenders into the ground.

players.name: Neymar
players.note: Brazil's all-time top scorer, back at boyhood club Santos and chasing one last World Cup after years of injuries kept interrupting him. A calf strain in the build-up means even getting on the pitch is no certainty, but few players generate this much hope and worry at once.

players.name: Raphinha
players.note: Arrives off a brilliant season at Barcelona where he chipped in with goals and assists in roughly equal measure. A right winger who cuts inside onto his stronger left foot, he is one of Brazil's most reliable sources of end product.

players.name: Rayan
players.note: A 19-year-old winger who burst out of Vasco da Gama and onto Europe's transfer radar before earning his first Brazil caps in early 2026. A genuine bolt-from-the-blue pick whose inclusion turned plenty of heads.

players.name: Thiago
players.note: A proper centre-forward who answered a slow start at Brentford by becoming one of the Premier League's most prolific strikers, finishing the season just behind Erling Haaland in the scoring charts. After a year like that he has earned the right to lead Brazil's line.

players.name: Vinícius Júnior
players.note: The star of the show and Brazil's main attacking threat, a Real Madrid winger whose dribbling can pull a defence apart on its own. The puzzle Ancelotti has to solve is why his ruthless club form has never quite carried over to the national team.

players.name: M. Crépeau
players.note: He came back from a broken leg suffered in the 2022 MLS Cup final, which tells you most of what you need to know about his stubbornness. A safe pair of hands who has waited a long time for a tournament like this.

players.name: O. Goodman
players.note: Born in England but raised in small-town Ontario from age five, he took his citizenship oath in late 2025 just in time to make the squad. A Crystal Palace keeper still collecting his first regular senior minutes out on loan.

players.name: D. St. Clair
players.note: He was named the 2025 MLS Goalkeeper of the Year, only the second Canadian ever to win it, after a season of league-leading saves. The number one shirt and the gloves both look very much like his to lose.

players.name: D. Cornelius
players.note: After falling out of favour at Marseille he took a deadline-day loan to Rangers to get his career back on the pitch. The kind of well-travelled centre-back who has learned to win his place over and over again.

players.name: L. De Fougerolles
players.note: A Fulham academy graduate sent to Belgium on loan to grow up faster, he was Canada's Young Player of the Year for 2025 at just 20. Already trusted enough to share the back line with far older heads.

players.name: R. Laryea
players.note: He spent the back half of 2025 playing nearly every outfield position for Toronto, the squad's reliable handyman. If Davies isn't fit, this is the energetic full-back most likely to step in.

players.name: J. Waterman
players.note: A centre-back who can also fill in at right-back or in midfield, useful for a manager who likes options on his bench. Steady and unflashy, exactly the type you only notice when he's missing.

players.name: A. Johnston
players.note: A reliable fixture at right-back for Celtic, though hamstring trouble cost him big stretches of the 2025-26 season. When he's on the pitch, the whole right side of the team tends to tick along better.

players.name: A. Jones
players.note: Bristol-born and a relative latecomer, he qualifies through an Alberta-born grandmother and only made his Canada debut in late 2025. The newest face in the back line, brought in for his Championship steadiness at centre-back.

players.name: M. Bombito
players.note: The Montreal-born centre-back fractured his leg playing for Nice in October and spent much of the season clawing his way back to fitness. A powerful young defender Marsch clearly wants in this team, injury permitting.

players.name: A. Davies
players.note: Born in a Ghanaian refugee camp and resettled in Edmonton at five, the captain is now the most famous footballer his country has produced. He's still rebuilding after a torn ACL kept him out for most of a year, so his fitness may be the headline of Canada's whole tournament.

players.name: N. Sigur
players.note: Born in Burnaby with dual Croatian citizenship, he switched his allegiance from Croatia to Canada in 2024. A right-back who can also sit in midfield, he has done enough at Hajduk Split to draw scouts from bigger leagues.

players.name: J. Shaffelburg
players.note: A winger from Kentville, Nova Scotia whose entire game is built around frightening pace down the left. He helped Nashville lift the club's first trophy in 2025, then carried that form straight into the national team.

players.name: L. Millar
players.note: He spent nearly a year out with a torn ACL before returning to help Hull win promotion to the Premier League late in the season. A left-sided attacker whose timing to make this squad was tight but ultimately rewarded.

players.name: M. Choinière
players.note: He took the long way round, from Montreal to Switzerland and back to MLS with LAFC, picking up two Canadian Championships along the way. A tidy central midfielder who keeps the ball moving without much fuss.

players.name: S. Eustáquio
players.note: Born in Leamington, Ontario to Portuguese parents, the vice-captain is the calm metronome who sets Canada's tempo from deep. If you want to understand how this team plays, watch where he stands when they have the ball.

players.name: I. Koné
players.note: After a move to Marseille stalled, he chose Sassuolo on loan chasing the regular minutes a young midfielder needs, and the club later made it permanent. A box-to-box runner finally settling into a club where he plays every week.

players.name: J. Osorio
players.note: He has spent his entire career with hometown Toronto FC and holds the club's all-time appearance record, a rare one-club man at 33. This is his second World Cup, and very likely the sentimental veteran of the dressing room.

players.name: N. Saliba
players.note: A Longueuil, Quebec product who left CF Montreal for Anderlecht in 2025 and was once named Canada's Young Player of the Year. At 21 he's one for the future, here mostly to learn from the older midfielders around him.

players.name: M. Flores
players.note: Georgetown, Ontario born and Arsenal academy raised, he switched his allegiance from Mexico to Canada in early 2026 saying Canada simply felt more like home. A creative number ten who can unpick a defence with one clever pass.

players.name: T. Buchanan
players.note: A loan spell at Villarreal went well enough that they signed him outright from Inter Milan, the player saying it helped him rediscover his confidence. Quick and direct on the wing, he can also drop back and cover at full-back when needed.

players.name: J. David
players.note: Canada's all-time leading scorer left Lille on a free transfer to become the first Canadian Juventus have ever signed. His first Serie A season was quieter than he'd like, so a home World Cup is the perfect stage to remind everyone what he does best.

players.name: P. David
players.note: Born in Brampton to Nigerian parents, he was in Nigeria's youth setup before switching to Canada and scoring on his senior debut. His 24 goals helped Union to their first Belgian title in 90 years, the sort of breakout that gets a striker on a plane.

players.name: C. Larin
players.note: Once Canada's all-time top scorer before Jonathan David passed him, he revived his career at Southampton by scoring with his first touch on debut. A penalty-box poacher who has been doing this for the national team for the better part of a decade.

players.name: A. Ahmed
players.note: A winger who lit up 2025 with a pile of assists and a starring role in Vancouver's cup run before earning a move to England. Fearless at taking on defenders, the kind of player a home crowd will lift off their seats for.

players.name: T. Oluwaseyi
players.note: Nigerian-born and Canada-capped, his goals for Minnesota earned a club-record move to Villarreal, where he scored within weeks of arriving. A big, mobile forward giving Marsch a different shape of striker to bring off the bench.

players.name: Márcio Rosa
players.note: The Bulgarian-league keeper who's third in the goalkeeping queue here, which on a first-ever World Cup squad still means a front-row seat to history.

players.name: Vózinha
players.note: At 39 he's the squad's elder statesman and vice-captain, the steady voice who waited his whole career for the islands to finally reach a World Cup.

players.name: C. dos Santos
players.note: Born in the US and once a youth international for the hosts, he switched to his father's Cape Verde and now gets a home World Cup with his MLS club San Diego on the doorstep.

players.name: Diney Borges
players.note: A defender plying his trade in the UAE, one of those quietly-travelled names that make this the most well-stamped passport collection at the tournament.

players.name: Logan Costa
players.note: Born near Paris and once in France's youth ranks, he chose Cape Verde and is now the squad's only man from Europe's top five leagues, anchoring the back line at Villarreal.

players.name: S. Lopes Cabral
players.note: The Dutch-born right-back climbed from German lower divisions to a Benfica move in early 2026, the kind of fast rise that lands you at a debut World Cup at 23.

players.name: Pico
players.note: Dublin-born Roberto Lopes was tracked down through a message online and capped by descent, and now becomes the first active League of Ireland player to grace a World Cup.

players.name: S. Moreira
players.note: Steven Moreira does his defending in MLS with Columbus, so unlike most of his teammates he won't need a map for the long American summer ahead.

players.name: Wagner Pina
players.note: A young full-back earning his keep in Turkey with Trabzonspor, part of the next generation Bubista is folding into this history-making group.

players.name: Kelvin Pires
players.note: His football home is the Finnish league with SJK, about as far from a Group H showdown with Spain as a defender can travel and still get there.

players.name: Stopira
players.note: At 37 he's one of the longest-serving Blue Sharks of all, the sort of loyal old hand who's seen every near-miss and finally gets the payoff.

players.name: Telmo Arcanjo
players.note: A Vitória Guimarães midfielder who adds youthful legs to a side that leans heavily on its veterans, with plenty of room left to grow into the moment.

players.name: Deroy Duarte
players.note: Rotterdam-raised and now at Bulgaria's Ludogorets, he's the younger of two Duarte brothers in this squad, which makes for one very proud household back home.

players.name: L. Duarte
players.note: Laros is the elder Duarte, a former Sparta Rotterdam man now in Hungary, sharing a midfield and a debut World Cup with his little brother Deroy.

players.name: João Paulo
players.note: He patrols the middle for Romania's Oțelul Galați, another of the under-the-radar names whose steady leagues quietly built this remarkable qualifying run.

players.name: Kevin Pina
players.note: Based in Russia with Krasnodar, he's one of the wide runners Bubista can call on to stretch defences that will mostly outrank Cape Verde on paper.

players.name: Jamiro Monteiro
players.note: The Rotterdam-born playmaker spent years lighting up MLS with Philadelphia and San Jose before heading back to the Dutch top flight, and he's the engine in this midfield.

players.name: Yannick Semedo
players.note: Born Jair Semedo Monteiro, this Farense midfielder is a relative latecomer to the cause who timed his arrival perfectly for the islands' big year.

players.name: Garry Rodrigues
players.note: A Rotterdam kid who picked his parents' islands over the Netherlands, he won a Turkish title at Galatasaray and at 35 brings the most glamour to the wing.

players.name: Nuno da Costa
players.note: A French-cup winner with Strasbourg who later had a Nottingham Forest spell, the well-travelled forward now turns out in Istanbul for Başakşehir.

players.name: Jovane Cabral
players.note: Raised in the Sporting academy and once loaned to Lazio, this island-born winger is the rare squad member who actually grew up in Cape Verde rather than the diaspora.

players.name: Willy Semedo
players.note: France-born and now a tidy finisher for Omonia in Cyprus, he's another diaspora pick-up who answered the call to wear the blue.

players.name: Hélio Varela
players.note: At 23 and playing for Maccabi Tel Aviv, he's one of the youngest of the bunch, wearing the symbolic No. 26 shirt for a 26-man trip into the unknown.

players.name: Ryan Mendes
players.note: The captain, 36, is Cape Verde's record scorer and most-capped player, a former Lille man who finally gets to lead the islands out at a World Cup.

players.name: Gilson Benchimol
players.note: A young forward making his way in the Russian league with Akron, handed the No. 9 shirt and the chance to chase the islands' first World Cup goals.

players.name: D. Livramento
players.note: The qualifying campaign's breakout striker, his winner against Cameroon and opener against Eswatini did as much as anyone to drag the islands to a first World Cup.

players.name: Á. Montero
players.note: Millonarios' long-serving number one, tipped to start ahead of the more famous names in goal. At 30 he is, by Colombian keeper standards this tournament, practically a kid.

players.name: D. Ospina
players.note: Colombia's most-capped player ever, back home at Atletico Nacional at 37 for what is almost certainly his last tournament. He may not start, but having him in the room is its own kind of insurance.

players.name: C. Vargas
players.note: The third 30-something keeper in a notably greying goalkeeping group, plying his trade in Mexico's Liga MX with Atlas. More likely to watch than play, but a steady pair of hands if called.

players.name: S. Arias
players.note: A right-back whose career was nearly ended by a brutal ankle break on international duty in 2020. That he is here at 33, still going, tells you most of what you need to know about him.

players.name: W. Ditta
players.note: Voted the best defender in Mexico's top flight for the 2024-25 season, and a Champions Cup winner with Cruz Azul. Quietly become one of the more reliable centre-backs in the region.

players.name: J. Lucumí
players.note: A composed, ball-playing centre-back who has made himself a fixture at Bologna in Serie A. The kind of defender who looks unflustered right up until you realise he has snuffed out the danger.

players.name: D. Machado
players.note: A left-back who moved to Nantes late in 2025 after running short of minutes at Lens. Left-footed and willing to bomb forward, he is competing for a starting berth that is far from settled.

players.name: Y. Mina
players.note: A towering centre-back who topped Serie A for duels won in 2024-25, when he can stay fit. The 'when he can stay fit' has followed him around his whole career, which is the maddening part.

players.name: J. Mojica
players.note: A LaLiga left-back at Mallorca who has built a tidy career out of being dependable rather than flashy. At 33 he provides the experienced cover Colombia want down that side.

players.name: D. Muñoz
players.note: An all-action right-back who became a fan favourite at Crystal Palace and chipped in as they lifted the 2025 FA Cup. He defends one minute and turns up at the back post the next, which is exactly why Colombia love him.

players.name: G. Puerta
players.note: The baby of the squad at 22, a midfielder cutting his teeth in Spain's second tier with Racing Santander. He scored on his senior Colombia debut against New Zealand, which is a fine way to make people remember your name.

players.name: D. Sánchez
players.note: A nailed-on starter at centre-back, now anchoring the defence at Galatasaray in Turkey. Quick across the ground and good in the air, he is the one Colombia build the back line around.

players.name: K. Castaño
players.note: A defensive midfielder who won a Russian title with Krasnodar before becoming one of River Plate's priciest-ever signings. Plenty of technical quality for a player whose main job is breaking things up.

players.name: J. Lerma
players.note: Daniel Munoz's Crystal Palace clubmate, a combative holding midfielder who does the unglamorous covering and tackling. The sort of player you only really notice in the games where he is missing.

players.name: J. Portilla
players.note: A tough-tackling holding midfielder making his name in Argentina with Talleres, and still early into his Colombia career. Brought along as a combative depth option for the engine room.

players.name: J. Arias
players.note: A technically gifted forward-thinking midfielder, now at Wolves, who can drift in off the wing or operate more centrally. Likely part of Colombia's preferred midfield trio rather than a winger this time around.

players.name: J. Carrascal
players.note: A silky attacking midfielder at Flamengo who can produce the unexpected pass or shot. The kind of player who frustrates you for an hour and then wins the game in one moment.

players.name: J. Quintero
players.note: A playmaker with a wand of a left foot, back in Colombia after years bouncing around South America. When the cross or the killer pass is needed, he is the one you want on the ball.

players.name: R. Rios
players.note: A box-to-box midfielder whose rise has been startling, from Brazilian football to Benfica in a couple of seasons. At 25 he may be Colombia's most dangerous engine in the centre of the park.

players.name: J. Rodríguez
players.note: The captain, who won the Golden Boot at the 2014 World Cup and is still pulling the strings at 34. The legs may have slowed, but the left foot has not forgotten a thing.

players.name: J. Campaz
players.note: A small, quick left winger who was tipped as a teenage prospect years ago and has since become a key man at Rosario Central. Direct, two-footed trouble for any full-back.

players.name: J. Córdoba
players.note: A powerful centre-forward who became Krasnodar's all-time leading scorer and won the Russian league's golden boot. Whatever you think of the league, the man simply keeps putting the ball in the net.

players.name: C. Hernández
players.note: Known to everyone as Cucho, a forward at Real Betis with a habit of scoring outrageous, acrobatic goals. Unpredictable in the best sense, which makes him a genuine wildcard off the bench or from the start.

players.name: L. Díaz
players.note: The Guardian's pick of the squad and the man Colombia's attack runs through, fresh off a flying first season at Bayern after his Liverpool years. Give him space on the left and bad things happen to defenders.

players.name: A. Gómez
players.note: At 23, a winger who earned a permanent deal at Brazil's Vasco da Gama after impressing on loan. One of the squad's young wildcards, picked as much for what he might become as what he is now.

players.name: L. Suárez
players.note: A striker in the form of his life at Sporting, where the goals have arrived almost weekly. Not to be confused with the other, more notorious Luis Suarez, and rather keen to write his own headlines.

players.name: M. Epolo
players.note: The youngest name in the squad, a 20-year-old keeper who came up through Standard Liege. He's the long-shot understudy here, more likely to be soaking it all in than starting.

players.name: T. Fayulu
players.note: A keeper who's wandered far from the bright leagues to find regular football, these days minding the net in Armenia. Steady and well-travelled, the kind who knows exactly what a tournament squad needs from him.

players.name: L. Mpasi
players.note: The most experienced of the three keepers and the one wearing the number one, plying his trade in France's top flight at Le Havre. At 31 he's the safe pair of hands the Leopards lean on.

players.name: D. Batubinsika
players.note: A centre-back who moved to Greece's Larisa early in 2026, having helped DR Congo grind to the last 16 at the Africa Cup of Nations. Not flashy, just the sort who throws himself in front of things.

players.name: G. Kalulu
players.note: A right-back from Lyon who is one of four footballing Kalulu brothers, two of whom chose DR Congo while younger sibling Pierre went with France. He earns his living in Cyprus and offers honest cover down the right.

players.name: S. Kapuadi
players.note: A centre-back who has built his career in Poland and become a reliable fixture in the Leopards' back line. Quietly dependable, the kind of defender you only notice when he isn't there.

players.name: J. Kayembe
players.note: A left-sided defender at Belgian side Genk who once turned out for Belgium in friendlies before committing to DR Congo. Comfortable on the ball and happy to push forward, he's a different flavour of full-back than the no-nonsense types around him.

players.name: A. Masuaku
players.note: A left-back born in Lille to Congolese parents, now back in France with Lens after years in the Premier League with West Ham. He brings a bit of an attacking streak and plenty of big-game miles in the legs.

players.name: C. Mbemba
players.note: The captain and the country's all-time most-capped player, a centre-back whose career climbed from a rocky Newcastle start to standout years at Porto and Marseille before Lille. He has a habit of popping up with vital late goals, including in the playoff run that got DR Congo here.

players.name: A. Tuanzebe
players.note: Born in DR Congo and raised in England, he came up through Manchester United's academy and even captained England's under-21s before switching to the country of his birth. He scored the extra-time goal against Jamaica that finally booked this World Cup place.

players.name: A. Wan-Bissaka
players.note: The West Ham right-back famous for tackles that arrive out of nowhere, born in England but Congolese by descent. With Walker, Alexander-Arnold and others blocking his England path, he switched to DR Congo in 2025 and slotted straight in.

players.name: E. Kayembe
players.note: A central midfielder at Watford who does the unglamorous covering and shuffling that lets the more eye-catching names get forward. The sort of engine-room player every squad quietly relies on.

players.name: S. Moutoussamy
players.note: A defensive midfielder of Indo-Guadeloupean and Congolese roots, now in Greece after a long spell at Nantes. With more than fifty caps he's become one of the steadier voices in the Leopards' midfield.

players.name: N. Mukau
players.note: At 21 one of the brightest young midfielders in the group, holding his own at Lille and drawing interest from Premier League clubs. A composed passer who looks years older than he is in the middle of the park.

players.name: C. Pickel
players.note: A defensive midfielder born in Switzerland to Congolese parents, who joined Espanyol in 2025 for his first taste of Spanish football. He's the screen in front of the back four, the bloke who breaks things up before they get dangerous.

players.name: N. Sadiki
players.note: A 21-year-old midfielder who earned a big-money move from Union Saint-Gilloise to newly promoted Sunderland in 2025, and is already tipped to become one of the Premier League's better ones. Born in Belgium, he chose the Leopards and looks like a foundation piece for years.

players.name: A. Tshibola
players.note: A combative midfielder who once wore England youth shirts before turning out for DR Congo, and who returned to Kilmarnock in Scotland early in 2026. A well-travelled pro adding bite and depth to the middle.

players.name: N. Mbuku
players.note: A quick, direct wide player on loan at Montpellier from Augsburg, who only switched his allegiance to DR Congo in 2024. Once a hyped French youth talent, he's looking to rediscover that early spark on the biggest stage.

players.name: T. Bongonda
players.note: The number ten, a winger who spent three seasons in Russia with Spartak Moscow after stops in Spain and Belgium. When he's on song he's a direct, unpredictable handful out wide.

players.name: C. Bakambu
players.note: At 34 the veteran striker and one of the country's most prolific scorers, now back in Spain with Real Betis after years bouncing through China and the Gulf. He sits just shy of the national goal record and would dearly love to close that gap here.

players.name: S. Banza
players.note: A striker who made his name banging in goals at Lens before moving on to Braga and then the UAE with Al-Jazira. He waited a while for his first DR Congo goals, then helped himself to two in a single friendly against Madagascar.

players.name: B. Cipenga
players.note: Born in Kinshasa and raised in Portugal's youth system, he's been one of the brighter sparks in Spain's second tier with Castellón, chipping in goals and a stack of assists. The number nine who'd love to turn a breakout club season into a national-team moment.

players.name: M. Elia
players.note: A forward who moved to Turkey's Alanyaspor in late 2025 and quickly found his shooting boots there. Pacy and willing to run the channels, he's a useful option off the bench or out wide.

players.name: G. Kakuta
players.note: Once labelled the most gifted of his generation as a teenager and the youngest Chelsea player ever in the Champions League, the now-34-year-old's career took him all over Europe and into Turkey's second tier. The early hype never quite landed, but a World Cup at this age is a lovely late chapter.

players.name: F. Mayele
players.note: The CAF Champions League's top scorer as Egypt's Pyramids won their first continental crown, and the club's all-time leading marksman. A genuine penalty-box predator who arrives at the World Cup brimming with goals and form.

players.name: Y. Wissa
players.note: The Leopards' headline attacker and the Guardian's pick of the squad, who earned a deadline-day move to Newcastle after becoming Brentford's record Premier League scorer. Quick, clever and dangerous in the final third, he's the man opponents will plan around.

players.name: D. Kotarski
players.note: A Dinamo Zagreb academy keeper who rebuilt his career abroad, first in Greece and now as Copenhagen's number one. He's the youngest of Croatia's three goalkeepers and very much the understudy here.

players.name: D. Livakovic
players.note: The man who turned Croatia's 2022 World Cup run into folklore, saving three penalties against Japan and standing on his head against Brazil. If a knockout game goes to a shootout, he's the reason Croatia fans quietly fancy their chances.

players.name: I. Pandur
players.note: Hull City's keeper, who swept their 2024-25 player-of-the-year awards in a season where he was about the only thing the fans agreed on. He's the third-choice gloves here but has quietly earned the trip.

players.name: D. Caleta-Car
players.note: A towering centre-back, nearly two metres tall, who was already winning headers for Croatia in the 2018 final. Now at Real Sociedad, he's the steady old hand at the back rather than the star.

players.name: M. Erlic
players.note: A no-frills defender who became Danish side Midtjylland's record signing in 2025 after years in Italy. He made his Croatia debut in a draw with France, which is a fairly intimidating place to start.

players.name: J. Gvardiol
players.note: Croatia's defensive crown jewel, a Manchester City centre-back happy to bomb forward at left-back, who's just battled back from a broken shin in time for the tournament. Quick, calm and only getting better.

players.name: M. Pongracic
players.note: A German-born centre-back at Fiorentina who can also fill in at right-back or in front of the defence. He's the kind of versatile body every manager likes to have on the bench just in case.

players.name: J. Stanisic
players.note: Bayern Munich's Swiss-army-knife defender, comfortable at either full-back or centre-back, who could have played for Germany but chose Croatia. Bayern rate him so highly they've declared him not for sale.

players.name: J. Sutalo
players.note: A tall, ball-playing centre-back who left Dinamo Zagreb for Ajax in a big-money move. Settling in Amsterdam took a while, but he's grown into a regular for club and country.

players.name: L. Vuskovic
players.note: The teenage prodigy of this squad, a Tottenham-owned centre-back who spent the season on loan in Germany and was voted one of the Bundesliga's standout players, ahead of Harry Kane in one poll. Croatia's defensive future, arriving early.

players.name: M. Baturina
players.note: A Dinamo Zagreb academy playmaker who led the Croatian league in assists before joining Como, and gets the inevitable next-Modric comparisons. A creative passer being eased in behind the old guard.

players.name: T. Fruk
players.note: An attacking midfielder who was Rijeka's top scorer as they won the Croatian league and cup double. One of the few squad members still playing his football back home.

players.name: K. Jakic
players.note: Augsburg's defensive midfielder, the type who breaks up play and lets the artists create, and who can drop into defence if needed. He has a Europa League winner's medal from his Eintracht Frankfurt days.

players.name: M. Kovacic
players.note: A Manchester City midfielder with over 100 caps who glides past challenges and ties Croatia's defence to its attack. With Modric ahead of him, he does the running so the captain doesn't have to.

players.name: L. Modric
players.note: The 40-year-old captain and 2018 Ballon d'Or winner, still pulling the strings, now at AC Milan and heading to a record sixth World Cup alongside the likes of Messi and Ronaldo. Croatia's most-capped player and the heartbeat of everything they do.

players.name: N. Moro
players.note: A defensive midfielder at Bologna who does the unglamorous tidying-up in front of the back four. Another of the depth options in a midfield that runs deep.

players.name: M. Pasalic
players.note: Atalanta's all-time leading scorer in the Champions League, a midfielder with a knack for arriving late in the box to finish. He chips in with goals from deep that Croatia badly need.

players.name: L. Sucic
players.note: An Austrian-born midfielder at Real Sociedad, and cousin of teammate Petar Sucic. The two play together for Croatia, which makes for an unusual family WhatsApp group.

players.name: P. Sucic
players.note: A young central midfielder who earned a big move from Dinamo Zagreb to Inter Milan, and is cousin to fellow squad member Luka Sucic. He shuns social media and keeps his head down, which in modern football is almost a personality trait.

players.name: N. Vlasic
players.note: An attacking midfielder enjoying a strong scoring season at Torino, and a regular at major tournaments since 2018. The kind of player who can pop up with a goal when the bigger names are being marked.

players.name: A. Budimir
players.note: A proper old-school number nine who finished third in the La Liga scoring charts with Osasuna, behind only Mbappe and Muriqi, and was Croatia's top scorer in qualifying. At 34 he's having the best run of his career at exactly the right time.

players.name: A. Kramaric
players.note: Hoffenheim's all-time record scorer who has spent more than a decade quietly racking up goals at the same German club. A clever finisher and one of Croatia's most reliable sources of goals over the years.

players.name: I. Matanovic
players.note: A towering young striker, nearly two metres tall, now leading the line for Freiburg in Germany. He's early in his Croatia career but offers a different, more physical option up front.

players.name: P. Musa
players.note: A big striker scoring freely in MLS for FC Dallas, where he's their record signing and a regular near the top of the goal charts. His club form dragged him back into the national team after a couple of years in the wilderness, on home soil no less.

players.name: M. Pasalic
players.note: A right winger (no relation to Croatia's other Pasalic) who moved from Rijeka to Orlando City as a designated player. Direct and quick, he's one of the squad's fresher attacking faces.

players.name: I. Perisic
players.note: The veteran left-sided forward who scored in the 2018 World Cup final and is now winning Eredivisie titles with PSV well into his thirties. Heading to his fourth World Cup, he's living proof that Croatia's golden generation just won't quit.

players.name: T. Bodak
