players.note: The youngest of the three keepers, plying his trade at Dutch second-tier Telstar. He's almost certainly here to watch, learn and soak up a World Cup most goalkeepers his age only dream about.

players.name: T. Doornbusch
players.note: A backup keeper at VVV-Venlo who's used to waiting his turn, and he's the squad's number 26, which tells you where he sits in the pecking order. He calls the whole thing a dream coming true, and honestly, who could argue.

players.name: E. Room
players.note: At 36 he's the steady hand between the posts and, alongside captain Bacuna, the most-capped man in the whole squad. He's won two MLS Cups with Columbus Crew, so the big-occasion nerves got left behind years ago.

players.name: R. Bazoer
players.note: Once tipped as the next big thing at Ajax, he's since wound his way to Turkey's Konyaspor and only switched to Curaçao in the summer of 2025. A late convert who brings proper pedigree to the back line.

players.name: J. Brenet
players.note: A PSV academy graduate full-back who's bounced around Europe and landed at Scotland's Livingston. The well-travelled sort who's seen enough dressing rooms to keep the younger lads calm.

players.name: S. Floranus
players.note: A right-back who came up through Sparta Rotterdam and now patrols the flank for PEC Zwolle in the Eredivisie. Dependable rather than flashy, which is exactly what you want from a defender.

players.name: Deveron Fonville
players.note: At 22 he's one of the babies of the group, a left-back who earned a move up to NEC Nijmegen after working through the PSV and Utrecht youth setups. Young legs for a squad that leans a little experienced.

players.name: J. Gaari
players.note: A right-back earning his living in Saudi Arabia's second tier with Abha, and reportedly straight back to the day job once qualification was done. The kind of quiet professional who turns up and gets the work in.

players.name: S. Sambo
players.note: A PSV-schooled right-back currently on loan at Sparta Rotterdam, still only in his early twenties. Quick and willing to get forward, the sort who likes the touchline more than his own box.

players.name: R. van Eijma
players.note: A centre-back who joined RKC Waalwijk on a free and has quietly stacked up Eerste Divisie minutes ever since. Carries the full set of given names but keeps things simple where it counts, at the heart of defence.

players.name: A. Obispo
players.note: A left-footed centre-back at PSV Eindhoven, which makes him one of the few in this squad still playing Champions League nights. Probably the most coveted defender Curaçao can put on the pitch.

players.name: L. Bacuna
players.note: The captain and beating heart of the side, with nearly a hundred Premier League games for Aston Villa behind him and the joint-most caps Curaçao has ever handed out. At 34, leading the smallest nation ever to reach a World Cup is the story he'll tell forever.

players.name: A. Martha
players.note: A 22-year-old winger who became Rotherham's first player ever to reach a World Cup, and called it a boyhood dream out loud. Direct, quick, and not shy about taking a defender on.

players.name: T. Noslin
players.note: A versatile right-sided player who only made his Eredivisie debut with Telstar in 2025 and got off the mark soon after. A fresh face whose rise has been quick enough to land him on the biggest stage of all.

players.name: L. Comenencia
players.note: A 21-year-old right-back who came through PSV, spent time on Juventus's books with their reserve side, and now plays his football in Switzerland with Zürich. A tidy CV for someone so young, and one of the squad's brightest prospects.

players.name: K. Felida
players.note: A defensive midfielder at Den Bosch who does the unglamorous job of breaking up play and letting the flair players ahead of him shine. The kind of name fans forget until they notice how much he covers.

players.name: T. Chong
players.note: Born in Willemstad and groomed at Manchester United before settling at Sheffield United, he switched to the country of his birth in 2025 and promptly scored twice against Bermuda. The most natural-born Curaçaoan story in the whole guide.

players.name: G. Roemeratoe
players.note: A defensive midfielder who can fill in at right-back for RKC Waalwijk, the sort of flexibility a manager quietly treasures. He does his shift wherever the team needs a body.

players.name: J. Bacuna
players.note: The captain's younger brother and one of the team's more inventive passers, with Premier League time at Huddersfield and a spell at Rangers on his ticket. Curaçao gets the Bacuna brothers in the same engine room, which is rather lovely.

players.name: J. Antonisse
players.note: A forward who took the road less travelled to Greek football with Kifisia, well off the usual Dutch-and-English path the rest of the squad walked. Sometimes the scouting net stretches further than you'd expect.

players.name: B. Kuwas
players.note: At 33 he's one of the elder statesmen of the front line, a winger with years of Dutch football in his legs at Volendam. The experienced head you bring on when a game needs settling rather than starting.

players.name: K. Gorré
players.note: A winger who passed through the youth ranks of Manchester City, United and Swansea before finding his level at Maccabi Haifa in Israel. English academies raised him, but it was his mother's Curaçao that he chose to play for.

players.name: S. Hansen
players.note: An Ajax-schooled winger who cost Middlesbrough a few million in 2025 and switched to Curaçao that same autumn. Brings pace and width down the left, and is one of the more recent additions to the project.

players.name: G. Kastaneer
players.note: A forward who signed for Malaysia's Terengganu early in 2026, making him the squad's furthest-flung traveller by some distance. From a Caribbean island of 150,000 to the Malaysia Super League, the geography alone is a talking point.

players.name: J. Locadia
players.note: The squad's marquee striker, who banged in goals for PSV as a youngster and had a Premier League spell at Brighton before drifting through Hoffenheim, Cincinnati and beyond. He carries the number 9 and the weight of being Curaçao's most proven finisher.

players.name: J. Margaritha
players.note: A left winger born in Groningen who took his game across the Atlantic to Phoenix Rising in the American second tier. A USL Championship forward at a World Cup is the sort of underdog detail this whole squad is built on.

players.name: L. Hornícek
players.note: First-choice keeper at Portugal's SC Braga, where the 23-year-old has racked up a full season of games and a healthy pile of clean sheets. He is one for the future in the Czech goal, brought along behind the more capped options here.

players.name: M. Kovár
players.note: Came up through Manchester United's youth ranks without ever cracking the first team, then rebuilt himself in the Netherlands; PSV liked him enough to turn his loan into a permanent deal in January 2026. At 25 he is a serious contender for minutes between the posts.

players.name: J. Stanek
players.note: The man who has worn the Czech national-team number one in recent years, the 29-year-old Slavia Praha keeper played at Euro 2024 and is the most likely starter here. Steady and experienced, he anchors a goalkeeping group with three genuine options.

players.name: S. Chaloupek
players.note: A 22-year-old centre-back from champions Slavia Praha who has been getting a Champions League education this season, logging real minutes against top European sides. He is squad depth at the back for now, but the kind a manager is happy to blood early.

players.name: V. Coufal
players.note: At 33 the elder statesman of the defence, a right-back who spent five seasons grinding out games in the Premier League with West Ham before moving to Hoffenheim in Germany. Tough, vocal and reliable, he is exactly the sort of head you want in a back line at a tournament.

players.name: T. Holes
players.note: The Czech fans will always love this one: at Euro 2020 he scored and set up the goals that knocked the Netherlands out. A versatile Slavia Praha defender who can slot in across the back line or sit in midfield, he turns 32 here as a trusted utility man.

players.name: R. Hranác
players.note: A 25-year-old centre-back who earned a move to Germany's Hoffenheim off the back of his form at Viktoria Plzen, and has been a regular starter in the Bundesliga this season. Calm on the ball, he is one of the likely first-choice partnerships at the heart of this defence.

players.name: D. Jurásek
players.note: A left-back whose career stalled after a big-money move to Benfica barely worked out, then came roaring back once he returned home to Slavia Praha, where his crossing and overlapping runs have produced a string of assists. At 25 he looks like the first-choice on the left.

players.name: L. Krejcí
players.note: The captain, and the first Czech player Wolves have ever signed, arriving from Spain's Girona in 2025. A left-footed centre-back comfortable carrying the ball out, the 26-year-old led Sparta Praha to two titles before going abroad and now leads his country at its first World Cup in 20 years.

players.name: J. Zelený
players.note: A 33-year-old Sparta Praha defender who can fill in at left-back or centre-back, the kind of experienced squad hand who gives the manager cover in two positions. He is unlikely to start but knows the level and won't be fazed.

players.name: D. Zima
players.note: A tall, physical centre-back who tried his luck in Italy's Serie A with Torino before deciding regular football back at Slavia Praha suited him better. At 25 he offers competition and aerial presence as a backup option in the middle of the defence.

players.name: D. Doudera
players.note: A Slavia Praha full-back whose club season ended badly, sent off in the heated Prague derby and then frozen out by his own club. He travels as defensive cover, but arrives at the tournament short of recent match sharpness and minutes.

players.name: L. Cerv
players.note: A 25-year-old central midfielder who has quietly become one of Viktoria Plzen's most dependable players, all running and tidy distribution. With single-digit caps he is still establishing himself internationally, more squad rotation than guaranteed starter.

players.name: V. Darida
players.note: The grand old man of the group at 35, a former Hertha Berlin captain now winding down his career back home at Hradec Kralove. He has seen everything in the game, and his presence is as much about steadying the dressing room as the minutes he might play.

players.name: L. Provod
players.note: A left-sided attacking midfielder for Slavia Praha who scored the Czechs' first goal of Euro 2024 against Portugal, and has had a productive club season chipping in goals and assists. At 29 he is one of the team's main sources of creativity from the flank.

players.name: M. Sadílek
players.note: A combative central midfielder who was part of the Euro 2020 quarter-final squad and returned to Slavia Praha in 2025 after a spell in the Netherlands. At 26 he gives the engine room legs and bite, competing for a place in the middle.

players.name: H. Sochurek
players.note: The headline of the squad: a 17-year-old Sparta Praha midfielder who became the youngest player ever to appear for the senior national team. He is here to learn rather than start, but his composure and passing have people talking about him as one to watch for years.

players.name: A. Sojka
players.note: A young midfielder and one of the manager's newcomers for this campaign, included to add legs and energy to the squad. With little senior international football behind him, he is here mainly to develop and provide depth in the middle of the park.

players.name: T. Soucek
players.note: The squad's most experienced international and a real engine in midfield, this West Ham mainstay became the highest-scoring Czech in Premier League history during the season. A towering presence who arrives late into the box, he is central to everything his country does at its first World Cup since 2006.

players.name: P. Sulc
players.note: Named Czech Footballer of the Year in 2025, this attacking midfielder earned a move to French side Lyon after lighting up the league at Plzen with goals and assists. At 25 he is the squad's most dangerous creator-scorer and one of the players opponents will plan around.

players.name: T. Chorý
players.note: A genuine throwback at 1.99m tall, a target-man striker for Slavia Praha who bullies defenders in the air yet moves better than his frame suggests. He has been among the league's top scorers this season and offers a clear plan B: get it forward and let him win it.

players.name: M. Chytil
players.note: A 26-year-old Slavia Praha forward who has fought injuries and competition for a regular run, scoring in patches when he plays. He is a backup striking option here, providing a different body up front off the bench.

players.name: A. Hlozek
players.note: Once the great hope of Czech attacking talent, the 23-year-old has found minutes hard to come by at Germany's Hoffenheim this season, often used from the bench. Still gifted and versatile across the front line, he is a high-ceiling option the manager will hope rediscovers his spark.

players.name: J. Kuchta
players.note: A combative, hard-running striker for Sparta Praha who has been among the most reliable scorers in the Czech league this season. At 28 he offers energy and goals as a forward who presses relentlessly, pushing for a starting spot or a useful card off the bench.

players.name: P. Schick
players.note: The star turn: a striker for Germany's Bayer Leverkusen who passed 100 goals for the club and finished among the Bundesliga's top scorers this season. The Czechs' designated talisman up front, he is a clinical, two-footed finisher and the player most likely to win them a game on his own.

players.name: D. Visinský
players.note: A 22-year-old forward at Viktoria Plzen who has enjoyed a breakout season, scoring regularly and earning European nights along the way. Quick and direct, he is one of the younger attacking options and represents the future of this front line more than a guaranteed starter now.

players.name: H. Galíndez
players.note: At 38 the elder statesman of the squad, the Argentine-born keeper has been a steady presence in goal for Argentina's Huracan and is Ecuador's most experienced option. He is here as much for his calm and leadership as for game time.

players.name: M. Ramírez
players.note: The 25-year-old moved to Greek side Kifisia in 2025 and is in line to back up the senior goalkeepers. He was an unused squad member at the 2022 World Cup, so he knows the tournament rhythm without yet having played a minute on the big stage.

players.name: G. Valle
players.note: Gonzalo Valle made his name in 2025 dragging LDU Quito to the Copa Libertadores semis with a string of standout shot-stopping displays. The 29-year-old gives Ecuador a genuine in-form alternative between the posts.

players.name: P. Estupiñán
players.note: Ecuador's first-choice left-back and a real attacking weapon down that flank, the 27-year-old joined AC Milan in 2025 after several seasons in the Premier League with Brighton. His overlapping runs and crossing are a key part of how this team builds.

players.name: P. Hincapié
players.note: One of the best young defenders in the world, the 23-year-old centre-back is on loan at Arsenal and won the Premier League title in his first season there. Comfortable on the left of a back line and aggressive in the duel, he is central to Ecuador's defence.

players.name: Y. Medina
players.note: A 21-year-old who joined Belgian side Genk in early 2025, Medina is a versatile, energetic defender still establishing himself at international level. He came up through the same Independiente del Valle academy that has fed much of this squad.

players.name: J. Ordoñez
players.note: A composed, front-foot centre-back of just 21, Ordonez has become a regular for Club Brugge in Belgium and the Champions League, with several big clubs circling. He represents the next wave of Ecuador's defensive talent.

players.name: W. Pacho
players.note: At 24 the cornerstone of Ecuador's defence, Pacho made history in 2025 as the first Ecuadorian to win the Champions League, starting in PSG's final win over Inter. Calm, quick and rarely flustered, he anchors the back line.

players.name: J. Porozo
players.note: A 25-year-old centre-back who joined Mexico's Club Tijuana in 2025, Porozo is squad depth rather than a guaranteed starter. He brings size and Liga MX game time, having played regularly through the 2025-26 season.

players.name: A. Preciado
players.note: An attacking right-back who has spent recent seasons in the Czech league with Sparta Prague, the 27-year-old is one of Ecuador's options on the right flank. He likes to push high and join the attack.

players.name: F. Torres
players.note: A 28-year-old centre-back at Brazilian giants Corinthians, Torres is an experienced and reliable squad option who has been a regular call-up for years. He offers height and aerial presence as backup in central defence.

players.name: J. Alcívar
players.note: Jhegson Mendez is a hard-working defensive midfielder who returned home to Independiente del Valle in 2025 after six years abroad, including spells in MLS. The 26-year-old shields the back four and played at the 2022 World Cup.

players.name: M. Caicedo
players.note: The engine of this team and one of the finest holding midfielders in the world, the 24-year-old has been a near ever-present for Chelsea, who named him their Player of the Season. He breaks up play and starts attacks, and is the player Ecuador are built around.

players.name: D. Castillo
players.note: A box-to-box midfielder of 21 enjoying a strong run at Denmark's Midtjylland, where he has chipped in with goals and assists. He gives the midfield legs and energy and is part of Ecuador's young core.

players.name: A. Franco
players.note: A 27-year-old defensive midfielder who has spent years at Brazil's Atletico Mineiro, winning a string of titles. With nearly 60 caps, Franco is a dependable, experienced option to sit in front of the defence.

players.name: K. Páez
players.note: The teenage jewel of Ecuadorian football, this 18-year-old attacking midfielder is owned by Chelsea and spent the season on loan at Strasbourg in France, where he was even named a Ligue 1 young player of the month. Hugely gifted with the ball, he is one to watch even if minutes may come off the bench.

players.name: A. Minda
players.note: A 22-year-old winger listed here in midfield, Minda spent recent seasons in Belgium with Cercle Brugge and has been working his way into Ecuador's setup. He offers pace and directness from wide areas as a squad option.

players.name: A. Valencia
players.note: An attacking midfielder of 22 who has had his most productive season yet at Belgium's Royal Antwerp, scoring regularly. Left-footed and creative, Anthony Valencia adds an extra spark in the final third.

players.name: P. Vite
players.note: Pedro Vite is a creative attacking midfielder who moved from Vancouver to Mexico's Pumas UNAM in 2025. The 23-year-old brings vision and passing range and is a useful option to unlock defences off the bench.

players.name: K. Rodríguez
players.note: A 25-year-old centre-forward enjoying a breakout season at Belgium's Union Saint-Gilloise, where his goals have flowed after a quieter start to his time there. Strong and direct, Rodriguez is a real alternative to lead the line.

players.name: J. Yeboah
players.note: Born in Germany but playing for Ecuador, the 25-year-old winger has been one of Serie B's standout creators at Venezia, racking up goals and assists. Quick and tricky, Yeboah offers width and end product from the flank.

players.name: N. Angulo
players.note: A 22-year-old winger who became a key contributor at Anderlecht in Belgium, chipping in with goals and plenty of assists. Angulo's pace and crossing make him a lively option out wide for La Tri.

players.name: J. Caicedo
players.note: Jordy Caicedo is a 28-year-old striker who spent 2025 on loan in Spain's second tier with Sporting Gijon. A traditional target man, he is squad depth at centre-forward rather than a first-choice pick.

players.name: Jeremy Arévalo
players.note: A 20-year-old striker born in Spain to Ecuadorian parents, Arevalo chose to represent Ecuador and earned his first caps in late 2025 after a prolific spell with Racing Santander. Raw but sharp in front of goal, he is one for the future.

players.name: G. Plata
players.note: A 25-year-old left-footed winger who won the 2025 Copa Libertadores with Flamengo, Plata is one of Ecuador's most exciting attackers. Direct and unpredictable in one-on-ones, he is expected to be a starter out wide.

players.name: E. Valencia
players.note: Ecuador's captain and all-time top scorer with 49 goals, the 36-year-old has also scored a record six World Cup goals for his country. Still leading the line for Brazil's Internacional, the veteran striker is the emotional heart of this squad.

players.name: M. Alaa
players.note: The third-choice keeper from El Gouna, out on the Red Sea coast, who is here mostly to train hard and stay ready. If he gets on the pitch, something has gone very wrong for Egypt.

players.name: Mohamed El Shenawy
players.note: Egypt's No. 1, who turned 37 just before the tournament and last kept goal at a World Cup back in 2018. Eight years on, he is still the safest pair of hands the Pharaohs have, and probably writing the final chapter of a long career.

players.name: Mostafa Shobeir
players.note: The son of a former Egypt keeper who has quietly outdone his dad's reputation, once stringing together nine straight clean sheets in the African Champions League. If El Shenawy's legs go, this is the man waiting in the wings.

players.name: Al Mahdi Soliman
players.note: At 38, the elder statesman of the squad, a keeper who has bounced around half the Egyptian league and been called up plenty of times without ever actually playing a senior international. A World Cup squad spot is a lovely reward for a patient career.

players.name: Hossam Abdelmaguid
players.note: A young Zamalek centre-back who has grown into one of the steadier heads at the back for the Cairo side. The World Cup is a big jump up, but he has time on his side to grow into it.

players.name: Mohamed Abdelmonem
players.note: The centre-back who made the leap from Cairo to French football with Nice, giving Egypt a defender tested week in, week out against top-flight forwards. He is the one at the back who has seen this level of opponent before.

players.name: Ahmed Fatouh
players.note: Zamalek's left-back, who likes to get forward and overlap as much as defend. A useful outlet down that flank when Egypt have the ball and want to stretch the pitch.

players.name: Karim Hafez
players.note: A left-back at Pyramids who spent earlier years drifting through clubs in Europe before settling back home. Steady cover on the left, the sort who does the job without anyone noticing.

players.name: Mohamed Hany
players.note: Al Ahly's right-back, a reliable full-back who has spent his whole career with the Cairo club. The kind of dependable option a manager reaches for when he wants no surprises.

players.name: Yasser Ibrahim
players.note: An experienced Al Ahly centre-back who has won most of what there is to win in African club football. At 32 he brings the calm and the trophy-laden know-how Egypt will lean on at the back.

players.name: Rami Rabia
players.note: A centre-back who took his game to the Gulf with Al Ain in the UAE. Another of the older heads in defence, picked for his reading of the game rather than his pace.

players.name: T. Alaa
players.note: At 23, one of the youngest defenders in the group, plucked from a smaller Egyptian club rather than the Cairo giants. A squad pick for the future as much as the present.

players.name: Emam Ashour
players.note: Egypt's engine in midfield and one of the names Hossam Hassan builds the team around. The Al Ahly man does the running and the linking that lets Salah and Marmoush stay fresh further up.

players.name: Marwan Attia
players.note: A holding midfielder at Al Ahly who is happiest breaking up play and keeping things simple. Not flashy, but the sort of shield in front of the back line a tournament side quietly needs.

players.name: Nabil Emad Dunga
players.note: Everyone calls him Dunga, a defensive midfielder who has gone from Pyramids to Zamalek and on to the Saudi league. A tidy operator who keeps the ball moving and the tempo under control.

players.name: Hamdi Fathy
players.note: A combative midfielder now earning his living with Al Wakrah in Qatar. He is the one who throws himself into tackles and does the unglamorous work so the creative players can play.

players.name: Mohanad Lasheen
players.note: A midfielder for Pyramids, the ambitious Cairo club that has muscled its way into the conversation with the old giants. He gives Hossam Hassan another option in the middle of the park.

players.name: Mahmoud Saber
players.note: At 24, a midfielder from a smaller domestic side who has played his way into the conversation. Proof that Egypt's net is cast wider than just Al Ahly and Zamalek.

players.name: Mostafa Zico
players.note: A Pyramids attacking midfielder who goes by Zico, a nickname that sets a high bar. He offers a creative spark off the bench when Egypt need someone to unlock a stubborn defence.

players.name: Trézéguet
players.note: The winger who cuts in from the right and was Egypt's other big scorer in qualifying, with braces against Ethiopia and Burkina Faso. English fans may remember his Aston Villa days; these days he does his damage back home at Al Ahly.

players.name: H. Hassan
players.note: A France-born winger who chose Egypt and earns his stripes with Oviedo in Spain's top flight. An energetic, direct runner who gives the attack a different flavour off the bench.

players.name: Ahmed Zizo
players.note: An experienced winger who made his name at Zamalek before crossing the Cairo divide to Al Ahly. He brings goals and assists, though even at 30 he is no longer guaranteed a starting spot in this attack.

players.name: H. Abdelkarim
players.note: The teenage striker who is the squad's big surprise, a wonderkid Barcelona have been chasing and some have nicknamed Egypt's Haaland. At 17 he is here for the experience, but the future clearly has his name on it.

players.name: Ibrahim Adel
players.note: A young winger who moved to Denmark's Nordsjaelland, a club famous for polishing rough African talent into the finished article. A move to Europe at the right age to keep climbing.

players.name: Omar Marmoush
players.note: Egypt's second big gun, a Manchester City forward who arrived from Germany for big money and announced himself with a hat-trick. Quick, sharp, and able to play off Salah or lead the line himself, he gives the Pharaohs a genuine second threat.

players.name: Mohamed Salah
players.note: The captain, the talisman, and the reason much of the world will tune in to watch Egypt at all. He top-scored qualifying with nine goals, and at 33 this is almost certainly his last realistic shot at finally dragging the Pharaohs out of the group.

players.name: D. Henderson
players.note: Spent years as England's loyal understudy keeper, then finally got regular football at Crystal Palace. He's the safe pair of hands Tuchel keeps in reserve behind Pickford.

players.name: J. Pickford
players.note: England's number one and a genuine penalty-shootout specialist who seems to do his homework on every taker. He's the loud organiser at the back, now heading to a third World Cup.

players.name: J. Trafford
players.note: The young keeper who set a record run of clean sheets while getting Burnley promoted, which earned him a move back to Manchester City. Tuchel handed him his first England cap just months before this tournament.

players.name: D. Burn
players.note: A towering Blyth lad who scored the header that won Newcastle their first major trophy in 70 years, then made his England debut at 32. Proof that the late bloomers sometimes get the best stories.

players.name: M. Guéhi
players.note: Crystal Palace's calm, ball-playing captain who reads danger before it arrives rather than relying on a last-ditch lunge. One of the more dependable centre-backs in Tuchel's defence.

players.name: R. James
players.note: Chelsea's right-back has the engine and crossing of a wing-back when fit, but injuries have repeatedly stalled his career. This is the first World Cup his body has finally let him reach.

players.name: E. Konsa
players.note: Aston Villa's quietly versatile defender who can slot in at centre-back or right-back without complaint. Exactly the unflashy, do-his-job type tournament squads are built around.

players.name: T. Livramento
players.note: A flying full-back whose career was nearly derailed by a serious knee injury early on, but he fought all the way back to Newcastle's first team. Quick and direct when his fitness holds up.

players.name: N. Oreilly
players.note: The youngest name here, a Manchester City academy product who went from unknown to first-team regular in a single season, scoring in the cup final win over Arsenal. A boyhood City fan suddenly at the World Cup.

players.name: J. Quansah
players.note: The Liverpool academy centre-back who backed himself by moving to Germany with Bayer Leverkusen for regular football. It paid off with an England debut and a place on the plane.

players.name: D. Spence
players.note: Once written off and shipped out on loan after a stalled Spurs move, he chose to fight for his place rather than drift away. The reward was a Tottenham regular's role and a surprise England call-up.

players.name: J. Stones
players.note: The composed Manchester City defender famous for dribbling out of trouble where others would just hoof it clear. A serial trophy winner now at his third World Cup, when his body cooperates.

players.name: E. Anderson
players.note: A tireless box-to-box midfielder who left boyhood club Newcastle for Nottingham Forest and turned into one of the league's most underrated engines. Big clubs have been circling ever since.

players.name: J. Bellingham
players.note: England's big-moment midfielder at Real Madrid, the one who arrives late in the box and somehow scores the goal everyone was waiting for. Plays with a swagger that can drag a whole team forward.

players.name: E. Eze
players.note: A silky, close-control playmaker who finally got his big move to Arsenal after years lighting up Crystal Palace. The kind of player who can wriggle out of a tight corner and unlock a parked bus.

players.name: J. Henderson
players.note: At 35 he's the squad's elder statesman, equalling a record fourth World Cup appearance by an England player. Whether he starts or not, he's the dressing-room voice Tuchel trusts.

players.name: K. Mainoo
players.note: The Manchester United youngster with a midfielder's brain well beyond his years, gliding past challenges as if the ball's tied to his foot. Still only 20 but already trusted on the biggest stage.

players.name: D. Rice
players.note: England's midfield anchor and one of the most expensive British players ever after his move to Arsenal. He shields the back four, wins the ball, and has quietly turned into a serious set-piece threat.

players.name: M. Rogers
players.note: Took the scenic route through the lower leagues before exploding at Aston Villa, where he scored in their first European trophy win. A big, skilful number ten who genuinely came from nowhere.

players.name: A. Gordon
players.note: Newcastle's blistering left winger whose pace alone forces defenders backwards. Boyhood Everton fan who's grown into one of England's most direct attacking threats.

players.name: H. Kane
players.note: The captain and England's all-time top scorer, a striker who scores every kind of goal and drops deep to create them too. Endlessly chasing the one major trophy that's still eluded him.

players.name: N. Madueke
players.note: A powerful, fearless winger at Arsenal who runs straight at full-backs and trusts his strength to win the duel. Raw at times, but the kind of off-the-bench spark that breaks tired defences.

players.name: M. Rashford
players.note: Written off after falling out of favour at Manchester United, he rebuilt his game on loan at Barcelona and forced his way back into the England squad. A reminder that careers aren't always a straight line.

players.name: B. Saka
players.note: Arsenal's right-winger who cuts inside onto his left foot so often that everyone knows it's coming and still can't stop it. One of England's most reliable goal-and-assist machines.

players.name: I. Toney
players.note: Famous for his ice-cold, slow-motion penalty run-up where he barely looks at the ball, this Saudi-based striker came back from a long ban to keep scoring. England's specialist plan B up front.

players.name: O. Watkins
players.note: The Aston Villa striker who works the channels and has a habit of scoring decisive substitute goals for England. Late to the top level, he's made up for lost time with sheer reliability.

players.name: M. Maignan
players.note: France's first-choice keeper and the captain of his club in Milan, where they trust him enough to have tied him down on a long contract. He's a confident shot-stopper who likes to start attacks with his feet, basically a goalkeeper who fancies himself as an extra outfield player.

players.name: R. Risser
players.note: The fairytale pick: a 21-year-old who had never played a senior international when he was named in the squad, after a season so good at Lens that he was voted the league's best goalkeeper. The new boy along for the ride, learning from the men ahead of him.

players.name: B. Samba
players.note: The number two keeper, a calm and experienced head who knows his job is to be ready if Maignan ever falters. He wears the number 1 shirt, which is one of football's gentle little ironies for a backup.

players.name: L. Digne
players.note: An experienced left-back at Aston Villa who's been around the France setup for years, the reliable older option when the manager wants someone who won't be fazed. Famous for whipping in dangerous set-pieces, which makes him useful at both ends of the pitch.

players.name: M. Gusto
players.note: A young, energetic right-back at Chelsea who loves to bomb forward and overlap, the kind of full-back who treats defending as a chore he gets through so he can attack. One of the squad's up-and-comers rather than a guaranteed starter.

players.name: L. Hernández
players.note: The elder of the Hernández brothers and a versatile defender who can play left-back or centre-back, now at PSG. He's had more than his share of bad knee injuries over the years, so just being here fit is its own small victory.

players.name: T. Hernández
players.note: The younger Hernández brother, a flying left-back who's swapped Italy for the Saudi league but still gallops up and down the wing the same way. With Lucas also in the squad, France get two brothers for the price of one defensive berth.

players.name: I. Konaté
players.note: A big, quick centre-back from Liverpool, where he became the regular partner to Virgil van Dijk in one of the league's toughest defences. He's locked in a friendly three-way contest with Saliba and Upamecano for the two starting spots, so France can't really lose.

players.name: J. Koundé
players.note: A Barcelona defender who's spent years being shuffled between centre-back and right-back without ever complaining, the dependable utility man every squad needs. He has a knack for big-game goals, the sort that win cup finals.

players.name: M. Lacroix
players.note: A no-nonsense centre-back who helped Crystal Palace win their first big trophies, then earned his first France caps off the back of that form. A late bloomer at international level who's gatecrashed the party at exactly the right time.

players.name: W. Saliba
players.note: Arsenal's defensive anchor and, for a man not yet 25, remarkably unflappable, the sort of centre-back who makes the hard stuff look boring. Tall, fast and calm on the ball, he's exactly what you want when the opposition counter-attacks.

players.name: D. Upamecano
players.note: A powerful, aggressive centre-back at Bayern Munich who defends on the front foot and isn't afraid to step out and win the ball high up the pitch. The third name in France's centre-back puzzle, which is a luxury problem most teams would love to have.

players.name: R. Cherki
players.note: A gifted playmaker who joined Manchester City after dazzling in Lyon, where he was the league's best dribbler and top creator of chances. The squad's wildcard: capable of unlocking any defence with a single flick when nothing else is working.

players.name: N. Kanté
players.note: The much-loved engine of the 2018 World Cup-winning side, still chasing the ball down from box to box at 34, now playing his football in Saudi Arabia. Football's nicest man, the joke goes, because the 30 percent of the pitch he doesn't cover is where God plays.

players.name: M. Koné
players.note: A tall, ball-carrying midfielder who's become a key man for Roma, the type who sets the tempo and breaks up the game in equal measure. He gives France a younger alternative in the middle when they need fresh legs.

players.name: A. Rabiot
players.note: A tall, elegant midfielder and a long-standing favourite of the manager, now enjoying a strong season at AC Milan after a cut-price move. He glides around the pitch and chips in with surprising goals, the kind of player coaches trust more than fans expect.

players.name: A. Tchouaméni
players.note: The midfield shield in front of the defence, a Real Madrid regular who protects the back line and recycles the ball without fuss. He's the quiet, dependable foundation the flashier players are built on top of.

players.name: W. Zaïre-Emery
players.note: Still a teenager but already a two-time Champions League winner with PSG, where he became the club's youngest-ever player and one of its youngest captains. The wonderkid who skipped the slow part of the career and went straight to the trophies.

players.name: M. Akliouche
players.note: A creative, slightly shy attacking midfielder from Monaco who won Olympic silver on home soil in 2024 before breaking into the senior side. One to keep an eye on as France's next generation of playmakers.

players.name: B. Barcola
players.note: A rapid, direct winger at PSG, part of the young attack that won the Champions League, and a frontrunner to start out wide for France. He's all about pace and running in behind, the player defenders dread sprinting at them.

players.name: J. Mateta
players.note: A big, hard-working centre-forward at Crystal Palace who came late to the international party and made it count, finishing among the top scorers at the 2024 Olympics. The proper old-fashioned number nine in a squad full of speedsters and tricksters.

players.name: O. Dembélé
players.note: The reigning Ballon d'Or winner, who rebuilt his career at PSG and was the heartbeat of their first Champions League triumph. Two-footed and unpredictable, he's spent years being told he was wasting his talent, and has finally answered everyone at once.

players.name: D. Doué
players.note: A 20-year-old who announced himself to the world by scoring twice in PSG's Champions League final win, one of the youngest ever to do so. The kid who treats the biggest stage as if it's a kickabout in the park.

players.name: Kylian Mbappé
players.note: The captain, the talisman, and one of the fastest players on the planet, now leading the line at Real Madrid and closing in on France's record books at his third World Cup. If anyone scores the goal everyone remembers from this tournament, the smart money's on him.

players.name: M. Thuram
players.note: A strong, link-up centre-forward at Inter Milan and the son of Lilian Thuram, a France legend from the 1998 World Cup-winning team. Tall and good with his back to goal, he brings others into play as much as he scores himself.

players.name: M. Olise
players.note: A right-winger having a breakout season at Bayern Munich, where he racked up assists at a remarkable rate and pushed his way into the Ballon d'Or conversation. He cuts inside onto his clever left foot to either score or set up a team-mate, and you rarely know which until it's too late.

players.name: O. Baumann
players.note: The Hoffenheim keeper carried Germany through qualifying, keeping clean sheet after clean sheet while Neuer was retired. Then the legend changed his mind and reclaimed the No. 1 shirt, leaving Baumann to take a tough demotion on the chin.

players.name: M. Neuer
players.note: Germany's great goalkeeper came out of international retirement to chase one last World Cup, and Nagelsmann handed him back the No. 1 shirt without hesitation. He's the man who rewrote what a keeper is allowed to do, charging out of his box like an extra defender.

players.name: A. Nübel
players.note: He's technically a Bayern keeper, but he's spent years out on loan at Stuttgart because the man ahead of him simply wouldn't budge. Patient, reliable, and forever waiting for a door that Neuer keeps holding shut.

players.name: W. Anton
players.note: Born in Uzbekistan to Russian-German parents and brought to Germany as a toddler, the Dortmund centre-back is the quiet, unflashy type who just keeps things tidy at the back. A captain's temperament without needing the armband to prove it.

players.name: N. Brown
players.note: The Frankfurt left-back burst from nowhere into the World Cup conversation, with the manager praising his pace and one-on-one bite enough to suggest he could shove the established starter aside. A fast, fearless newcomer barging into the picture at exactly the right moment.

players.name: D. Raum
players.note: The Leipzig captain has been Germany's first-choice left-back for years, famous for whipping in crosses with the precision of a set-piece specialist. He goes into this tournament fending off a younger challenger and nursing a few knocks, so the spot isn't quite as nailed-on as it once was.

players.name: A. Rüdiger
players.note: Germany's defensive leader and a serial winner at Real Madrid, heading to his third World Cup as the snarling, combative presence every back line wants. Forwards know that getting a quiet afternoon against him is not on the menu.

players.name: N. Schlotterbeck
players.note: A left-footed Dortmund centre-back who treats defending as the start of an attack, slicing passes through the lines to launch his team forward. Increasingly the man Germany trusts most at the heart of the back four.

players.name: J. Tah
players.note: A calm, towering centre-back who won the Bundesliga title with Leverkusen, then strolled across to Bayern on a free transfer when his contract ran out. The understated half of Germany's first-choice defensive pairing, all positioning and composure rather than fireworks.

players.name: M. Thiaw
players.note: Born in Germany to a Senegalese father and Finnish mother, he polished his game in Italy with AC Milan before a big-money move to Newcastle. A first World Cup for a defender who's quietly become one of the squad's coolest heads under pressure.

players.name: J. Kimmich
players.note: The captain and the brain of this team, a Bayern leader who'll likely line up at right-back even though midfield is his natural home. Wherever you put him, he organises everyone around him and rarely wastes a pass.

players.name: N. Amiri
players.note: The Mainz playmaker forced his way into the squad on the back of a career-best season, finishing as his club's top scorer and barely missing from the penalty spot. A late-blooming reward for a player most had stopped expecting to see in a Germany shirt.

players.name: L. Goretzka
players.note: Written off at Bayern barely a year ago, the powerful midfielder fought his way back into the team and then back into the national side. Box-to-box, good in the air, and a likely starter in Germany's engine room after the comeback nobody saw coming.

players.name: P. Groß
players.note: The squad's elder statesman in midfield, who didn't earn his first Germany cap until he was 32 after years of being quietly brilliant in the Premier League. A clever, do-it-all operator who can fill in at right-back, the kind of low-maintenance pro every manager wants on the bench.

players.name: L. Karl
players.note: At 17, the Bayern wonderkid had a breakout season so wild he became the youngest player ever to score in three Champions League games in a row, beating a record once held by Mbappé. The youngest face in the squad and proof Germany's production line is still humming.

players.name: J. Leweling
players.note: A direct, busy winger who's racked up goals and assists for Stuttgart and turned himself into a useful option off the flank for Germany. The sort who runs at defenders all day and asks questions they'd rather not answer.

players.name: J. Musiala
players.note: The squad's spark of pure magic, a dribbler who glides through crowds of defenders like they aren't there, and the star of Germany's last big tournament. He's only just back from a horrible leg-and-ankle injury, so every minute he plays here feels like a small miracle.

players.name: F. Nmecha
players.note: A Hamburg-born, English-raised midfielder who came up through Manchester City's academy before settling at Dortmund, and yes, his older brother Lukas is a footballer too. He fought back from a knee injury just in time to make the plane.

players.name: A. Pavlovic
players.note: A homegrown Bayern midfielder with a Serbian father and German mother, all calm passing and tidy ball-winning in front of the back four. He missed Euro 2024 after illness cruelly struck on the eve of the squad announcement, so this is the big stage he was robbed of last time.

players.name: L. Sané
players.note: A blisteringly quick winger with Manchester City and Bayern on his CV, who took the bold step of leaving Munich for the noise and passion of Galatasaray in Turkey. On his day he's unplayable, all pace and a vicious left foot, even if the consistency comes and goes.

players.name: A. Stiller
players.note: The metronome at the base of Stuttgart's midfield, a left-footed passer who dictates tempo and quietly became one of the league's most efficient playmakers. The kind of deep-lying conductor good teams build everything around, even if casual fans rarely notice him.

players.name: F. Wirtz
players.note: Widely rated as one of the best attacking midfielders alive, the silky playmaker swapped a title-winning Leverkusen for Liverpool and the Premier League spotlight. Germany's creative heartbeat, the player they hope sets this whole tournament alight.

players.name: K. Havertz
players.note: The Arsenal forward is the likeliest man to lead the line, more of an elegant all-rounder than a brute of a No. 9. With Germany short of a classic goal-poacher, a lot rests on whether his clever movement and finishing click at the right moments.

players.name: M. Beier
players.note: A sharp, mobile Dortmund forward who chipped in close to double figures in goals this season and snuck into the squad almost as a surprise pick. Quick, willing to run the channels, and the type of fresh-legged option a manager loves to throw on late.

players.name: D. Undav
players.note: Released by Werder Bremen as a kid for being too small, he clawed his way up through the lower leagues to become one of the Bundesliga's deadliest finishers at Stuttgart. A late-developing box striker whose whole career is a quiet two fingers to everyone who wrote him off.

players.name: N. Woltemade
players.note: A towering striker at around 6ft 6in who exploded out of nowhere, top-scored at the Under-21 Euros, and earned a club-record move to Newcastle. Surprisingly nimble for his size, he often drops deep to link play rather than just loiter in the box.

players.name: B. Asare
players.note: The only home-based player in the squad, this 33-year-old keeps goal for Accra's Hearts of Oak and was named Ghana's goalkeeper of the year in 2025. He started keeping for the Black Stars during qualifying and is likely to be first choice at the tournament.

players.name: J. Anang
players.note: Born near Accra, this 25-year-old keeper came through West Ham's academy before settling at Dublin's St Patrick's Athletic, where he has become a reliable first choice. He is the first St Pat's player ever to make a World Cup squad, here as a backup option behind the gloves.

players.name: L. Zigi
players.note: Wearing the number 1 shirt, Lawrence Ati-Zigi has been Ghana's go-to keeper for years and is a long-serving fixture at Swiss club St Gallen, where he passed 250 appearances and helped them finish runners-up. At 29 he brings the most international experience of the goalkeeping group.

players.name: J. Adjetey
players.note: A 22-year-old centre-back who made his name winning the Swiss title with Basel, Adjetey is one of Ghana's brightest young defenders and drew interest from bigger clubs. He is comfortable on either side of the back line and is part of the squad's future at the back.

players.name: D. Luckassen
players.note: A Dutch-born centre-back who only committed to Ghana in early 2026, Luckassen got the nod after Alexander Djiku was ruled out injured. At 30 he arrives off a fine season with Cypriot side Pafos, who won the league and cup and reached the Champions League, where he played and even scored.

players.name: G. Mensah
players.note: A 27-year-old left-back who played at the 2022 World Cup, Mensah has been a regular for French side Auxerre, racking up around 30 league outings. He is an experienced, left-footed option for the left side of Ghana's defence.

players.name: A. Seidu
players.note: A versatile full-back at French club Rennes who can cover both flanks and centre-back, Seidu lost nearly a year to a serious knee injury before fighting his way back to fitness. His return to the Black Stars after that long layoff makes him a useful, adaptable defensive option.

players.name: J. Opoku
players.note: England-born centre-back of Ghanaian descent, Opoku has become a steady regular for Istanbul's Basaksehir, where he even chips in with the odd goal. At 27 he offers experienced cover in the middle of the back line.

players.name: K. Peprah Oppong
players.note: A 21-year-old defender who only debuted for Ghana late in 2025, Peprah Oppong earned his move to French side Nice after spells in Sweden and became a near-ever-present starter there this season. Young but already trusted, he is one of the squad's emerging names at the back.

players.name: A. Mumin
players.note: A commanding centre-back from Spain's Rayo Vallecano, Mumin lost over 400 days to a knee injury before returning to action in spring 2026. Whether he is fully sharp after that lay-off is the question, but his physical presence is exactly the kind Ghana want against Group L's bigger forwards.

players.name: M. Senaya
players.note: France-born and eligible for both Ghana and Togo, Senaya picked the Black Stars in 2026 and quickly looked like a first-choice right-back. He has been one of Auxerre's better defenders for tackles and interceptions, and at 24 he is one to watch on the right.

players.name: A. Baba
players.note: A familiar face at left-back, Baba Rahman has worn the Ghana shirt for over a decade and reached a Cup of Nations final back in 2015. He put up the strongest numbers among Ghana's left-back options this season at Greek club PAOK, giving the veteran a real claim to the starting spot.

players.name: E. Owusu
players.note: A defensive midfielder for French side Auxerre, Owusu featured at the 2022 World Cup and offers a screening presence in front of the back four. Injuries have nibbled at his season, but at 28 he is an experienced body for the engine room.

players.name: T. Partey
players.note: Ghana's most decorated midfielder, the 32-year-old left Arsenal for Spanish side Villarreal in 2025 and has clocked over 30 games there. As the deep-lying anchor he is the steadying presence the rest of the midfield plays around.

players.name: K. Sibo
players.note: A combative midfielder who helped Real Oviedo climb back into Spain's top flight, Sibo earned his Ghana place with that promotion run and a role in qualifying. At 27 he is squad depth in central midfield, ready to add legs and bite if called upon.

players.name: Caleb Marfo Yirenkyi
players.note: The teenager of the group, Yirenkyi was named Danish league young player of the year and made the league's team of the season for Nordsjaelland, the club linked to Ghana's Right to Dream academy. Manager Queiroz has tipped him as a future Ghana mainstay, and he can fill in across midfield and defence.

players.name: A. Semenyo
players.note: Ghana's in-form attacker arrives off a breakout season, scoring freely before a January move to Manchester City and netting the winner in the 2026 FA Cup final. Quick and direct down the flank, the 25-year-old carries much of Ghana's goal threat into the tournament.

players.name: A. Boakye
players.note: A left-footed right winger at French club Saint-Etienne, Boakye was one of the second division's best creators this season, piling up assists. At 25 he is an attacking option off the bench who brings dribbling and final-ball quality.

players.name: A. Fatawu
players.note: An exciting 21-year-old winger at Leicester, Fatawu lost the best part of a year to a knee injury suffered on Ghana duty before returning to score for club and country. When fit and flying he is one of the squad's most dangerous one-on-one runners.

players.name: P. Adu
players.note: A 22-year-old forward who scored his way into the squad with a productive season for Czech side Viktoria Plzen, Adu earned his first Ghana call only in late 2025. His own coach backed him to handle the World Cup stage; here he is a fresh attacking option in reserve.

players.name: B. Thomas-Asante
players.note: A centre-forward who fired Coventry to promotion and was a Championship player of the month, Thomas-Asante was born in England and chose Ghana. The 27-year-old gives the front line a more traditional target-man option to lead the attack or change a game from the bench.

players.name: J. Ayew
players.note: The captain and elder statesman at 34, Ayew leads the line and the dressing room, with this set to be his third World Cup. Son of Ghana legend Abedi Pele, he left Leicester after their relegation but remains the emotional anchor of the Black Stars.

players.name: C. Bonsu Baah
players.note: A 21-year-old winger who moved from Belgium to Saudi side Al-Qadisiyah in a sizeable deal, Bonsu Baah racked up double-figure assists there this season under Brendan Rodgers. Young and pacy, he is an attacking option with plenty of creative upside.

players.name: I. Williams
players.note: Born in Spain to Ghanaian parents, Williams once played for Spain before switching to Ghana, and he captains Athletic Bilbao as the first black player to wear their armband. At 31 the pacey forward is set for his second World Cup, leading the line alongside Ayew and Semenyo.

players.name: E. Nuamah
players.note: A 22-year-old winger at Lyon, Nuamah missed more than a year and over 50 matches with a knee injury, only returning to play in spring 2026. If he can rediscover his sharpness, his pace and directness add another dimension to Ghana's attack.

players.name: K. Sulemana
players.note: A left winger known for his pace and dribbling, Sulemana joined Italian side Atalanta in 2025 but had a frustrating, low-scoring first season there. He scored his first Ghana goal during qualifying, and at 23 the tournament is a chance to show the talent that earned a big-money move.

players.name: J. Duverger
players.note: Born in Canada, Josue Duverger may be the lowest-ranked club player at the whole tournament: his side plays in Germany's fifth tier. He is here as a backup keeper behind captain Placide, and his selection is a feel-good story in its own right.

players.name: A. Pierre
players.note: A 24-year-old keeper born just outside Paris, Alexandre Pierre is one of the goalkeeping understudies behind Placide. He plies his trade in France's second division with Sochaux and is unlikely to start unless something goes wrong ahead of him.

players.name: J. Placide
players.note: The captain and first-choice goalkeeper, and at 38 the wise old head of this squad with more caps than anyone else in it. He keeps goal for Bastia in France's second tier, and his job against Brazil, Morocco and Scotland is to organise the defence and keep Haiti's first World Cup since 1974 from getting away from them.

players.name: C. Arcus
players.note: Carlens Arcus is Haiti's likely starting right-back, a Port-au-Prince native who plays top-flight football for Angers in France. He is more of a defend-first full-back than an overlapping attacker, which is exactly what this group will need against stronger opponents.

players.name: K. Thermoncy
players.note: At 20, Keeto Thermoncy is the youngest player in the squad, a Switzerland-born defender on the books of Swiss champions Young Boys. He is more a project for the future than a guaranteed starter, but Haiti's brightest young talent at the back gets to learn at a World Cup.

players.name: Ricardo Ade
players.note: A 35-year-old centre-back and one of the team's co-captains, Ricardo Ade is the experienced anchor of the back line. Born in Haiti, he won a league title in Ecuador and now plays for one of the country's biggest clubs, LDU Quito, bringing exactly the kind of calm this young defence needs.

players.name: H. Delcroix
players.note: Born in Haiti and raised in Belgium, Hannes Delcroix came through the Anderlecht academy and can play centre-back or left-back. Now at Lugano in Switzerland, he is one of the more pedigreed defenders here and a likely starter alongside Ade.

players.name: J. Duverne
players.note: A 28-year-old centre-back born in France, Jean-Kevin Duverne plays his club football in Belgium for Gent. He gives the manager another experienced option in the middle of defence and competes for one of the starting centre-back spots.

players.name: M. Expérience
players.note: Martin Experience is a left-footed wing-back who plays in France's second division with Nancy, where he chipped in a goal and an assist this season. He gives Haiti an attacking option down the left flank and is in contention to start there.

players.name: D. Lacroix
players.note: Duke Lacroix is a New Jersey-born defender who has spent years as a reliable presence in America's second-tier USL Championship with Colorado Springs. He chipped in goals during World Cup qualifying and offers squad depth across the back line.

players.name: W. Paugain
players.note: Wilguens Paugain is a 24-year-old right-back from Haiti who earned promotion to Belgium's top flight with Zulte Waregem. He provides cover and competition for the full-back spots and is part of the rising generation in this defence.

players.name: J. Bellegarde
players.note: The squad's marquee name and creative engine, Jean-Ricner Bellegarde plays in England for Wolves and only switched his international allegiance to Haiti in 2025. He started every game of the qualifying run, and Haiti's best chances of making something happen in midfield run through him.

players.name: D. Jean-Jacques
players.note: Danley Jean-Jacques is a defensive midfielder who broke out in MLS in 2025, helping Philadelphia Union win the Supporters' Shield and becoming one of the league's better holding players. He is the shield in front of Haiti's defence, doing the unglamorous work that lets Bellegarde push forward.

players.name: L. Pierre
players.note: Leverton Pierre is an experienced defensive midfielder, born in Haiti, who plays in Portugal's second division for Vizela. A veteran of multiple Gold Cups, he gives the manager a steady, ball-winning option in the centre of the park.

players.name: W. Pierre
players.note: Woodensky Pierre is the only player in the squad based in Haiti's domestic league, a two-time league MVP whose visa to enter the United States was held up before the tournament. At 21 he is a developing defensive midfielder and depth option, but his presence carries real meaning for fans back home.

players.name: C. F. Sainte
players.note: A 23-year-old midfielder from Grand-Goave in Haiti, Carl-Fred Sainte plays in America's second-tier USL Championship with El Paso Locomotive. He is squad depth rather than a likely starter, but reaching a World Cup from that level is a story in itself.

players.name: D. Simon
players.note: Dominique Simon is a France-born defensive midfielder who joined Slovakia's Tatran Presov on loan in 2025. At 25 he is one of the squad's depth options in the middle of the park, more likely to feature off the bench than to start.

players.name: J. Casimir
players.note: Born in Guadeloupe, Josue Casimir is a versatile attacker who can play out wide or at wing-back, and he was a near ever-present for top-flight Auxerre in France this season. That flexibility makes him a useful card for the manager to play depending on the opponent.

players.name: L. Deedson
players.note: A pacey winger known for his runs in behind, Louicius Don Deedson moved to MLS side FC Dallas in 2025 after helping his Danish club earn promotion. He is one of Haiti's more reliable goal threats from wide and a candidate to start on the flank.

players.name: D. Etienne
players.note: Derrick Etienne Jr. is a New Jersey-raised winger with nearly a decade in MLS and a long list of caps for Haiti. Now at Toronto FC after winning silverware earlier in his career, his experience and directness make him a useful option in attack.

players.name: Y. Fortuné
players.note: Yassin Fortune is a tall, right-footed forward who has been scoring goals for Vizela in Portugal's second division. At 26 he gives Haiti an alternative profile up front and another finishing option off the bench.

players.name: W. Isidor
players.note: The Guardian's pick as Haiti's star player, Wilson Isidor is a Premier League forward at Sunderland who only committed to Haiti in 2026 after a push from supporters. He scored important goals in his first top-flight season, including a late winner against Chelsea, and his finishing could be Haiti's best route to a memorable result.

players.name: L. Joseph
players.note: Lenny Joseph is a France-born forward who lit up the Hungarian league with 16 goals and 10 assists for champions Ferencvaros, including Champions League experience. At 25 and in red-hot form, he gives Haiti genuine firepower and is pushing to start up front.

players.name: D. Nazon
players.note: Duckens Nazon is Haiti's all-time leading scorer and a true journeyman striker who has played in roughly a dozen countries, recently passing 100 career club goals. His club Esteghlal is in Iran, and his road to the tournament was disrupted when war there forced him to scramble for travel before the World Cup.

players.name: F. Pierrot
players.note: Raised in Massachusetts, Frantzdy Pierrot is the focal point of Haiti's attack, a powerful target striker with more than 30 international goals. He plays for AEK Athens in Greece, and his hold-up play and finishing led the line through the qualifying campaign.

players.name: R. Providence
players.note: A France-born forward who came through the academies at PSG and Roma, Ruben Providence now plays in the Netherlands for Almere City and is sometimes nicknamed the 'Haitian Neymar' by fans. He scored a key goal during qualifying and offers pace and trickery off the bench.

players.name: A. Beiranvand
players.note: Iran's long-serving number one and the man who saved a Cristiano Ronaldo penalty at the 2018 World Cup. Now 33 and playing at home with Tractor, he heads to his third finals as the experienced safe pair of hands behind this defence.

players.name: H. Hosseini
players.note: A 33-year-old keeper who left Esteghlal for Sepahan in 2025, he comes to the tournament as the backup option behind Beiranvand. Reliable domestic form keeps him in the picture if the first-choice gloves ever falter.

players.name: P. Niazmand
players.note: The Persepolis goalkeeper who once set an Iranian record by going 940 minutes without conceding. At 30 he is the third keeper in this squad, here to push the senior pair in training rather than expecting to start.

players.name: D. Eiri
players.note: At 21 the youngest defender in the squad, he came up through Iran's youth sides and earned this call-up with steady form on loan at Malavan. He is the bright young option in a back line otherwise stacked with veterans.

players.name: R. Rezaeian
players.note: A 35-year-old right-back who attacks like a winger, with an unusually heavy goal tally for a defender. A veteran of the 2018 and 2022 finals, his deliveries from the right give Iran a direct outlet going forward.

players.name: E. Hajisafi
players.note: Iran's most experienced World Cup player and a former captain, heading to a fourth finals at 35. A left-sided defender who can also fill in across midfield, he is the calm elder statesman of this group.

players.name: Saleh Hardani
players.note: A 27-year-old right-back at Esteghlal who is the younger challenger to Rezaeian on that flank. He has been in and out of the recent national side, so expect him as cover and competition rather than a guaranteed starter.

players.name: H. Kanani
players.note: A tall, physical Persepolis centre-back, full name Kanaanizadegan, who anchored Iran's defence at two Asian Cup semi-finals. At 31 he brings height and aerial dominance to the heart of the back line.

players.name: S. Khalilzadeh
players.note: At 36 the oldest outfield player here, a battle-hardened centre-back who helped Tractor win the 2024-25 league title. Experience and positional sense are what he offers; pace, less so at this stage of his career.

players.name: M. Mohammadi
players.note: A well-travelled left-back with spells in Russia, Belgium, Greece and Turkey before returning home to Persepolis. At 32 and past 70 caps, his speed and reliability make him a likely starter on the left of defence.

players.name: A. Nemati
players.note: A 29-year-old centre-back now at Foolad, who won back-to-back league titles during his Persepolis years. He can cover at left-back too, giving Ghalenoei a versatile depth option across the back line.

players.name: A. Yousefi
players.note: One of Iran's emerging defenders at 23, a Sepahan academy product who can fill in across the back line. He earned this call-up with composed club form and arrives as a versatile, developing squad option.

players.name: A. Jahanbakhsh
players.note: The captain and a former Premier League winger with Brighton, heading to his fourth World Cup at 32. He once became the first Asian player to finish top scorer in a major European league, and still carries Iran's creative load from wide.

players.name: R. Cheshmi
players.note: The Esteghlal captain, a 32-year-old who can sit in front of the defence or drop into central defence itself. He started Iran's opening win over Morocco at the 2022 finals and brings tactical flexibility to midfield.

players.name: S. Ezatolahi
players.note: Iran's defensive midfield shield, a holding player with 80-plus caps now winning titles in the UAE with Shabab Al Ahli. At 29 he is the screen who lets the attackers go forward, doing the unglamorous work in front of the back four.

players.name: S. Ghoddos
players.note: A clever, two-footed midfielder who spent years in the Premier League with Brentford before moving to the UAE. At 32 his vision and ability to link play make him an important creative presence in the middle of the park.

players.name: A. Razzaghinia
players.note: The youngest player in the squad, a tall teenage central midfielder who broke into the Esteghlal side after coming up through Iran's youth ranks. He is here for the experience and the future, not to start.

players.name: M. Ghorbani
players.note: A 24-year-old central midfielder now playing in the UAE with Al Wahda after a spell in Russia. Still building his international experience, he offers fresh legs and energy as a younger option in the middle.

players.name: M. Mohebi
players.note: A direct, hard-running winger based in Russia with Rostov, where he has chipped in with regular goals and assists. At 27 his pace makes him a useful counter-attacking weapon off the flank for Iran.

players.name: M. Torabi
players.note: A 31-year-old winger and Tractor fan favourite, capable on either flank or in an attacking-midfield role. A veteran of both the 2018 and 2022 finals, he adds wide depth and a willingness to shoot from distance.

players.name: M. Ghaedi
players.note: A skilful, close-control winger who racked up goals in the UAE before joining Al-Nasr, and wears Iran's number 10. At 27 his dribbling in tight spaces is one of the team's main sources of unpredictability in attack.

players.name: A. Hosseinzadeh
players.note: The 2024-25 Iranian league top scorer with Tractor, a quick forward equally happy out wide or through the middle. At 25 his pace on the counter has made him an increasingly important attacking option.

players.name: A. Alipour
players.note: A proven domestic goalscorer who once won the league's Golden Boot and remains central to the Persepolis attack. At 30 he provides Iran with a reliable penalty-box striker option behind Taremi.

players.name: S. Moghanlou
players.note: A 31-year-old centre-forward scoring steadily in the UAE with Kalba after a well-travelled career across Iran and Portugal. A relatively late bloomer internationally, he offers extra height and finishing as a backup striker.

players.name: D. Eckert Ayensa
players.note: A Germany-born striker of Iranian descent who switched allegiance to Team Melli only in 2026, his Iranian passport arriving just before the finals. A newcomer to the group playing in Belgium with Standard, he is the wildcard forward in this squad.

players.name: M. Taremi
players.note: Iran's talisman and main goal threat, scoring freely for Olympiakos and netting ten times in qualifying as Iran topped their group. With more than 100 caps and 50-plus goals, this 33-year-old is the player opponents must plan around.

players.name: Ahmed Basil
players.note: A 29-year-old keeper who has been the last line for Al Shorta during their run of four straight Iraqi titles, so he is used to winning even if international caps came late. He travels to the World Cup as backup behind the captain, the kind of safe pair of hands a squad leans on without fuss.

players.name: Jalal Hassan Hachim
players.note: Iraq's captain and first-choice goalkeeper, the 34-year-old has been the team's reliable presence for most of the past decade and passed 100 international appearances during qualifying. He also captains his club, Al Zawra'a, and is the steady, experienced head this young-ish squad is built around.

players.name: Fahad Talib
players.note: The third goalkeeper here at 31, though he has real pedigree: he was in goal for Al Quwa Al Jawiya when they became the first Iraqi club to win an Asian competition, and he kept goal for Iraq's bronze-medal U-23 side a decade ago. Wears number 1 but is most likely watching from the bench unless injuries strike.

players.name: Hussein Ali
players.note: A full-back born in Malmo to Iraqi roots, one of the squad's growing band of European-raised players who chose to represent Iraq. He moved to Poland's Pogon Szczecin in late 2025 and brings the kind of overlapping energy down the flank that suits a team happy to spring forward on the counter.

players.name: Merchas Doski
players.note: A left-sided defender born in Germany to Iraqi Kurdish parents, he plays his club football for Plzen in the Czech top flight, a step up in level from much of the squad. He marked his arrival in style by scoring on one of his first appearances for Iraq, in a friendly against Spain just before the tournament.

players.name: Frans Putros
players.note: The squad's well-travelled centre-back, born in Denmark to an Assyrian-Iraqi family and a fixture in Iraq defences since the 2019 Asian Cup. After years in Scandinavia and Thailand he now plays in Indonesia for Persib Bandung, and at 32 he is the kind of calm, organising head a back line wants alongside its quicker, younger options.

players.name: Mustafa Saadoun
players.note: A 24-year-old right-back at perennial champions Al Shorta who came up through Iraq's youth ranks, where he once scored a decisive goal at the U-23 Asian Cup. Squad depth on the flank for this World Cup, with his best years likely still ahead of him.

players.name: Rebin Solaka
players.note: At 33 the elder statesman of the back line, a centre-back of Swedish-Iraqi background who started out in Swedish football and now plays in Thailand for Port FC. He offers experience and aerial steel as cover, the senior option a manager turns to when a game needs locking down.

players.name: Zayed Tahseen
players.note: A 24-year-old centre-back who earned a 2025 move to Uzbek heavyweights Pakhtakor after captaining Iraq's youth sides. He is one of the defenders pushing for game time rather than a guaranteed starter, part of a generation Iraq hope will anchor the team for years.

players.name: A. Yahya
players.note: A tall left-back from Basra who has won back-to-back league titles with Al Shorta and become a regular in the national setup. At 30 he is in his prime and offers a dependable, locally-grown option down the left, the sort of player who quietly does the defensive job without drawing attention.

players.name: Munaf Younus
players.note: A centre-back for champions Al Shorta who is remembered fondly by Iraq fans for heading home the winner deep into extra time in the 2023 Gulf Cup final against Oman. At 29 he is an experienced, no-nonsense defender competing for a spot at the heart of the back four.

players.name: Akam Rahman
players.note: An Erbil-raised centre-back, now at Al Zawra'a, who broke into the national team during the 2023 Asian Cup and has become one of Iraq's more highly rated defenders over the past couple of seasons. Comfortable enough on the ball to step into midfield, he is firmly in the mix to start at 27.

players.name: Amir Al Ammari
players.note: A key midfielder for both club and country, born in Sweden to an Iraqi father and Palestinian mother before switching his international allegiance. At 28 he plays regularly in Poland's top flight for Cracovia and provides the engine and composure in the centre that lets Iraq's flashier attackers take risks ahead of him.

players.name: Youssef Amyn
players.note: A 22-year-old winger raised in Germany, where he came through the Borussia Dortmund youth setup before his path took him via Saudi Arabia to Cyprus and AEK Larnaca. He scored on his Iraq debut as a teenager and gives the attack a direct, dribbling option off the bench or out wide.

players.name: Ibraheem Bayesh
players.note: An attacking midfielder and playmaker who plays his club football in Saudi Arabia for Al Riyadh, and one of Iraq's genuine creative hubs. He was named the standout player of the 2023 Gulf Cup, which Iraq won, so when the team needs someone to unlock a defence he is often the answer.

players.name: Zidane Iqbal
players.note: The Manchester-born midfielder who came through Manchester United's academy and became the first British-born South Asian to play in the Champions League before leaving to find regular football in the Netherlands. Son of a Pakistani father and Iraqi mother, the 22-year-old chose Iraq, and his passing range makes him one of the squad's most watchable players.

players.name: Z. Ismaeel
players.note: A 23-year-old who plays his football at home in Iraq for Al Talaba and is one of the less-heralded names in the squad. He is here as midfield depth, a domestic-based player given the chance to learn on the biggest stage rather than someone expected to start.

players.name: A. Sher
players.note: A central midfielder born in Kirkuk but raised in Sweden, where he came through Hammarby and even played youth international football before formally becoming an Iraq player in 2025. Now at Norway's Sarpsborg, the 23-year-old is one of Arnold's newer recruits to the diaspora project, adding legs and bite in the middle.

players.name: Kevin Yakob
players.note: A midfielder born in Gothenburg to an Assyrian family with roots in Basra, he has just enjoyed the season of his life: in May 2026 his Aarhus side won the Danish league for the first time in 40 years, with Yakob scoring in the title-clinching match. He arrives at the World Cup full of confidence at 25.

players.name: A. Jasim
players.note: At 21, one of Asia's brightest attacking prospects, a left winger who earned a move to Serie A side Como before being loaned out, currently with Al Najma in Saudi Arabia to get regular minutes. Quick and fearless in one-on-ones, he is exactly the kind of young talent a World Cup can turn into a star.

players.name: Ali Al Hamadi
players.note: A 23-year-old striker who built his reputation in England's lower leagues with a prolific spell at AFC Wimbledon, then earned a move up the ladder. His 2025-26 loan at Luton was badly disrupted by injury, but at his sharpest he is a mobile front man and one of Iraq's most promising attacking options.

players.name: M. Farji
players.note: A 21-year-old winger born in Norway to Kurdish parents, who lit up the Norwegian league with nine goals and earned a move to Italian football, where his old club had just won promotion. Direct and dangerous from the left, he is one of the exciting young attackers giving this Iraq side a different, faster edge.

players.name: Aymen Hussein
players.note: The Guardian's pick as Iraq's player to watch, and the man whose goal against Bolivia sent Iraq to their first World Cup since 1986. A powerful penalty-box striker nicknamed the Hatchet Man, he is one of the country's leading all-time scorers and the focal point of the attack at 29.

players.name: Meme
players.note: Known simply as Meme, this Baghdad-born centre-forward wears the number 10 and was once tipped as the great hope of Iraqi attack after breaking through as a teenager. Now 25 and playing in the UAE for Dibba Al Fujairah, he offers a different striking profile to Hussein up top.

players.name: A. Qasem
players.note: A 22-year-old left winger born in Sweden who switched from the Swedish youth setup to Iraq just before the tournament. He plays in MLS for Nashville, where he helped win the club's first trophy in 2025, and gives Iraq pace and creativity on the wing in front of what will be a sympathetic American crowd.

players.name: A. Y. Hashim
players.note: A 29-year-old forward playing at home for Al Talaba, where he chips in with goals as one of the side's attacking options. He is squad depth here rather than a frontline starter, a domestically based forward offering Arnold a different look late in games.

players.name: Y. Fofana
players.note: The number one shirt belongs to this Paris-born keeper, who moved to Turkish football in 2025 and was a regular in the Super Lig. He was already trusted in goal during Ivory Coast's title defence, so expect him between the posts here too.

players.name: M. Koné
players.note: A 23-year-old keeper born in Abidjan who came up through French youth football before settling at his Belgian club. He is the backup here, most likely watching from the bench unless the first choice gets hurt.

players.name: A. Lafont
