players.note: An experienced keeper who spent years in French football before moving to Greece, he only switched his international allegiance to Ivory Coast in late 2025 and kept a clean sheet on debut in a qualifier rout. He adds depth and a calm head to the goalkeeping group.

players.name: E. Agbadou
players.note: A 28-year-old centre-back who spent a season in the Premier League's relegation scrap, where he played most games and was rated a solid, no-nonsense defender. The World Cup is part of the same chapter as his first Africa Cup of Nations, so this is a relatively late international bloom for him.

players.name: O. Diomande
players.note: At 22 he is already one of the most valuable Ivorian players around, a composed centre-back for the Portuguese champions who recently signed a long contract extension. He started in the 2024 Africa Cup of Nations win and is a likely starter in this defence.

players.name: G. Doué
players.note: A French-born right-back who chose Ivory Coast while his younger brother Désiré plays for France, a family split that became headline material when he scored and set up the winner in a warm-up against France in June. Expect an attacking full-back who likes to get forward.

players.name: G. Konan
players.note: A well-travelled left-back at 30, with stops in France, Saudi Arabia and Portugal behind him, and a regular starter at his current club. He brings experience and cover down the left rather than a guaranteed starting spot.

players.name: O. Kossounou
players.note: A quick, athletic centre-back for his Italian club who can also cover at right-back, and a winner of the 2023 Africa Cup of Nations. A hamstring injury late in the club season had put his tournament in some doubt, so his fitness is worth keeping an eye on.

players.name: E. Ndicka
players.note: A dependable left-sided centre-back for his Italian club who, after collapsing on the pitch with a lung issue in 2024, recovered to play every single minute of the next league season. He is one of the first names on the team sheet at the back.

players.name: C. Operi
players.note: A 28-year-old left-back at his Istanbul club who came into the squad partly through injuries to others, having missed earlier internationals himself. He is squad depth on the left rather than a guaranteed starter.

players.name: W. Singo
players.note: One of the team's standout names, a powerful, pacy defender who moved to his Turkish club in a big-money deal in 2025 and is tracked by several Premier League sides. He can play centre-back but is at his best charging forward from right-back, and should be a key starter.

players.name: S. Fofana
players.note: A box-to-box midfielder, born in France, who arrived at the Portuguese champions mid-season and quickly became one of their most influential players. At 30 he brings drive and goals from deep, and is a strong bet to start in central midfield.

players.name: C. Inao Oulai
players.note: At 19 he is the squad's brightest young midfield prospect, a tempo-setter at his Turkish club who caught the eye at the Africa Cup of Nations and has Premier League clubs circling. One to watch even if he starts the tournament as a rotation option.

players.name: F. Kessié
players.note: The captain and the spine of this team, a powerful all-action midfielder now playing in Saudi Arabia who passed 100 caps for his country in early 2026. He led the side to the 2023 Africa Cup of Nations title and will set the tone in midfield.

players.name: I. Sangaré
players.note: A tall, ball-winning defensive midfielder in the Premier League who shields the back four and breaks up play. He gives the captain a natural partner in the middle and is one of the team's most reliable starters.

players.name: J. Seri
players.note: At 34 he is the elder statesman of the midfield, a passer who once starred for Nice and Fulham and now plays in Slovenia after recovering from a serious injury. A 2023 Africa Cup of Nations winner, he is here for his experience and calm on the ball rather than to play every minute.

players.name: P. Guiagon
players.note: A small, versatile attacking midfielder and winger who has been chipping in with goals at his Belgian club. At 24 he is squad depth here, a useful option to change a game from the bench rather than a guaranteed starter.

players.name: B. Touré
players.note: A 19-year-old winger who came through the famous ASEC Mimosas academy, spent time in Sweden, and has since become one of the most exciting young attackers in the Bundesliga, with several big clubs reportedly interested. Raw and electric, he is one for the future who could get minutes off the bench.

players.name: S. Adingra
players.note: A direct, tricky winger wearing the number 10, who was man of the match with two assists in the 2024 Africa Cup of Nations final and rediscovered his form on loan in Ligue 1. He is one of the team's main creative threats and a likely starter out wide.

players.name: A. Bonny
players.note: A France-born forward who turned down France to commit to Ivory Coast just before the tournament, coming off a strong season helping his Italian club win the league title. Wearing the number 9, he is a fresh option up front who adds real quality to the attack.

players.name: O. Diakité
players.note: A 22-year-old forward who can lead the line or play just behind, on loan in Belgium where he has been among the better goalscorers in the league. A 2024 Africa Cup of Nations winner, he is attacking depth here rather than a nailed-on starter.

players.name: A. Diallo
players.note: One of the team's best-known names, a Premier League winger who scored the winner against France in a June warm-up. His club season was quieter than his breakout the year before, but his energy and eye for a big moment make him a key attacker for Ivory Coast.

players.name: Y. Diomande
players.note: A lightning-quick 19-year-old winger with an unusual path through a US soccer academy and Spain before his Bundesliga club, where he had a hand in 20 goals and was named the league's best newcomer. He carries real pace and big-club interest into his first World Cup.

players.name: E. Guessand
players.note: A 24-year-old forward who came through the Nice academy before a big-money move to the Premier League, holding French and Ivorian nationality but committing to Ivory Coast. Strong and mobile up front, he gives the attack another physical, flexible option.

players.name: N. Pépé
players.note: The Guardian's pick as the team's player to watch, a once-record-breaking winger who rebuilt his career in La Liga and even won a league player-of-the-month award this season. Controversially left out of the Africa Cup of Nations, he is back in the fold to add pace and experience to the attack.

players.name: E. Wahi
players.note: A 22-year-old centre-forward who switched from France to Ivory Coast only in spring 2026, joining the squad late after staying at his club to help fight off relegation. He is expected to lead the line, a genuine number nine to give the attack a focal point.

players.name: T. Hayakawa
players.note: He had a remarkable 2025 in Japan's top flight, playing every league minute for Kashima as they won the title and being voted the J.League's best player of the season. Here he is back-up cover, but a keeper in fine form to push the starter.

players.name: K. Osako
players.note: A goalkeeper for Sanfrecce Hiroshima in Japan's top division, he is one of the squad's home-based keepers and a long-serving Samurai Blue squad member. Expect him as a reliable option behind the first choice rather than a starter.

players.name: Z. Suzuki
players.note: Japan's first-choice keeper and the only one wearing the number 1, despite being just 23. He spent the season in Italy's Serie A with Parma, and his shot-stopping at that level is why he has leapfrogged more experienced names into the net.

players.name: K. Itakura
players.note: A composed, ball-playing centre-back who anchors Japan's back line, he became the first Japanese player to sign for Ajax in 2025 after three solid seasons in Germany's Bundesliga. He is one of the first names on the team sheet at the back.

players.name: H. Ito
players.note: A left-sided defender at Bayern Munich, where a long run of foot and muscle injuries has cost him most of two seasons since his move from Stuttgart. If fully fit he adds real quality, but the question mark is whether he has the match minutes behind him.

players.name: Y. Nagatomo
players.note: At 39, the FC Tokyo full-back becomes the first Japanese player ever selected for five World Cups, having featured at every edition since 2010. He is here as a veteran leader and squad presence as much as a likely starter.

players.name: A. Seko
players.note: A 25-year-old centre-back who became Le Havre's first Japanese signing in 2025 and played regularly in France's Ligue 1 this season. He provides defensive depth, with a handful of caps and still building his international experience.

players.name: Y. Sugawara
players.note: An attacking right-back who spent the season on loan at Werder Bremen in the Bundesliga, racking up assists from the flank. His energy going forward makes him a strong contender to start on the right of Japan's defence.

players.name: J. Suzuki
players.note: A 22-year-old defender who moved to FC Copenhagen in 2025 after topping Japan's top flight for aerial duels won. Quick and versatile across the back line, he is one of the squad's younger options gaining European experience.

players.name: S. Taniguchi
players.note: A 34-year-old centre-back now playing in Belgium with St. Truiden, after years in Japan with Kawasaki and a spell in Qatar. He brings calm experience to the defensive group and is more a senior squad option than a guaranteed starter.

players.name: T. Tomiyasu
players.note: A versatile defender who can fill any position across the back four, his recent years have been wrecked by knee trouble that ended his time at Arsenal. He joined Ajax to rebuild fitness, so this is as much a comeback story as a tournament.

players.name: T. Watanabe
players.note: A centre-back who joined Feyenoord in 2025 and quickly became a regular, even chipping in with goals from set pieces. Comfortable in possession, he gives Moriyasu another dependable option in Japan's three-man defence.

players.name: R. Doan
players.note: A direct, left-footed right winger who wears Japan's number 10 and spent the season scoring and creating for Eintracht Frankfurt in the Bundesliga. He is one of the team's main attacking outlets and a near-certain starter.

players.name: W. Endo
players.note: Japan's captain and defensive-midfield anchor, he led his country to become the first nation to qualify for this World Cup. Game time at Liverpool dried up this season and a foot injury interrupted his spring, but his leadership keeps him central to the plan.

players.name: D. Kamada
players.note: A clever, two-footed midfielder at Crystal Palace, where he has collected a clutch of trophies including a European cup this season. He can play deep or further forward, and his passing range makes him one of Japan's key creators.

players.name: K. Sano
players.note: A tireless defensive midfielder for Mainz in the Bundesliga, where he covers some of the most ground of any player in the league. He gives Japan an energetic engine in front of the defence, either alongside or in place of the captain.

players.name: A. Tanaka
players.note: A central midfielder who helped Leeds reach the Premier League and was voted their players' player of the year the season before. Good for a long-range goal, he offers Japan composure and drive in the middle of the park.

players.name: J. Ito
players.note: An experienced right winger with around 70 caps, now back in Belgium with Genk after his French club were relegated. His pace and crossing on the flank make him a useful starter or impact option off the bench.

players.name: T. Kubo
players.note: The Guardian's pick as Japan's star man, a gifted winger and Spain's Real Sociedad's main creative force who came through Barcelona and Real Madrid's youth systems. He is the player most likely to unlock a tight defence with a moment of magic.

players.name: D. Maeda
players.note: A relentless runner who finished the Scottish season on fire for Celtic, scoring in five league games in a row plus the cup final. Whether wide or up top, his pressing and goal threat give Japan a real cutting edge in attack.

players.name: Keito Nakamura
players.note: A quick, dribbling left winger who was Reims' top scorer in France this season. His direct running and eye for goal give Japan another attacking option from wide areas, likely from the bench in a deep forward line.

players.name: Y. Suzuki
players.note: An attacking midfielder who joined Freiburg in 2025 after lighting up the Danish league as a playmaker. At 24 he is one of the newer faces in the squad, offering creativity and a goal threat from midfield off the bench.

players.name: K. Goto
players.note: A 20-year-old striker who broke through in Belgium this season with double figures in goals and a monthly player-of-the-month award. Wearing the number 9, he is the squad's exciting young forward and a bright prospect to watch.

players.name: Koki Ogawa
players.note: A penalty-box striker for NEC Nijmegen in the Dutch league, the kind of forward who does his work inside the area rather than dropping deep. His near-double-figure goal return this season makes him a genuine option through the middle.

players.name: K. Shiogai
players.note: A 20-year-old forward who made his name at NEC in the Netherlands after coming straight from university football, earning a January move to Germany. One of the youngest in the squad, he is here to develop and provide attacking depth.

players.name: A. Ueda
players.note: Feyenoord's main striker and the Dutch league's standout scorer this season, with more than 20 goals to his name. He was also lethal in qualifying, so despite wearing 18 he is a leading candidate to lead Japan's line.

players.name: Yazid Abu Layla
players.note: Jordan's first-choice keeper at their debut World Cup, the 32-year-old plays his club football at home with Al Hussein. He'll be the last line against Argentina, Algeria and Austria in Group J, so expect a busy summer.

players.name: Abdallah Al Fakhouri
players.note: Long tipped as the heir to Jordan's legendary keeper Amer Shafi, the 25-year-old made his senior debut at just 17. He plays for Al Wihdat and is the most likely back-up if the starter is unavailable.

players.name: Noureddin Zaid
players.note: The third goalkeeper in the squad, this 32-year-old is a regular for domestic side Al-Faisaly in Amman. He's here as experienced cover and is unlikely to play unless injuries strike ahead of him.

players.name: H. Abu Al Dahab
players.note: A 25-year-old centre-back who has spent recent football in Kuwait, he sits among the squad's defensive depth rather than the first-choice back line. Useful cover for a back three if Jordan need to shore things up.

players.name: M. Abu Hasheesh
players.note: A 30-year-old left-back who was born in Iraq and chose to represent Jordan, he plays his club football across the border with Al-Karma. He gives the squad an option down the left flank.

players.name: M. Abualnadi
players.note: A 24-year-old centre-back born in Kansas, he played college soccer at Notre Dame before choosing Jordan over the United States and moving to Malaysian side Selangor. A composed left-sided defender pushing for minutes at the back.

players.name: Yazan Al Arab
players.note: One of the squad's most reliable defenders and a fixture in the back line since 2017, the 29-year-old centre-back plays in South Korea for FC Seoul, where he settled in quickly. He even scored against Barcelona in a 2025 friendly.

players.name: Saed Al Rosan
players.note: A 28-year-old centre-back for domestic powerhouse Al Hussein, he scored his first international goal in a 7-0 thrashing of Pakistan during qualifying. He's part of Jordan's home-based defensive group.

players.name: A. Badawi
players.note: A 28-year-old defender from Amman club Al-Faisaly, he's one of the squad's less-capped members and sits in the depth chart at the back. Expect him to be cover rather than a regular starter.

players.name: Abdallah Naseeb
players.note: A 31-year-old centre-back currently playing in Iraq with Al Zawra'a, he brings experience to the defensive ranks. A steady veteran option as Jordan navigate a tough Group J.

players.name: Saleem Obaid
players.note: At 33, this left-back from Al Hussein is one of the squad's elder statesmen, having first played for Jordan back in 2019. A dependable veteran offering depth and experience down the left.

players.name: Ehsan Haddad
players.note: Jordan's captain and a defensive leader with around 75 caps, the 31-year-old has been a serial title winner at home, first with Al-Faisaly and now with Al Hussein. He'll wear the armband leading the nation out at its first World Cup.

players.name: Mohannad Abu Taha
players.note: At 22, he's one of the squad's youngest and most versatile players, comfortable across the left flank as a defender, midfielder or winger. He's bounced between Jordan, Saudi Arabia and Iraq, where he now plays for Al-Quwa Al-Jawiya.

players.name: M. Al Daoud
players.note: The squad's oldest outfield player at 33, this Al Wihdat midfielder made his Jordan debut all the way back in 2011 and is the son of former international Rateb Al-Dawoud. A deep-lying veteran whose experience matters more than his minutes here.

players.name: Ibrahim Sa'deh
players.note: A 25-year-old central midfielder now plying his trade in Iraq with Al-Karma, he was part of Jordan's run to the 2023 Asian Cup final. He's squad depth in the engine room rather than a guaranteed starter.

players.name: Nizar Al Rashdan
players.note: A 26-year-old defensive midfielder who shields the back four and links defence to attack, letting Jordan sit deep and counter. Born in Irbid, he moved to Qatar SC in early 2026 and is central to the team's game plan against bigger sides.

players.name: Noor Al Rawabdeh
players.note: A 28-year-old midfielder who has carved out a key role for club and country since moving to Malaysian side Selangor in 2023. He featured in the 2023 Asian Cup final run and is a regular contributor in Jordan's midfield.

players.name: Rajaei Ayed
players.note: A 32-year-old central midfielder and a serial winner with Al Hussein, where he's collected a dozen trophies. With around 72 caps, he brings ball progression and tireless work rate to the middle of the park.

players.name: Amer Jamous
players.note: A 23-year-old midfielder who helped Al Wihdat win the Jordanian FA Cup, he's part of the squad's younger generation. He spent the early part of 2026 on loan in Iraq and provides energetic depth in midfield.

players.name: Mahmoud Al Mardi
players.note: A 32-year-old left winger with around 60 caps, currently playing in the UAE for Dibba Al-Fujairah. He's been part of the national team since 2015 and offers experienced width and depth in attack.

players.name: Mohammed Abu Zurayq
players.note: A 28-year-old forward nicknamed "Sharara," he joined Moroccan giants Raja Casablanca in early 2026 and started the Arab Cup final. A handy attacking option who can lead the line or play off the main striker.

players.name: O. Al Fakhouri
players.note: At 19, he's the squad's youngest member and one of its brightest prospects, a left winger who can also play up top. He made a record-breaking move to Egyptian side Pyramids FC and scored on his debut, so he's a name to file away for the future.

players.name: A. Azaizeh
players.note: A 21-year-old winger born in Germany who chose Jordan, he was top scorer at the AFC U-23 Asian Cup and earned a loan move to Saudi side Al Shabab off the back of it. He scored a brace soon after arriving, marking him out as one to watch.

players.name: Ali Olwan
players.note: Jordan's deadliest finisher and their main hope for goals, the 25-year-old striker plays in Qatar with Al-Sailiya and scored nine times in qualifying, including a hat-trick away to Oman that clinched their World Cup place. He's been recovering from ankle surgery, so his sharpness will be one to monitor.

players.name: Ibrahim Sabra
players.note: A 20-year-old centre-forward and exciting young talent, he scored on his way into the Croatian top flight with Lokomotiva Zagreb. Known for his power and pace, he's one of Jordan's promising attackers, though a recent ankle injury has clouded his summer.

players.name: Mousa Tamari
players.note: Jordan's talisman and by far their highest-profile player, the 28-year-old winger plays in France for Rennes and was the first Jordanian to score in Ligue 1. Nicknamed the "Jordanian Messi," he led the side to its first World Cup and is the man their attack runs through.

players.name: C. Acevedo
players.note: Santos Laguna's keeper and the third-choice option in goal, the kind of steady hand a squad keeps around even when his club is having a rough season. He's only played a handful of times for the national team, so a World Cup appearance would be a rare day out.

players.name: G. Ochoa
players.note: At 40, the veteran keeper is chasing history: a sixth World Cup, a feat only Messi and Ronaldo would share. He's the elder statesman here, famous for the kind of penalty-saving heroics that turned him into a folk hero back in 2014.

players.name: J. Rangel
players.note: Known as "Tala," the Chivas keeper has quietly worked his way into pole position for the starting spot, a big leap for someone who only broke into top-flight football a couple of years ago. The new generation pushing past the old guard, basically.

players.name: J. Gallardo
players.note: A left-back with well over a hundred caps, the Toluca man is heading to his third World Cup, which makes him one of the most experienced bodies in the squad. He started out as a winger, so he loves to gallop forward and lend a hand in attack.

players.name: C. Montes
players.note: A towering centre-back now plying his trade at Lokomotiv Moscow, he's the sort of defender who chips in at the other end too, heading home a few set-pieces at last summer's Gold Cup. Good in the air, hard to get past, and not shy about the dark arts of defending.

players.name: I. Reyes
players.note: A do-it-all defender for Club América who can slot in at centre-back or right-back depending on what the day demands, the kind of versatility coaches quietly adore. He'll get to play the World Cup opener in front of his home crowd, which is about as good as it gets.

players.name: J. Sánchez
players.note: A right-back who has had spells in Europe with Ajax and Porto before circling back home, so he's seen a bit of the world. Quick and busy down the flank, he's the type who'd rather overlap the winger than sit back and watch.

players.name: J. Vásquez
players.note: The centre-back who captains Genoa in Serie A, which tells you everything about how much they trust him: a foreign player handed the armband at an Italian club doesn't happen by accident. He's racked up more Serie A appearances than any Mexican before him, so Italy clearly suits him.

players.name: E. Álvarez
players.note: Mexico's captain and the engine in front of the back four, equally happy breaking up play in midfield or dropping into defence when needed. He scored the winner in last summer's Gold Cup final against the USA and walked off with the player-of-the-tournament award, so the armband is well earned.

players.name: M. Chávez
players.note: A young left-back who came up through the Chivas academy and then made the leap to the Dutch league, betting that a move abroad was the surest route to this World Cup. Fast, disciplined, and keen to join the attack, he's one of the squad's bright young things.

players.name: O. Vargas
players.note: A central midfielder born in Alaska who could have played for the United States but chose Mexico instead, and made his pro debut for the Seattle Sounders at just 15. Still only 20, he's the kind of calm, ball-winning presence good teams build a midfield around.

players.name: L. Chávez
players.note: A midfielder with a left foot that turns dead balls into chances: his thunderbolt free-kick against Saudi Arabia at the last World Cup is still replayed today. Now at Dynamo Moscow, he's recently fought back from a long injury layoff just in time for this tournament.

players.name: Álvaro Fidalgo
players.note: A Spanish-born playmaker who came through Real Madrid's youth ranks, then spent years winning titles with Club América and earned Mexican citizenship along the way. FIFA cleared him to switch allegiance to Mexico early in 2026, so this World Cup is the start of a brand-new international chapter for him.

players.name: B. Gutiérrez
players.note: An attacking midfielder raised in the Chicago Fire academy who took out Mexican citizenship in late 2025 to play for El Tri. He's one of several in this squad who could have lined up for the United States and chose the green shirt instead.

players.name: É. Lira
players.note: A defensive midfielder who captains Cruz Azul, the type who does the unglamorous shielding and tackling so the creative players can shine. Still in his mid-twenties, he's reportedly on the radar of a few big European clubs for after the tournament.

players.name: G. Mora
players.note: At 17, the Tijuana midfielder is the youngest player at the entire World Cup, out of all 1,248 names across the 48 squads. He's been breaking precocious records for a while now, starting and scoring in the Mexican top flight at 15 and helping win the Gold Cup last summer, which is why Europe's biggest clubs are already circling.

players.name: O. Pineda
players.note: A clever playmaker who has made a real home for himself at AEK Athens, where he's collected league titles and a reputation for threading passes nobody else spots. He can play deep or high up the pitch, which gives the coach plenty of options.

players.name: L. Romo
players.note: A genuine Swiss-army-knife player for Chivas who can fill in as a holding midfielder, a sweeper, or a centre-back without missing a beat. He strikes a lovely long pass, so even when he's playing deep he tends to start the attacks.

players.name: R. Alvarado
players.note: Nicknamed "El Piojo," the Chivas winger is a popping-up-in-the-right-place type who has lately taken on more of a playmaking role for his club. This is his second World Cup, so he knows what the big stage feels like.

players.name: S. Giménez
players.note: The AC Milan striker is Mexico's sharpest finisher, a proper number nine who scores with either foot and lives off smart movement in the box. The son of former player Christian Giménez, he's had an injury-bothered season in Serie A, so his place in the XI isn't quite nailed down.

players.name: A. González
players.note: Known as "La Hormiga" (The Ant), the young Chivas striker earned this call-up the hard way, finishing as a top scorer in the Mexican league and forcing his name into the conversation. At 22 he's one to watch, with European clubs already sniffing around.

players.name: C. Huerta
players.note: A direct, quick-footed winger at Anderlecht in Belgium, the kind who likes to take defenders on one-against-one. He's been working his way back from a groin problem, so the question is whether he'll arrive at full sharpness.

players.name: R. Jiménez
players.note: The Fulham striker and one of Mexico's all-time leading scorers, now heading to his fourth World Cup and still chasing an elusive first goal at the tournament. That he's even here is remarkable: he fractured his skull in a sickening collision back in 2020 and came all the way back to the Premier League.

players.name: G. Martínez
players.note: A big, old-fashioned target man for Pumas, nicknamed "Memote," who chips in a steady handful of goals each season. He's one of the squad's home-based forwards, more of a squad option than a guaranteed starter.

players.name: J. Quiñones
players.note: Born in Colombia, he naturalised as Mexican in 2023 and has since turned into a goal machine in Saudi Arabia, outscoring even Cristiano Ronaldo in the league this season. That hot streak makes him one of the more intriguing names in the attack.

players.name: A. Vega
players.note: The Toluca captain and a forward who can drift across the front line or drop in to create, he was electric for his club last season with goals and assists by the bagful. The puzzle is form: he hasn't fired for the national team the way he does at Toluca, and the coaches are betting this is where he turns it around.

players.name: Y. Bounou
players.note: Morocco's undisputed number one and one of the calmest keepers around, he won the 2025 CAF Goalkeeper of the Year award and made a string of famous saves for Al-Hilal at the 2025 Club World Cup. At 34 he is at his third World Cup and remains the spine of this defence.

players.name: M. Mohamedi
players.note: A vastly experienced backup keeper who captains Renaissance Berkane in the Moroccan league and helped them to a domestic title and a continental cup. At 36 he is the squad's elder statesman in goal, here for his know-how rather than to start ahead of Bounou.

players.name: A. Tagnaouti
players.note: The home-based third-choice keeper, he plays for FAR Rabat and was also part of the squad that reached the 2022 World Cup semi-final. At 29 he is unlikely to feature here unless injuries strike, but he adds depth and a familiar voice in the goalkeeping group.

players.name: N. Aguerd
players.note: A composed, ball-playing centre-back who left West Ham for Marseille last summer, he is one of the first names on the team sheet at the heart of Morocco's defence. At 29 he brings the calm head Morocco leaned on during their run to the 2022 semi-finals.

players.name: I. Diop
players.note: A big, physical centre-back at Fulham who came up through France's youth ranks before switching to Morocco through his mother, only making his senior debut in March. At 28 he is a recent addition to the squad and provides extra height and cover at the back rather than a guaranteed start.

players.name: Z. El Ouahdi
players.note: An attacking right-back at Belgian side Genk who has had a remarkable goalscoring season, chipping in with double figures and earning recognition as the league's standout Maghreb player. At 24 he is the long-term understudy to Hakimi, here to learn and to cover that demanding flank.

players.name: A. Hakimi
players.note: The captain and the team's biggest star, a flying right-back for PSG who won the Champions League and Ligue 1 last season and finished sixth in the 2025 Ballon d'Or, the highest ever by a Moroccan. At 27 and on his third World Cup, he is the engine down the right and the player opponents fear most.

players.name: R. Halhal
players.note: A defender who earned his first Morocco call-up off the back of a solid breakthrough season at Belgium's KV Mechelen, having come through the French system. At 22 this is a reward for that form and a chance to settle into the senior set-up rather than a likely starting role.

players.name: N. Mazraoui
players.note: A versatile, technically tidy full-back at Manchester United who can play either flank, often shifting to the left to accommodate Hakimi on the right. At 28 he is a regular starter, though a shoulder injury picked up in a pre-tournament friendly is a fitness worry going into the opener.

players.name: C. Riad
players.note: A La Masia-schooled centre-back at Crystal Palace whose early years in England were wrecked by knee injuries, before he came back to start the 2026 Conference League final win. At 22 he is finally healthy and offers Morocco a calm, modern centre-half who is comfortable on the ball.

players.name: A. Salah-Eddine
players.note: An Ajax-trained left-back, owned by Roma and spending this season on loan at Dutch champions PSV, where he won the title. At 24 he switched his allegiance to Morocco in late 2025 and gives the squad a genuine specialist option on the left side of defence.

players.name: Y. Belammari
players.note: A left-sided defender who moved to Egyptian giants Al Ahly in early 2026 and quickly became a first-choice pick there. At 27 he was part of the squad that reached the AFCON final on home soil, and after recovering from a muscle injury he offers added cover across the back line.

players.name: S. Amrabat
players.note: The tireless defensive midfielder who shielded the back four during Morocco's 2022 semi-final run, now on loan at Real Betis from Fenerbahce. At 29 his all-action engine remains the team's anchor, though a knee knock late in 2025 means his sharpness will be worth watching.

players.name: A. Bouaddi
players.note: At 18 the youngest player in the squad, a deep-lying midfielder already a regular at Lille and one of Ligue 1's most coveted teenagers, with big clubs circling. He only committed to Morocco over France in May, so this tournament is an exciting glimpse of a future cornerstone rather than a settled starter.

players.name: N. El Aynaoui
players.note: A box-to-box midfielder who earned a big move from Lens to Roma last summer, son of former tennis pro Younes El Aynaoui and a dual French-Moroccan who chose the Atlas Lions. At 24 his minutes in Italy have been limited, so he is squad depth in a crowded midfield rather than a guaranteed starter.

players.name: B. El Khannouss
players.note: A creative, left-footed attacking midfielder enjoying a productive season at Stuttgart, chipping in with goals and assists in the Bundesliga. At 21 he is one of the brightest young talents in this squad and the kind of player who can unlock a stubborn defence with a single pass or carry.

players.name: S. El Mourabet
players.note: A young central midfielder who has quietly become one of Strasbourg's most-used players this season despite his age. At 20 he is squad depth here, called up on the back of consistent Ligue 1 minutes, with plenty of room still to grow.

players.name: A. Ounahi
players.note: The elegant midfielder whose dazzling 2022 World Cup made his name, now reborn at Girona after a quiet spell at Marseille and named their player of the month early this season. At 25 his graceful dribbling and passing add a touch of magic, though a foot injury kept him out of the AFCON knockouts, so his fitness is one to track.

players.name: I. Saibari
players.note: An attacking midfielder who was named PSV's player of the year after a brilliant season with 15 goals and 8 assists as the club retained the Dutch title. At 24 he is one of Morocco's most dangerous creative options, with his fitness after a late-season rehab spell the only question mark.

players.name: C. Talbi
players.note: A direct, exciting winger who moved from Club Brugge to Sunderland and became a fan favourite, scoring against the likes of Chelsea, Liverpool and Newcastle in his debut Premier League season. At 20 he chose Morocco over Belgium and gives the attack a fearless one-on-one threat off the bench or out wide.

players.name: Gessime Yassine
players.note: An instinctive, quick-footed winger who joined Strasbourg in early 2026 and was a key figure in Morocco's run to the 2025 Under-20 World Cup title. At 20 this senior call-up is recognition of that promise; he is squad depth for now, learning alongside the seniors.

players.name: Brahim Díaz
players.note: The Real Madrid forward and Morocco's chief creator, who lit up AFCON 2025 by scoring in every group game and taking the Golden Boot, even if the final ended in heartbreak. At 26 the Spanish-born attacker is a starter and the team's most likely source of a moment of brilliance.

players.name: A. Amaimouni
players.note: A left-footed winger who racked up goals in Germany's lower divisions and earned a move up, a Spanish-born talent who has chosen to push for Morocco. At 20 he is a developmental pick in this attack, here to gain experience rather than to start, with a high ceiling on the wing.

players.name: A. El Kaabi
players.note: A prolific poacher who has been banging in goals for Olympiakos, including a string of European competition top-scorer finishes, and weighed in heavily at AFCON 2025 with some spectacular overhead kicks. At 32 he is Morocco's most natural number nine and a strong candidate to lead the line.

players.name: A. Ezzalzouli
players.note: A tricky left winger at Real Betis who has hit double figures for goals this season and drawn interest from several Premier League clubs. At 24 his pace and dribbling give Morocco a real cutting edge wide on the left, and he is firmly in the mix to start.

players.name: S. Rahimi
players.note: A clinical forward at Al Ain who top-scored as they won the 2024 AFC Champions League and was once named the world's best international goalscorer in a calendar year. At 29 he offers Morocco a proven finisher, an option to start or to change a game from the bench.

players.name: M. Flekken
players.note: After two seasons in England with Brentford, Flekken went back to Germany with Leverkusen chasing the Champions League nights he'd been missing. He's the experienced hand in the Dutch keeping order, even if the gloves aren't guaranteed to be his.

players.name: R. Roefs
players.note: Two summers ago Roefs was an unknown keeping goal for NEC in the Dutch league; now he's a Premier League starter at Sunderland and along for the World Cup ride. A rapid rise for a 22-year-old most fans couldn't have named a year ago.

players.name: B. Verbruggen
players.note: Don't let the low squad number fool you into thinking he's a veteran; Verbruggen is barely into his twenties but has already been the Netherlands' first-choice keeper since their run to the Euro 2024 semi-finals. This is his first proper World Cup as the number one.

players.name: N. Aké
players.note: Aké is the Swiss-army-knife defender Koeman loves: happy at centre-back, just as comfortable filling in at left-back, and quietly reliable at Manchester City for years. The one knock is that injuries keep nibbling at his big tournaments.

players.name: D. Dumfries
players.note: Dumfries is the engine down the Dutch right: technically a defender, but he spends most of the game charging up and down the touchline and turning up in the box to score. Years at Inter have made him one of the most dependable wing-backs in Europe.

players.name: J. Hato
players.note: At 19, Hato is the baby of the squad, a left-sided defender Chelsea paid serious money to prise out of Ajax's famous youth setup. He's been captaining the youth teams and earning senior caps almost simultaneously, which tells you how highly he's rated.

players.name: J. Timber
players.note: Jurrien is the Timber twin who went to England, where he's become a defensive fixture at Arsenal capable of slotting in at right-back or centre-back. His identical twin Quinten is also in this squad, so good luck telling the team sheet apart.

players.name: V. van Dijk
players.note: The captain and the calm at the back: Van Dijk has anchored Liverpool's defence for years and is the player every Dutch teammate looks to when things get nervy. At 34 this is almost certainly his last World Cup, and the Guardian made him their Dutch star pick.

players.name: J. van Hecke
players.note: Van Hecke is the late bloomer who turned himself into Brighton's defensive leader and Player of the Season, which got bigger clubs sniffing around. He only broke into the senior Dutch side a couple of years ago, but he's earned his seat on the plane.

players.name: M. van de Ven
players.note: Van de Ven's superpower is flat-out speed: he's been clocked as one of the fastest players in the Premier League, which lets him cover acres of space behind the Dutch defence. A ball-playing centre-back who can sprint a striker down and start the attack himself.

players.name: M. Wieffer
players.note: Wieffer is a holding midfielder by trade who Brighton also use further back, the kind of all-running, hard-tackling player who does the unglamorous work so the stars can shine. He cost Feyenoord's record sale fee, so someone clearly values that engine.

players.name: R. Gravenberch
players.note: Gravenberch finally clicked at Liverpool, anchoring their midfield in a standout season and shaking off the 'wasted talent' label that once followed him. For the Dutch he sits deep alongside Frenkie de Jong, doing the calm, composed work in the middle.

players.name: T. Koopmeiners
players.note: Koopmeiners arrived at Juventus for a fortune off the back of brilliant box-to-box years at Atalanta, but the move just hasn't sparked and he's been in and out of form ever since. The talent's there; the World Cup is a chance to remind everyone of it.

players.name: T. Reijnders
players.note: Reijnders is the Dutch midfield's link man, breaking up play and then gliding forward to join the attack; when he plays well, the Netherlands usually do too. He was named Serie A's best midfielder at Milan before Manchester City came calling.

players.name: G. Til
players.note: Til is an attacking midfielder who scores like a forward: he banged in 14 league goals for PSV this season, which is a lot for a man supposedly playing behind the strikers. The squad's quiet goal threat from deep.

players.name: Q. Timber
players.note: The other Timber twin, a midfielder rather than a defender like brother Jurrien, who skippered Feyenoord and scored in World Cup qualifying. Knee trouble cost him a big chunk of last season, so this tournament is a welcome clean slate.

players.name: F. de Jong
players.note: De Jong is the metronome who keeps Barcelona and the Netherlands ticking, gliding past pressers and rarely giving the ball away. He makes the hard stuff look unhurried, which is exactly why every coach wants him in the middle.

players.name: M. de Roon
players.note: At 34, De Roon is the squad's grizzled holding midfielder, a one-club loyalist who recently became Atalanta's all-time appearance record holder. Not flashy, but the sort of dependable presence you want when a tournament tightens up.

players.name: J. Kluivert
players.note: Yes, that surname is the giveaway: Justin is the son of Dutch great Patrick Kluivert, and he's carved out his own name at Bournemouth as a sharp attacking threat. He famously scored a Premier League hat-trick entirely from the penalty spot, which is as rare as it sounds.

players.name: B. Brobbey
players.note: A powerful, bustling striker who made his name banging in goals for Ajax before moving to the Premier League with Sunderland. Brobbey leads the line with muscle rather than finesse, the kind of forward who wrestles defenders all afternoon.

players.name: M. Depay
players.note: Depay is the Netherlands' all-time leading scorer, the talisman who took a left turn most European stars don't and went to play in Brazil with Corinthians. He's the squad's only player from the Brazilian league, and still the man they look to for a moment of magic.

players.name: C. Gakpo
players.note: Gakpo can play left wing or lead the line, and his calm finishing helped Liverpool win the league. For the Dutch he's a likely starter up top, a versatile attacker who tends to deliver his goals on the biggest nights.

players.name: N. Lang
players.note: Lang is the squad's flair pick, a direct, tricky winger who tore up the Dutch league for PSV before his move to Italy. Confident on and off the pitch, he's the kind of player who can win a game on his own or frustrate you trying.

players.name: D. Malen
players.note: Malen is a pacey winger-cum-forward who made his name with bundles of goals at Borussia Dortmund. He's in the mix for the spot on the right of the Dutch attack, the sort of player who's most dangerous running at a tired defence.

players.name: C. Summerville
players.note: Summerville was a surprise late call-up who only earned his first senior Dutch cap in the warm-up games, having been the standout player in England's second tier before stepping up. A quick, direct winger getting his shot at the very biggest stage.

players.name: W. Weghorst
players.note: At nearly six-and-a-half feet, Weghorst is the squad's old-fashioned target man, the giant you bring on to win headers and bully tired defenders late in games. A folk hero since his dramatic 2022 World Cup cameo against Argentina, he's exactly the plan B you want.

players.name: M. Crocombe
players.note: At 32, the Millwall keeper looks set to be New Zealand's number one in goal at the World Cup. He arrived in south London as a backup, then seized the gloves when the first-choice got injured and refused to let go, putting together a long run of starts and clean sheets.

players.name: A. Paulsen
players.note: A 23-year-old goalkeeper owned by Bournemouth but spending the season on loan in Poland with Lechia Gdansk to get regular games. He is highly rated for his age and pushes Crocombe hard for the starting spot, so the gloves could yet be his.

players.name: M. Woud
players.note: The third-choice keeper, here to train and provide cover rather than expecting minutes. He had a fine season at home, keeping a clean sheet as Auckland FC won the A-League title in their second-ever year, so he arrives in form even if the pecking order is against him.

players.name: Tyler Bindon
players.note: At just 20, he is one of the brightest young centre-backs in the squad and a likely starter at the back. He is owned by Premier League Nottingham Forest and spent this season out on loan in the Championship, where he showed he is comfortable defending against grown men and even chipped in with a goal.

players.name: M. Boxall
players.note: The 37-year-old elder statesman of the defence and the captain of Minnesota United, where he is the club's all-time leader in appearances. He scored the goal that clinched New Zealand's World Cup place, so expect a calm, vocal organiser marshalling the younger players around him.

players.name: L. Cacace
players.note: An attacking left-back and one of the team's key men, he joined Wrexham last summer for a club-record fee after years in Italy's Serie A. Calf and hamstring trouble wrecked his first season in Wales, so getting fully fit before the tournament is the big question over him.

players.name: F. de Vries
players.note: A 31-year-old left-back who was one of the standout creators in the A-League this season, racking up assists from the flank for champions Auckland FC. A calf strain picked up on international duty cut his club campaign short, so his fitness and form heading into the tournament are worth watching.

players.name: C. Elliot
players.note: A versatile defender for champions Auckland FC who filled in at right-back, left-back and even midfield this season as injuries piled up. Born in Scotland and raised in New Zealand from age seven, he fought his way back from a spell without a club to reach a World Cup, which makes him a useful squad option rather than a guaranteed starter.

players.name: T. Payne
players.note: An experienced Wellington Phoenix full-back with more than 50 caps who can cover right-back or centre-back, exactly the kind of versatility a coach loves. He briefly went viral online before the tournament as the squad's supposed 'least known' player, and a broken collarbone in October interrupted his season.

players.name: N. Pijnaker
players.note: A 26-year-old centre-back, born in the Netherlands, who was part of the Auckland FC side that won the A-League title this season. He is comfortable on the ball and has a habit of popping up with dramatic late goals, giving the squad a reliable option in central defence.

players.name: T. Smith
players.note: At 35, a remarkable story: he started all three games at the 2010 World Cup and spent more than a decade in England's top divisions with Ipswich, yet now plays for Braintree in the fifth tier. His recall makes him perhaps the lowest-division player at the whole tournament, brought in for big-stage experience as squad depth.

players.name: F. Surman
players.note: A tall, 22-year-old centre-back who broke out for Portland Timbers in Major League Soccer this season, starting most weeks and winning his club's supporters' player of the year. Quick and composed for his size, he is one of the country's most promising young defenders and pushing hard for a starting role.

players.name: L. Bayliss
players.note: A 23-year-old central midfielder who was born and raised in Australia but chose to play for New Zealand, earning his first cap only a few months before the squad was named. A bright A-League season with Newcastle Jets put him on the radar, so he arrives as an exciting, lightly capped newcomer rather than a regular.

players.name: J. Bell
players.note: A defensive midfielder and one of the engine-room regulars, he just helped Norwegian club Viking win their first league title in 34 years and was named in the division's team of the season. Expect him to sit in front of the back four, break up play and keep things ticking over.

players.name: M. Garbett
players.note: A 23-year-old midfielder who can play anywhere across the middle, from a holding role to the number ten. He moved to England's League One with Peterborough last summer after a spell in the Dutch top flight and chipped in with goals, though an injury during the season is something to keep an eye on.

players.name: C. McCowatt
players.note: Listed here as a midfielder, he is really an attacking left winger and one of the squad's in-form players, scoring double figures in the Danish top flight including a hat-trick away at Copenhagen, and named his club's player of the year. He gives New Zealand a genuine goal threat from wide areas.

players.name: A. Rufer
players.note: A combative midfielder from New Zealand football royalty: his uncle Wynton Rufer was named Oceania's player of the century and his father also played for the national team. He is the longest-serving player and first homegrown captain at Wellington Phoenix, giving the squad a tireless, experienced option in central midfield.

players.name: S. Singh
players.note: An attacking playmaker who carries the number ten and was once a teenage signing for Bayern Munich, though he never quite cracked their first team. Now at Serbian club TSC, he is of Indian Punjabi heritage and would be a rare and notable presence at a World Cup, bringing creativity if he can find his best form.

players.name: M. Stamenic
players.note: A 23-year-old central midfielder and one of the team's key men, he joined Championship side Swansea last summer after time on the books at Nottingham Forest. He has settled into English football well, weighing in with goals and assists, and is expected to be a starter in the middle of the park.

players.name: R. Thomas
players.note: An experienced midfielder who has spent most of his career in the Dutch top flight and is now a regular for PEC Zwolle, recently signing a contract extension there. After a long spell away from the national team he forced his way back into the picture, so he brings hard-earned European know-how to the group.

players.name: E. Just
players.note: A winger who had the best season of his career in the Scottish Premiership with Motherwell, scoring regularly and earning a place in the league's team of the year. That form has reportedly drawn interest from bigger clubs, and it makes him a real attacking weapon off either flank for New Zealand.

players.name: B. Old
players.note: A 23-year-old attacking midfielder who made history as one of the first New Zealanders to play in France's top division with Saint-Etienne. After falling out of favour earlier in the season he battled back into the side and strung together a long run of starts, so he is a player on the rise heading into the tournament.

players.name: K. Barbarouses
players.note: A 35-year-old winger and the most experienced active player in the A-League, having made more appearances than anyone and won four league titles across his long career. He moved to Western Sydney Wanderers this season and gives the squad a wily, well-travelled attacking option from the bench.

players.name: J. Randall
players.note: A 23-year-old forward who enjoyed a breakout season for champions Auckland FC, scoring nine goals and laying on plenty more while starting every game of their title-winning campaign. He has already lined up a move to Scotland and arrives as a young, in-form attacker pushing for minutes.

players.name: B. Waine
players.note: A 24-year-old striker who finished as joint top scorer for English club Port Vale this season and built a reputation for big cup goals, including a winner against Premier League opposition. He gives New Zealand a hard-working, willing-runner alternative to lead the line behind Chris Wood.

players.name: C. Wood
players.note: The captain, the talisman and the country's all-time leading appearance maker, this 34-year-old Premier League striker is the man New Zealand will lean on for goals. He missed several months of the season after knee surgery, so how sharp he is after that long lay-off may decide how far the team goes.

players.name: Ø. Nyland
players.note: At 35, the veteran of the squad and Norway's likely number one in goal, even though he spent much of the season as a backup at Sevilla. Steady and experienced rather than flashy, exactly what you want behind a young defence at a first World Cup in nearly three decades.

players.name: E. Selvik
players.note: A 28-year-old keeper at Watford in England's second tier, here as a backup option behind Nyland. He spent years as a reliable starter and captain in Norway before moving abroad, so he brings calm cover rather than a likely starting spot.

players.name: S. Tangvik
players.note: The youngest of the three keepers at 23, a tall shot-stopper who broke through as a regular starter in the Norwegian league and earned his first senior call-ups late in qualifying. This tournament is mostly about experience for him; expect him to train and learn rather than play.

players.name: K. Ajer
players.note: A tall, ball-playing centre-back for Brentford and one of Norway's likely starting defenders. He even chipped in with goals during qualifying, and at 27 he is now one of the senior heads anchoring a fairly young back line.

players.name: F. Bjørkan
players.note: A 27-year-old left-back for Bodo/Glimt, the club that punched above its weight in Europe, where he gained Champions League experience. He provides cover and competition at left-back rather than a guaranteed start.

players.name: H. Falchener
players.note: A towering 22-year-old centre-back who had a breakout season for Viking, scoring more goals than any other defender in the Norwegian league as his club topped the table for the first time in over thirty years. Newly capped and one for the future, he is squad depth at this tournament.

players.name: S. Langås
players.note: A 24-year-old centre-back who became a regular starter for Derby in England's second tier after moving over from Norway, even chipping in with a few goals. He is part of the defensive cover here rather than a first-choice pick.

players.name: T. Heggem
players.note: A 26-year-old centre-back whose stock has risen fast: a player-of-the-season award in England earned him a move to Bologna in Italy's Serie A, and he is now pencilled in to start alongside Ajer at the back. Comfortable on the ball and able to fill in at left-back.

players.name: L. Østigård
players.note: A 26-year-old centre-back at Genoa with a well-travelled career and a Serie A title from his Napoli days. He had a productive league season scoring a handful of goals, but in this squad he is experienced backup behind the first-choice pairing.

players.name: M. Pedersen
players.note: A 25-year-old right-back at Torino who became a league regular in Italy and won an Eredivisie title earlier in his career with Feyenoord. He can cover both flanks, which makes him useful depth behind Norway's first-choice full-backs.

players.name: D. Møller Wolfe
players.note: A 23-year-old left-back who earned a big-money move to Wolves in the Premier League after standing out in the Netherlands for his attacking output from the flank. He is in the frame to start at left-back, offering plenty going forward.

players.name: T. Aasgaard
players.note: A 23-year-old midfielder at Rangers in Scotland, born in Liverpool and Norwegian through his father. An attack-minded player who chips in with goals, he is one of the squad's younger options in midfield rather than a regular starter.

players.name: F. Aursnes
players.note: A 30-year-old midfielder at Benfica, reliable and versatile across the middle and flanks. He had actually retired from international football, then reversed that decision once Norway reached the finals so he could finally play at a World Cup.

players.name: P. Berg
players.note: A 28-year-old defensive midfielder and captain of Bodo/Glimt, from a famous Norwegian footballing family. He racked up assists and led his club to league titles and a deep European run, bringing leadership and tidy passing to Norway's midfield depth.

players.name: S. Berge
players.note: A 27-year-old defensive midfielder at Fulham and one of Norway's likely starters in the engine room. Tall and rangy, his job is the unglamorous one of breaking up play and screening the back four so the creative players ahead of him can shine.

players.name: Oscar Bobb
players.note: A 22-year-old winger who joined Fulham in January chasing regular minutes after years on the fringes at Manchester City, partly due to injuries. Quick and inventive, he is one of Norway's most exciting attacking options off the bench.

players.name: M. Ødegaard
players.note: Norway's captain and creative heartbeat, the 27-year-old Arsenal playmaker who pulls the strings from midfield. A knee injury wrecked much of his club season, but he marked his return by scoring in a World Cup warm-up; how fit he is may shape how far Norway can go.

players.name: M. Thorsby
players.note: A 29-year-old hard-running midfielder with a Serie A pedigree, valued for his energy and willingness to do the dirty work. He famously wears number 2 as a nod to his climate campaigning, and offers experienced cover in the middle of the park.

players.name: K. Thorstvedt
players.note: A 26-year-old box-to-box midfielder at Sassuolo who weighs in with goals and assists from deeper positions. He is firmly in the mix for a starting role and is set for his first World Cup, part of a midfield three meant to support Odegaard.

players.name: A. Schjelderup
players.note: A 21-year-old forward and one of the brightest young talents in the squad, he finished the season strongly at Benfica and is now among their most coveted players. A left-sided attacker who can play through the middle, he gives Norway dangerous depth in the final third.

players.name: J. Hauge
players.note: A 26-year-old left winger back at Bodo/Glimt after spells in Italy and Germany, where he shone in the Champions League with a brace against Tottenham. A direct dribbler with an eye for goal, he is a useful wide attacking option from the bench.

players.name: E. Haaland
players.note: The reason Norway are even here, and one of the most feared strikers on the planet. The 25-year-old Manchester City forward scored in all eight qualifiers, racking up 16 goals to drag his country to a first World Cup in 28 years. Defences will plan their whole match around stopping him.

players.name: J. Strand Larsen
players.note: A 25-year-old striker who enjoyed a strong first season in the Premier League with Wolves and scored the late goal in Italy that sealed Norway's qualification. With Haaland and Sorloth ahead of him, he is an able backup who can lead the line if needed.

players.name: A. Nusa
players.note: At 20, one of Norway's most exciting young attackers and a likely starter on the wing. The RB Leipzig winger is comfortable on either flank, with the explosive pace and direct dribbling to terrify full-backs on the counter.

players.name: A. Sørloth
players.note: A 30-year-old striker for Atletico Madrid who is among Europe's most prolific forwards, once scoring four times in a single La Liga match. Expected to start alongside Haaland, he gives Norway a powerful, physical front two that few defences will relish facing.

players.name: J. Ryerson
players.note: A 28-year-old full-back and wing-back for Borussia Dortmund, despite being listed here as an attacker, and tipped to start at right-back for Norway. He is an excellent crosser who racked up assists in the Bundesliga and is happy to bomb forward down either flank.

players.name: L. Mejía
players.note: Panama's first-choice goalkeeper and, at 34, one of the calmer heads in the squad. He has spent the last couple of years at Uruguayan club Nacional, and he is the man expected to stand between the posts when Panama plays only its second World Cup.

players.name: O. Mosquera
players.note: A tall, 31-year-old goalkeeper who gets regular minutes in the Saudi Pro League with Al-Fayha. He is the experienced backup behind Mejía, the kind of keeper a manager trusts to step in without the team missing a beat.

players.name: C. Samudio
players.note: The third goalkeeper, who plays his club football in Honduras with Marathón and was once named the standout player as he won the Panamanian league with CAI. He is unlikely to play here, but he gives the keeper group an extra body who knows how to win things.

players.name: A. Andrade
players.note: A 27-year-old centre-back who has become a fixture, and vice-captain, at Austrian club LASK. He is one of the more reliable defenders in this squad and someone Panama will lean on to organise the back line.

players.name: C. Blackman
players.note: An attack-minded right-back at Slovakia's Slovan Bratislava, where he has chipped in with goals and a healthy pile of assists this season. At 27 he offers Panama overlapping width down the right, the sort of full-back who likes getting forward as much as defending.

players.name: J. Córdoba
players.note: At 24, Panama's most valuable defender and a central pillar of the back line. A composed, left-footed centre-back, he moved to England's Norwich in 2024 and is comfortable bringing the ball out from the back; expect him to start every game.

players.name: É. Davis
players.note: A 34-year-old left-back and one of the squad's elder statesmen, who captained Panama through their run at the 2024 Copa América. He has played all over the place from Slovakia to MLS to Brazil, and his value here is as much about leadership as defending.

players.name: F. Escobar
players.note: A 30-year-old centre-back at Costa Rican giants Saprissa and a dangerous header of the ball, including one in qualifying that helped push Panama through. He made the Gold Cup Best XI in 2023, so he is a defender who shows up in the big moments.

players.name: E. Fariña
players.note: A towering 24-year-old defender who moved to Russia's Nizhny Novgorod in 2025 and has been getting steady minutes there. He is one of the younger options at the back, around to add height and develop into a longer-term starter.

players.name: J. Gutiérrez
players.note: A 27-year-old left-back who has built his career in Venezuela with Deportivo La Guaira and broke into the national team during qualifying. He is one of two players the Venezuelan league sent to this squad, useful cover and competition down the left.

players.name: C. Harvey
players.note: A 25-year-old who can fill in across defence and midfield, which makes him a handy utility option. He has become a regular at MLS side Minnesota United and was part of Panama's run to the 2025 Nations League final.

players.name: R. Miller
players.note: A well-travelled 33-year-old centre-back whose career has taken him from Iraq to Kazakhstan to Portugal and now Azerbaijan's Turan Tovuz. He is squad depth at the back, the experienced spare option a tournament squad always needs.

players.name: A. Murillo
players.note: Panama's marquee name and the Guardian's pick as their player to watch, a 29-year-old right-back playing his club football at France's Marseille. Quick, aggressive and good going forward, he is the most recognisable face in the team and a near-certain starter.

players.name: J. Ramos
players.note: A 28-year-old centre-back known for his strength and aerial presence, who has played across South America before this spell at home club Independiente de La Chorrera. He is depth in central defence, a reliable body to rotate in.

players.name: A. Carrasquilla
players.note: Panama's creative engine in midfield, a 27-year-old playmaker at Mexico's Pumas who dictates the team's tempo. He picked up an injury in the Liga MX final shortly before the tournament, so his fitness is something to keep an eye on, because Panama is a different side with him pulling the strings.

players.name: A. Godoy
players.note: The captain and the most-capped player in Panama's history, with more than 150 appearances since 2010. At 35 he is a defensive midfielder who screens the back four, now plying his trade at MLS newcomers San Diego FC and leading a team chasing a first-ever World Cup win.

players.name: C. Martinez
players.note: A 28-year-old defensive midfielder who moved to Israel's Ironi Kiryat Shmona in 2025 and has weighed in with a few goals from deep. He gives the manager a sturdier, more defensive option in the centre of the park.

players.name: J. Rodríguez
players.note: A 27-year-old left winger nicknamed 'El Puma', a direct, left-footed dribbler now at Mexico's FC Juárez after a spell in Serbia. He gives Panama pace and a one-on-one threat out wide, the kind of player who can change a game off the bench or from the start.

players.name: Y. Bárcenas
players.note: A 32-year-old winger at Mexico's Mazatlán with more than 100 caps for Panama, prized for his speed and dribbling down the flanks. He tore a knee ligament in early 2025, so this tournament is a reward for fighting his way back to fitness.

players.name: I. Díaz
players.note: Panama's main attacking spark, a 28-year-old who hits double figures for goals and assists at Mexico's León. He wears the number 10 and operates as a winger or second striker; if Panama is going to score at this World Cup, he is likely to be involved.

players.name: A. Quintero
players.note: At 38 the oldest player in the squad and the owner of its best story: a veteran winger who was named for the 2018 World Cup but lost his place to injury before a ball was kicked. Now at home club Plaza Amador, he finally gets the tournament that was taken from him.

players.name: C. Yanis
players.note: A 29-year-old central midfielder who moved to Chile's Cobresal and earned a contract renewal there. With more than 50 caps to his name, he is a squad option in the engine room rather than a guaranteed starter.

players.name: J. Fajardo
players.note: A 32-year-old centre-forward who scored at a steady clip for Universidad Católica through 2025. As one of the squad's recognised goalscorers, he is in the mix to lead the line and give Panama a genuine focal point up top.

players.name: A. Londoño
players.note: At 24, one of the youngest forwards in the squad, on loan at Universidad Católica where he got a full season of senior minutes. He is a project striker here to gain experience, more likely to feature from the bench than start.

players.name: T. Rodríguez
players.note: A 26-year-old forward who had a breakout 2025, becoming the first Panamanian to score in each of his first three Gold Cup appearances and piling up goals for Venezuela's Monagas. He is in-form depth up front, the kind of impact option a manager likes to have ready.

players.name: C. Waterman
players.note: The 34-year-old striker who wrote himself into Panamanian folklore with a late winner against the United States that sent the country to its first Nations League final. He won a Chilean league title with Coquimbo Unido in 2025, so he arrives a proven big-moment finisher.

players.name: R. Fernandez
players.note: Known to everyone as Gatito, the 37-year-old Cerro Porteno keeper is Paraguay's first choice and the calm, vastly experienced head behind a defence that conceded very little during qualifying. Expect him between the posts when the tournament starts.

players.name: O. Gill
players.note: A towering 25-year-old who has become San Lorenzo's regular keeper in Argentina, Gill is the heir apparent here but likely backs up the veteran Gatito for now. He only made his senior Paraguay debut in late 2025, so this is a fast education.

players.name: G. Olveira
players.note: Uruguay-born and naturalised, the 32-year-old Olimpia keeper is the third choice here, on hand to train and cover rather than play. A steady domestic-league veteran filling out the goalkeeping trio.

players.name: O. Alderete
players.note: A 29-year-old centre-back who moved to newly promoted Sunderland in 2025 and quietly helped them survive in the Premier League, the left-footed Alderete is one of the pillars of Paraguay's defence. Comfortable across the back line and good in the air.

players.name: J. Alonso
players.note: A 32-year-old left-sided centre-back who has spent years anchoring Atletico Mineiro's defence in Brazil, Alonso is a long-serving international first capped back in 2013. Reliable squad experience who can step into the back line when needed.

players.name: J. Cáceres
players.note: A 25-year-old right-back born and raised in Argentina who came through Boca Juniors' academy before moving to Russia, Caceres switched allegiance to Paraguay and earned his place by shutting down dangerous wingers in qualifying. Tough in one-on-one duels.

players.name: F. Balbuena
players.note: A 34-year-old centre-back with a long CV that includes three seasons at West Ham, Balbuena joined Gremio in 2025 and brings calm, battle-tested defending. A four-time Copa America participant, he is depth and leadership rather than a guaranteed starter now.

players.name: G. Gómez
players.note: The captain and the heartbeat of this side, the 32-year-old has anchored Palmeiras' defence for years and is unusually dangerous from set pieces, having become the club's highest-scoring defender. He leads Paraguay into his first World Cup with around 90 caps behind him.

players.name: A. Maidana
players.note: At 20 the baby of the squad, this left-back came through Guarani's youth ranks and played at the 2025 U-20 World Cup before a senior debut in early 2026. He is here to learn from the veterans, with the long-term left-back slot in mind.

players.name: G. Velázquez
players.note: A 34-year-old centre-back who returned home to Cerro Porteno in 2025 after a spell with Newell's in Argentina, Velazquez offers experienced cover at the back. More of a squad option than a nailed-on starter in this group.

players.name: J. Canale
players.note: A 29-year-old centre-back who became a fixture in Lanus' back line on their run to the 2025 Copa Sudamericana final, Canale earned a maiden Paraguay call-up only this year. A late-bloomer reward for consistent form, here as defensive depth.

players.name: D. Bobadilla
players.note: A 24-year-old central midfielder who has carved out a role at Sao Paulo since moving to Brazil, Bobadilla does the unglamorous covering and ball-winning in front of the defence. A useful option in Paraguay's engine room.

players.name: G. Caballero
players.note: A 24-year-old winger who was a joint top scorer in Paraguay's league before earning a move abroad, Caballero brings pace and direct running off the bench. One of the squad's wildcards, rewarded for a breakout couple of seasons.

players.name: A. Cubas
players.note: A 29-year-old defensive midfielder who has become a fan favourite at Vancouver for his relentless tackling and ball recovery, Cubas is the kind of player who lets the creative names shine. Born in Argentina, he is set for his first World Cup as a key shield in front of the defence.

players.name: M. Galarza
players.note: A 23-year-old midfielder who featured in several of Paraguay's qualifying matches, Galarza can play box-to-box or sit deeper. A youngster building his international footing, more likely to feature off the bench than start.

players.name: D. Gómez
players.note: At 22, one of Paraguay's brightest talents, this versatile midfielder earned a big-money move from Inter Miami to Brighton in 2025 and chips in with goals from midfield. Energetic and two-footed, he is central to how this team plays going forward.

players.name: Maurício
players.note: A 24-year-old Brazil-born attacking midfielder who took over the playmaker role at Palmeiras, Mauricio only switched allegiance to Paraguay through his father's family in early 2026. A fresh creative option still settling into the international setup.

players.name: B. Ojeda
players.note: A 25-year-old midfielder who briefly passed through Nottingham Forest before settling at Real Salt Lake, where he now scores and creates regularly. Recalled to the national team after a couple of years away, Ojeda is a useful all-rounder in the middle.

players.name: R. Sosa
players.note: A 26-year-old winger whose pace and one-on-one dribbling earned a move from Nottingham Forest to Palmeiras in 2025, Sosa gives Paraguay a direct threat out wide. Listed here as a midfielder but really an attacker who runs at defenders.

players.name: M. Almirón
players.note: The number 10 and most recognisable name, the 31-year-old spent six years at Newcastle, where he helped them back into the Champions League, before returning to Atlanta United in 2025. He carries Paraguay's creativity and is a near-certain starter.

players.name: A. Romero
players.note: A 30-year-old right winger and one half of the Romero twins (his brother Oscar is also a Paraguay regular), known for his crossing and a knack for big goals. An experienced wide option who can change a game from the flank.

players.name: A. Arce
players.note: A 30-year-old striker who made his name with a prolific scoring run at LDU Quito, banging in goals at better than one every other game. A genuine penalty-box finisher, he has pushed his way into Paraguay's forward line.

players.name: G. Ávalos
players.note: At 35 the oldest outfield player here, this Independiente striker is in fine scoring form in Argentina and was determined to arrive at the World Cup sharp. A target-man option and experienced head, useful from the bench when Paraguay need a goal.

players.name: J. Enciso
players.note: The Guardian's pick as Paraguay's star man, this 21-year-old left Brighton for Strasbourg in 2025 to play regular football in a World Cup year, and the gamble paid off with goals and assists in Ligue 1. Quick, inventive and unpredictable, he is the one who can produce a moment of magic.

players.name: I. Pitta
players.note: A 26-year-old forward who scores steadily for Bragantino in Brazil's top flight, Pitta is a relatively recent addition to the national team. Squad depth up front, ready to step in if the first-choice strikers tire or pick up knocks.

players.name: A. Sanabria
players.note: Paraguay's experienced number 9 and a Serie A regular for years, the 29-year-old moved to Cremonese in 2025 and leads the line for his country. He links play as much as he scores, and is the focal point of the attack.

players.name: Diogo Costa
players.note: Porto's first-choice keeper and the man who inherited the captain's armband there once the veterans moved on, he piled up a stack of clean sheets on the way to a league title. He's the calm, reliable presence Portugal trust to start, the sort of goalkeeper who makes the hard saves look routine.

players.name: José Sá
players.note: The backup keeper has spent the season at Wolves, where he lost his spot for a spell before clawing it back at a club scrapping near the bottom of the Premier League. He's here as cover rather than a starter, an experienced pair of hands to have on the bench.

players.name: Rui Silva
players.note: At 31, the Sporting keeper is having arguably the best run of his career, helping his club push deep into Europe in a standout season. The third name in Portugal's goalkeeping queue, but one who's earned the trip on form.

players.name: Tomás Araújo
players.note: A 23-year-old centre-back who has become a regular at Benfica, comfortable slotting in at right-back too, with a release clause big enough that the bigger clubs keep circling. He plays out from the back as readily as he defends, the modern sort of defender coaches build around.

players.name: João Cancelo
players.note: A full-back who can play either flank and loves stepping into midfield to pick a pass, he's now on Al-Hilal's books in Saudi Arabia after years at the top of the European game. The kind of attacking defender who treats overlapping runs as the whole point of the job.

players.name: Diogo Dalot
players.note: Manchester United's reliable right-back who'll happily fill in on the left, the type who quietly racks up appearances without much fuss. Steady, two-footed and rarely caught out, he's the dependable option Portugal can plug in either side of defence.

players.name: Rúben Dias
players.note: Manchester City's commanding centre-back and the man Portugal build their defence around, the sort who organises everyone in front of him and wins the ball without losing his shape. One of the squad's senior leaders, all calm authority at the back.

players.name: Gonçalo Inácio
players.note: A left-footed centre-back at Sporting whose passing range turns defending into the start of an attack, the kind of ball-player Europe's big clubs have been eyeing for a while. Good on the deck, dangerous from set-pieces, and still only 24.

players.name: Nuno Mendes
players.note: PSG's flying left-back, widely rated among the best in the world in his position, and named the standout player when Portugal won the Nations League final. He overlaps like a winger and recovers like a sprinter, all of 23 and only getting better.

players.name: Nélson Semedo
players.note: A quick, experienced right-back now playing in Turkey for Fenerbahçe after a long stint in the Premier League and Spain. At 32 he's the elder option on the right, all pace and tackling, the seasoned head behind the younger full-backs.

players.name: Renato Veiga
players.note: At 22 he's the squad's Swiss army knife in defence, a natural centre-back who can just as easily play left-back or sit in midfield, which is exactly why Villarreal made him a club-record signing. Wherever there's a gap, he's the one who fills it.

players.name: Samú Costa
players.note: Listed here as a defender but really a holding midfielder by trade, the Mallorca man is the squad's under-the-radar pick, the kind of name casual fans won't know yet. He does the unglamorous shielding-the-back-four work that lets the stars in front of him shine.

players.name: Bruno Fernandes
players.note: Manchester United's captain and Portugal's midfield engine, the man who takes the free-kicks, the penalties and the responsibility, then runs himself into the ground for ninety minutes. If you want one player to make something happen, he's usually the answer.

players.name: João Neves
players.note: At 21 he's already a Champions League winner with PSG and the youngest Portuguese player to reach a milestone in that competition that even Ronaldo hit later, then he went and scored two bicycle kicks in one game for good measure. Tiny, tireless and absurdly composed for his age.

players.name: Rúben Neves
players.note: A deep midfielder famous for spraying long, raking passes across the pitch, now plying his trade at Al-Hilal in Saudi Arabia. He sits in front of the defence and acts as the launch pad, the man who turns defence into attack with one swing of his right boot.

players.name: Matheus Nunes
