players.note: A powerful, ground-covering midfielder at Manchester City who's increasingly been used at right-back, proof that managers will find a way to get a good athlete on the pitch. Strong on the ball and hard to knock off it, he gives Portugal a useful different option in the middle.

players.name: Bernardo Silva
players.note: Manchester City's captain and one of the most two-footed, do-everything midfielders around, equally happy creating chances, tracking back, or filling in wherever the team needs a body. Endlessly clever and impossible to dispossess, the glue in Portugal's midfield.

players.name: Vitinha
players.note: The metronome at the heart of PSG's treble-winning side and a Ballon d'Or runner-up, he completes more passes than just about anyone and sets the tempo of every game he plays. Portugal build around him; give him the ball and the whole team starts to tick.

players.name: Francisco Conceição
players.note: A direct, dribbling winger at Juventus and the son of a former Portugal international, so the wing-play runs in the family. He's the kind of player who comes off the bench to beat his man and conjure something, all quick feet and fearless one-on-ones.

players.name: Gonçalo Guedes
players.note: A forward back in Spain with Real Sociedad after a spell in England, chipping in with a tidy run of league goals this season. He can play out wide or through the middle, a left-footed finisher with a knack for the spectacular when the mood takes him.

players.name: João Félix
players.note: Once hailed as Portugal's next great hope after a teenage breakout, the gifted forward has since bounced between big clubs and now lines up alongside Ronaldo at Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia. Still capable of moments only a few players can produce, with the touch to unlock a tight game.

players.name: Rafael Leão
players.note: AC Milan's powerhouse left winger, all raw pace and shoulders, the kind of player who can drift through a game and then win it in a single burst down the flank. When he gets running at a defender from wide, full-backs start checking the time until it's over.

players.name: Pedro Neto
players.note: A quick, generous winger at Chelsea who picked up a Club World Cup winner's medal in his first season there and bagged his first senior hat-trick along the way. As likely to tee up a teammate as score himself, the unselfish kind of attacker every coach wants.

players.name: Gonçalo Ramos
players.note: The PSG striker who announced himself to the world by scoring a hat-trick on his first World Cup start in 2022, the day Ronaldo was left on the bench. A natural number nine with a poacher's instinct, he's Portugal's option to lead the line when they want a proper centre-forward.

players.name: Cristiano Ronaldo
players.note: At 40 and still the captain, he's heading to a record sixth World Cup, chasing the one big trophy that has always eluded him with Portugal. Whatever you make of the noise around him, he's the most prolific international goalscorer the game has ever seen, and he's not done yet.

players.name: Trincão
players.note: A creative winger at Sporting who has rediscovered his best form back in Portugal, racking up goals and assists in a busy season across every competition. He drifts inside off the right to thread passes, the kind of player who makes the final ball look easy.

players.name: Mahmud Abunada
players.note: The 25-year-old Al-Rayyan keeper wears the number one shirt and has played his way into Lopetegui's good books, with recent friendly displays nudging him ahead in the battle to start. Born in Qatar to a Palestinian family, he was the country's best domestic goalkeeper last season.

players.name: Meshaal Barsham
players.note: The Al Sadd goalkeeper, 27, was long seen as Qatar's established number one and is the most experienced of the three keepers here. Sudan-born and a commanding presence in the box, he is now in a real fight with Abunada for the starting job.

players.name: Salah Zakaria
players.note: The 26-year-old is Al-Duhail's regular keeper at club level but sits third in the national-team pecking order, so he is most likely here to train and cover. Egypt-born and unusually tall for a Qatar goalkeeper, he has only a handful of caps to his name.

players.name: Homam Ahmed
players.note: A 26-year-old left-back who is the one Qatar player getting his football in Europe, spending this season on loan in Spain's second tier to test himself in a tougher league. He gives Lopetegui a genuine option down the left flank.

players.name: Sultan Al Braik
players.note: A 29-year-old full-back who was part of the squad that won the 2023 Asian Cup, so he knows how to deliver on a big stage. Reliable and steady rather than flashy, he gives Qatar dependable cover out wide.

players.name: A. Al Hussain
players.note: At 22, this Al-Arabi defender is one of the youngest in the squad and very much here for the experience rather than to start. Expect him to be learning from the veterans in front of him.

players.name: A. Al Oui
players.note: At 20, the Al-Gharafa defender is the youngest outfield player Qatar brought, a squad-depth pick handed an early taste of a World Cup. He is here to develop, not to be thrown straight into the back line.

players.name: Jassem Gaber
players.note: A 23-year-old who can play centre-back or sit in front of the defence, and who already has a knack for big moments: he scored the equaliser in Qatar's 2023 Asian Cup semi-final against Iran. Versatile and still rising, he is a useful option for Lopetegui.

players.name: Boualem Khoukhi
players.note: The 35-year-old Al Sadd man is the leader of Qatar's defence, with well over 100 caps and the rare habit of scoring goals for a centre-back, around 19 for his country. It was his header that helped secure the win over the UAE that booked this World Cup ticket.

players.name: Lucas Mendes
players.note: Brazilian-born and a former Marseille player, this 35-year-old defender switched to Qatar after years living there and was part of the 2023 Asian Cup-winning squad. He can fill in at left-back or centre-back and brings a lot of senior experience to the group.

players.name: G. Laye
players.note: A 27-year-old Al-Arabi defender and one of the naturalised players in Lopetegui's group, brought in for squad depth at the back. Little senior international football to his name, so he is more likely to feature off the bench than start.

players.name: Pedro Miguel
players.note: Known as Ro-Ro, this 35-year-old was born in Portugal and naturalised to play for Qatar, where he has won two Asian Cups and featured at the 2022 World Cup. A right-sided defender who can also play centre-back, he is one of the most decorated veterans in the squad.

players.name: Assim Madibo
players.note: Qatar's midfield enforcer, a 29-year-old whose job is to break up play and protect the back four so the creative players can get on with things. A regular through the Asian Cup wins, he is one of the names Lopetegui leans on in the engine room.

players.name: Ahmed Al Ganehi
players.note: A 25-year-old from Al-Gharafa who operates as a right-sided midfielder or winger, offering energy and width when called upon. He is more of a rotation option here than a guaranteed starter.

players.name: Abdulaziz Hatem
players.note: A 35-year-old Al-Rayyan midfielder and a veteran of Qatar's golden generation, having featured in both the 2019 and 2023 Asian Cup-winning runs. His experience and game-management are why he is still around at this World Cup.

players.name: Karim Boudiaf
players.note: A 35-year-old Al-Duhail midfielder who played at the 2022 World Cup on home soil, including the group game against Senegal. A long-serving holding option, he brings calm and know-how to the middle of the park.

players.name: Ahmed Fathi
players.note: Egypt-born and raised in Qatar from childhood, this 32-year-old is the kind of midfielder who does the unglamorous work, winning more tackles than any other Qatar player during qualifying. He sits at the base of the midfield and was part of both Asian Cup wins.

players.name: Hassan Al Haydos
players.note: Qatar's captain and record cap-holder, with well over 180 appearances to his name, who joined Al Sadd as a boy and never really left. At 35 he leads the side at his first qualified World Cup, having previously played as host in 2022.

players.name: Mohamed Al Manai
players.note: At 22, this Al Shamal forward is one of the squad's least-tested attackers and is here largely for the experience. Expect him on the fringes rather than leading the line.

players.name: Y. Abdurisag
players.note: A 26-year-old winger, born in Somalia, who is on loan at Al Wakrah and offers pace and directness off the flank. He is a squad attacking option, more likely to be used as an impact substitute than a nailed-on starter.

players.name: Akram Afif
players.note: Qatar's best player and a two-time Asian Footballer of the Year, this 29-year-old left winger top-scored at the 2023 Asian Cup and famously buried a hat-trick of penalties in the final. He also racked up more assists than anyone else across Asian qualifying, so if Qatar create anything dangerous, it usually runs through him.

players.name: Ahmed Alaa
players.note: Egypt-born and a one-club man with Al-Rayyan since he was a teenager, this 32-year-old attacker has been part of the Qatar setup for years. A rotation forward at this point in his career, he offers Lopetegui a familiar option off the bench.

players.name: Almoez Ali
players.note: Qatar's all-time leading scorer and the man who set a single-tournament Asian Cup record with nine goals back in 2019. The 29-year-old Al-Duhail captain led the line in qualifying as Asia's top scorer, and he is the obvious focal point for Qatar's attack at this World Cup.

players.name: Edmilson Junior
players.note: Born in Liege, Belgium, this 31-year-old winger became a Qatar regular at club level with Al-Duhail before naturalising and breaking into the national team. He brings direct one-on-one running and an eye for goal, a handy attacking weapon alongside Afif and Almoez.

players.name: Tahsin Jamshid
players.note: At 19 the baby of the squad, a quick, tricky winger who came through Qatar's Aspire Academy and is the first player of Indian origin, with family roots in Kerala, to make a World Cup squad. Whether he plays much or not, his selection is already a story, and he is one to keep an eye on for the future.

players.name: Mohammed Muntari
players.note: Ghana-born and naturalised, this 32-year-old striker holds a slice of history as the man who scored Qatar's first and so far only World Cup goal, against Senegal in 2022. Now an Al-Gharafa forward and a backup here, he would dearly love a second to call his own.

players.name: Nawaf Al Aqidi
players.note: The Al-Nassr keeper goes into the tournament as Saudi Arabia's first choice between the posts, having edged ahead of more experienced rivals during qualifying. At 25 he is young for the role and this is his chance to make the No. 1 shirt his own.

players.name: Ahmed Al Kassar
players.note: A 34-year-old keeper at Al-Qadisiyah, Al Kassar is here as a backup option rather than a starter, with only a handful of senior caps to his name. He once made the rare list of Saudi league goalkeepers credited with an assist, a quirky footnote to a long domestic career.

players.name: Mohammed Al Owais
players.note: If the name rings a bell, it should: this is the keeper whose heroics helped Saudi Arabia stun Argentina at the 2022 World Cup. Now 34 and playing his football in the second tier, he is the experienced head among the goalkeepers rather than the certain starter.

players.name: Saud Abdulhamid
players.note: The right-back is the only member of the squad playing his club football in Europe, on loan at Ligue 1's Lens after a spell in Italy with Roma. An attacking full-back who chips in with goals and assists, he is one of the team's most important defenders and a near-certain starter.

players.name: Mohammed Abu Al Shamat
players.note: A 23-year-old right-back at Al-Qadisiyah who came up through the youth ranks there, he has grown into a regular for his club and racked up a healthy pile of assists from the flank. He is one of the squad's younger defenders, more likely to provide cover than to start.

players.name: Nawaf Boushal
players.note: A right-back at Al-Nassr known for his energy getting up and down the flank, Boushal offers cover at full-back in this squad. He was a promising youngster a few years back and now provides squad depth alongside the more established defenders.

players.name: Abdulelah Al Amri
players.note: A centre-back at Al-Nassr and a regular through the World Cup qualifying campaign, the 28-year-old is one of the senior defensive options Saudi Arabia will lean on. He even chips in with the odd goal from set pieces, unusual for a player whose main job is at the back.

players.name: Moteb Al Harbi
players.note: A left-back at Al-Hilal who joined the Saudi champions in 2024, the 25-year-old offers cover down the left flank and contributes the occasional goal and assist. He is part of the squad's defensive depth rather than a guaranteed starter.

players.name: Hassan Kadesh
players.note: An experienced 33-year-old centre-back at Al-Ittihad, Kadesh has been around the Saudi game for well over a decade and once captained the country's youth sides. His leadership and know-how make him a useful presence in the squad's defensive ranks.

players.name: Ali Lajami
players.note: A versatile defender who joined Al-Hilal on a free transfer after five years at rivals Al-Nassr, Lajami gives the squad a dependable option at the back. He has a twin brother, Qassem, who is also a defender in the Saudi league, a neat family footnote.

players.name: Ali Majrashi
players.note: A right-back at Al-Ahli, Majrashi was one of the standout defenders in the club's run to Asian club glory, winning duels and putting in tackles by the bucketload. That form earned him national-team recognition and a place among Saudi Arabia's full-back options.

players.name: Hassan Tambakti
players.note: The Al-Hilal centre-back is the rock at the heart of Saudi Arabia's defence, a near-ever-present through qualifying who logged big minutes in the toughest matches. At 26 he is in his prime and one of the first names on the team sheet at the back.

players.name: J. Thakri
players.note: A 24-year-old centre-back who came through the academy at Al-Qadisiyah, Jehad Thakri has only a handful of senior caps and is here largely to add depth in central defence. The World Cup is a step up in class and a learning experience for him.

players.name: Nasser Al Dawsari
players.note: A 27-year-old midfielder at Al-Hilal, he holds a curious record: the fastest goal in AFC Champions League history, struck just 16 seconds into a final. A box-to-box presence, he offers Saudi Arabia useful legs and steel in the centre of the pitch.

players.name: Mohamed Kanno
players.note: A long-serving midfield anchor at Al-Hilal where he has collected a cabinet's worth of trophies, Kanno is one of the most capped and experienced players in the squad. He shields the defence and breaks up play, the kind of unglamorous job a good team needs done well.

players.name: Ziyad Al Johani
players.note: A defensive midfielder at Al-Ahli who featured in the club's Asian-title-winning campaign, including the final, the 24-year-old is a tidy ball-winner in the middle. He offers Saudi Arabia rotation and cover in central midfield.

players.name: Musab Al Juwayr
players.note: At 22 the playmaker is the one to watch, voted Saudi Arabia's player of the season at Al-Qadisiyah after a campaign of double-figure assists and goals. He carries much of the team's creative hope at this tournament, the rare young Saudi talent who makes things happen.

players.name: Abdullah Al Khaibari
players.note: A defensive midfielder at Al-Nassr valued for his reading of the game and his interceptions, Al Khaibari saw his minutes grow during the World Cup qualifiers as Saudi Arabia booked their place. He is a sensible, defensively minded option in the engine room.

players.name: Ala Al Haji
players.note: A 29-year-old central midfielder at newly promoted Neom SC, Al Haji is one of the less heralded names in the squad and offers depth rather than a starting spot. After a career across several Saudi clubs, this call-up is a deserved reward for his consistency.

players.name: Khalid Al Ghannam
players.note: The Al-Ettifaq winger arrives in form, finishing the league season as the top-scoring Saudi player with double figures in goals. Quick and direct, he gives the attack a genuine threat from wide and is one of the team's brighter creative sparks.

players.name: Sultan Mandash
players.note: A winger whose strong form earned him a January move to Al-Hilal, Mandash has carried that confidence into the national team, scoring in a pre-tournament friendly. At 31 he is a late bloomer enjoying the best spell of his career at just the right time.

players.name: Ayman Yahya
players.note: A small, quick winger at Al-Nassr who can also fill in at full-back, Yahya was the standout player when Saudi Arabia's under-23s won the Asian title a few years ago. He gives the squad pace and versatility off the bench or out wide.

players.name: Feras Al Brikan
players.note: The Al-Ahli striker leads the line for Saudi Arabia and arrives off the back of a memorable moment: the extra-time winner that retained his club's Asian crown. Tall and capable of dropping into wide areas, he is the team's main reference point up front.

players.name: Abdullah Al Hamdan
players.note: A striker who has won a stack of titles in the Saudi league, Al Hamdan offers a proven alternative or partner to the first-choice forward. He found the net for the national team in pre-tournament friendlies, useful timing ahead of the World Cup.

players.name: Saleh Al Shehri
players.note: A 32-year-old striker at Al-Ittihad with a long international scoring record, Al Shehri remains a reliable finisher for the national team, recently converting from the spot at the Gold Cup. Experienced and cool in front of goal, he is a valuable option up top.

players.name: Salem Al Dawsari
players.note: The captain, talisman and the man who scored the winner against Argentina in 2022, Al Dawsari is the heartbeat of this team at his third World Cup. At 34 he is the most-capped player in the squad and a two-time Asian Player of the Year, the left winger everyone else plays around.

players.name: C. Gordon
players.note: At 43 he's the grand old man of this whole tournament, on course to be one of the oldest players ever to feature at a World Cup. Still Hearts' first-choice keeper and still standing after a career-threatening broken leg a few years back, which tells you how stubborn he is about hanging up the gloves.

players.name: A. Gunn
players.note: Handed the No 1 shirt, which is a strong hint he's the one Steve Clarke trusts between the posts. He's the son of former Norwich keeper Bryan Gunn, so minding goals is very much the family business.

players.name: L. Kelly
players.note: The third keeper in the pecking order, with only a couple of caps to his name, so this is a watching-and-learning kind of trip. He earned the call on the back of plenty of steady games for Rangers.

players.name: G. Hanley
players.note: A 34-year-old centre-back who has fought through injuries and a suspension just to prove he's fit enough to make the plane. The kind of old-school, no-nonsense defender a squad keeps around for the dressing room as much as the pitch.

players.name: J. Hendry
players.note: A centre-back who has taken the well-trodden route to the Saudi league, where he played a full season's worth of games and stayed match-sharp. Comfortable on the ball, he's the type who likes to step out of defence and start something.

players.name: A. Hickey
players.note: At 23 he's already racked up close to twenty caps, even though injuries and bit-part minutes at Brentford have stalled his club season. A modern full-back who can play either flank, he's in a straight fight with Patterson for the right-back slot.

players.name: D. Hyam
players.note: A dependable centre-back who built his name at Coventry before signing on with Wrexham, the club Hollywood made famous. He's exactly the sort of unflashy, gets-the-job-done defender Clarke likes having in reserve.

players.name: S. McKenna
players.note: A centre-back who reinvented himself in Croatia, enjoying a fine season as Dinamo Zagreb went chasing the title. With nearly fifty caps behind him he's one of the more seasoned heads in the back line.

players.name: N. Patterson
players.note: A flying right-back whose Everton season has been mostly spent waiting for chances, yet he stays a key man for the national side. Quick and keen to overlap, he's young enough that the best version of him may still be coming.

players.name: A. Ralston
players.note: A Celtic full-back who has quietly collected a cabinet's worth of Scottish league titles without ever being the headline act. The handy, do-as-he's-told utility man every winning squad needs.

players.name: A. Robertson
players.note: The captain and Scotland's most-capped man in this squad, now within touching distance of the all-time record set by Kenny Dalglish. A Champions League and Premier League winner with Liverpool who famously went from being released as a teenager to one of the best left-backs in the world, so leading his country at a first World Cup in nearly thirty years is a fitting reward.

players.name: J. Souttar
players.note: A tall Rangers centre-back who debuted in Scottish football at just sixteen and has spent years since fighting off a string of nasty injuries. Left out of the last Euros, so this call-up is something of a comeback story for him.

players.name: K. Tierney
players.note: A left-back who couldn't nail down a regular spot at Arsenal and chose to go home to Celtic, where he's thriving again. He scored the dramatic 93rd-minute goal that put Scotland back in front against Denmark on the night they sealed qualification, so the homecoming gamble has paid off handsomely.

players.name: R. Christie
players.note: An Inverness-born midfielder who has become a reliable Premier League operator at Bournemouth and is heading to his third major tournament with Scotland. Versatile enough to play anywhere across the middle, he does a lot of the running others don't notice.

players.name: L. Ferguson
players.note: The captain at Bologna, where he played a packed season and helped them reach the latter stages in Europe, which says plenty about how an Italian club rates him. A box-to-box midfielder who comes from proper football stock as the nephew of former Rangers man Barry Ferguson.

players.name: T. Fletcher
players.note: An 18-year-old midfielder and son of the former United and Scotland captain Darren Fletcher, drafted in late as cover after Billy Gilmour got injured. His twin brother Jack opted to play for England, so the family is neatly split across the border.

players.name: J.  McGinn
players.note: The Aston Villa skipper and one of Scotland's surest sources of a goal from midfield, with around twenty to his name in over eighty caps. Nicknamed the Meatball by team-mates, he brings the energy and end-product that ties this side together.

players.name: K. McLean
players.note: The Norwich captain who put the bow on Scotland's qualification with a jaw-dropping lob from the halfway line against Denmark, spotting the keeper off his line and going for it. Proof that the unglamorous, hard-running midfielders get their moment too.

players.name: S. McTominay
players.note: The squad's standout name, fresh off being voted the best player in Serie A after leaving Manchester United and inspiring Napoli to the Italian title in his first season. He opened the scoring against Denmark with a stunning overhead kick on the night Scotland booked their place, so he arrives as a genuine star turn.

players.name: C. Adams
players.note: A striker plying his trade in Serie A with Torino, English-born but committed to Scotland through his family roots. A reliable scorer at international level, he leads the line with hard running as much as with goals.

players.name: L. Dykes
players.note: A big, awkward target man who was actually born and raised in Australia before choosing Scotland through his heritage. Not the flashiest finisher, but the kind of bustling number nine who occupies defenders and brings others into the game.

players.name: B. Doak
players.note: A direct, fearless winger who once became the youngest Scot ever to play for Liverpool before moving on for regular football. At 20 he's the bright spark of the attack, the player likely to run straight at full-backs and make something happen.

players.name: G. Hirst
players.note: A late convert who only switched his international allegiance to Scotland in 2025, qualifying through his family despite being English-born. The son of former Sheffield Wednesday striker David Hirst, he's a forward still making up for lost time in the dark blue.

players.name: L. Shankland
players.note: The Hearts captain and a prolific goalscorer at home, who fired in around twenty goals last season and very nearly dragged his club to a title. A proper poacher whose club form is hard to ignore, even if the international starting spot is hotly contested.

players.name: R. Stewart
players.note: Nicknamed the Loch Ness Drogba in his Sunderland days, this big striker is back in the squad after four years lost largely to injury. He rebuilt his career with a double-figure goal haul for Southampton, making his recall one of the feel-good stories of the selection.

players.name: Findlay Curtis
players.note: The squad's surprise inclusion, a 19-year-old winger who came through the Rangers academy from the age of six and spent the back half of the season on loan getting minutes. He'd only earned his first cap a few months earlier, so this is a whirlwind rise to a World Cup.

players.name: M. Diaw
players.note: A towering keeper, French-born and standing close to two metres, who became Le Havre's first-choice between the posts after arriving in 2025. Here he is back-up cover behind Mendy, the kind of experienced hand you want on the bench rather than starting.

players.name: Y. Diouf
players.note: Paris-born and only recently cleared by FIFA to play for Senegal, he was one of Ligue 1's standout keepers at Reims before joining Nice in 2025 as their new number one. With Mendy ahead of him for Senegal, he is the understudy gaining big-stage experience.

players.name: É. Mendy
players.note: Senegal's first-choice keeper and a former Champions League winner with Chelsea, he now captains Al-Ahli in Saudi Arabia and has lifted back-to-back Asian club titles there. Calm, commanding and a leader as much as a shot-stopper, he is the safe pair of hands behind this defence.

players.name: E. Diouf
players.note: A marauding left-back who earned a big move to West Ham in 2025 after a title-winning spell at Slavia Prague, and has since become one of the Hammers' most creative outlets from defence. At 21 he is one to watch on Senegal's left flank, comfortable getting forward and crossing.

players.name: I. Jakobs
players.note: German-born left-back who has settled into a key role at Turkish champions Galatasaray, where he is trusted to handle the toughest European nights. He provided an assist on Senegal's run to the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title and competes for the left-back slot here.

players.name: K. Koulibaly
players.note: The captain and emotional anchor of this team, a centre-back who built his reputation at Napoli and now plays for Al-Hilal in Saudi Arabia. At 34 he has lifted two Africa Cup of Nations titles with Senegal; his reading of the game and leadership matter as much as his tackling.

players.name: A. Mendy
players.note: A 21-year-old defender who came through the Nice academy and can play right-back or centre-back, prized for his aerial strength and composure on the ball. New to the senior squad with only a handful of caps, he is squad depth here, getting his tournament education early.

players.name: M. Niakhaté
players.note: A tall, left-footed centre-back who moved from Nottingham Forest to Lyon for a club-record fee and has since become a dependable fixture and vice-captain there. He partnered the back line on the way to the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations and is a strong contender to start alongside Koulibaly.

players.name: M. Sarr
players.note: A 20-year-old centre-back whose rise has been dizzying: he played the full 120 minutes of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations final, deputising for the injured and suspended Koulibaly, and won the trophy. He spent the season on loan at Strasbourg and is a genuine option in the heart of defence.

players.name: A. Seck
players.note: An experienced centre-back, now 33, who has been a steady presence for Maccabi Haifa in Israel and chipped in with the odd goal from set pieces. A 2025 Africa Cup of Nations winner, he offers reliable depth and a calm head behind the first-choice pairing.

players.name: K. Diatta
players.note: A natural attacker who reinvented himself as a tireless right wing-back, thriving in that role at Monaco and named their player of the month earlier in the season. That flexibility makes him a useful starter or rotation option, equally happy bombing forward or tucking in to defend.

players.name: L. Camara
players.note: A box-to-box midfielder still only 21 yet already an Africa Cup of Nations winner, having broken through at Metz before becoming a regular at Monaco. He chips in with goals and assists and has attracted big-club interest; expect him to be a key engine in Senegal's midfield.

players.name: P. Ciss
players.note: A versatile midfielder for Spain's Rayo Vallecano who can also fill in at centre-back, and a 2025 Africa Cup of Nations winner. He started as a depth option there before forcing his way into the side, which is exactly the kind of dependable utility man a tournament squad needs.

players.name: H. Diarra
players.note: An energetic 21-year-old midfielder who became Sunderland's record signing in 2025 after impressing at Strasbourg, where he chipped in with goals, assists and plenty of chances created. One of the brightest young talents in this squad and a likely starter in the middle of the park.

players.name: I. Gueye
players.note: At 36 the elder statesman of the midfield, a relentless ball-winner who keeps racking up tackles for Everton and was their player of the season not long ago. A hugely experienced figure who lifted the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations; his know-how is invaluable in the deep-lying role.

players.name: P. Gueye
players.note: A defensive midfielder who has quietly become one of La Liga's best, voted the division's top African player for the 2025-26 season after anchoring Villarreal's midfield. He shields the back four and dictates tempo, and is pushing hard for a starting spot alongside the veteran Gueye.

players.name: Bara Ndiaye
players.note: At 18 the youngest outfield player here, a midfielder whose journey from Senegal's regional football to Bayern Munich in barely a few months reads like a fairy tale; he made his Bundesliga debut in 2026 coming on for Jamal Musiala. He is in this squad to learn, not to start.

players.name: P. Sarr
players.note: A composed central midfielder who has grown into a trusted regular at Tottenham and helped them win the 2025 Europa League. A World Cup veteran from 2022 and a 2025 Africa Cup of Nations winner, the 23-year-old offers a smart mix of energy and passing in the middle.

players.name: Assane Diao
players.note: A quick, direct right winger who chose to represent Senegal over Spain, where he came through Real Betis's academy before moving to Como in Serie A. At 20 he is one of the squad's exciting young wide players, offering pace and unpredictability off the bench.

players.name: B. Dieng
players.note: A striker who revived his career with a prolific run for Lorient, scoring a flurry of Ligue 1 goals to earn a recall after time away from the national team. The former Marseille forward is back-up firepower up top, the kind of poacher who can change a game from the bench.

players.name: N. Jackson
players.note: A powerful, mobile centre-forward who joined Bayern Munich on loan from Chelsea and helped them to the Bundesliga title in his first season. At 24 he is Senegal's leading striker option, with the pace and physicality to lead the line and stretch defences.

players.name: S. Mané
players.note: Senegal's talisman and the Guardian's pick as the team's star man, a former Liverpool great who now plays alongside Cristiano Ronaldo at Al-Nassr. At 33 he was named best player of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations; whether starting or impacting late, he is the player opponents fear most.

players.name: I. Mbaye
players.note: At 17 the baby of the squad, a forward from the PSG academy who became Senegal's youngest-ever scorer when he netted on just his second cap. Picking Senegal over France, he is here for the experience; do not expect many minutes, but the future looks bright.

players.name: C. Ndiaye
players.note: A tall, physical target-man striker who has been scoring steadily for Samsunspor in Turkey, including in Europe. A late bloomer who only debuted for Senegal in his late twenties, he is squad depth up front, the kind of focal point you bring on to hold the ball up and chase a goal.

players.name: I. Ndiaye
players.note: A creative forward who plays wide or off the front for Everton and had a standout 2025-26 with goals and assists. He featured in all of Senegal's 2025 Africa Cup of Nations games, scoring the quarter-final winner; expect him to be a key attacking weapon, whether starting or breaking the deadlock late.

players.name: I. Sarr
players.note: A flying winger who was voted Crystal Palace's player of the season and finished top scorer as they won the 2026 UEFA Conference League. Fast, direct and a regular goal threat, the 27-year-old is one of Senegal's most dangerous attackers and a likely starter out wide.

players.name: S. Chaine
players.note: A goalkeeper who just had the season of his life, keeping 21 clean sheets to set a new South African league record as Orlando Pirates won the title. He's behind captain Williams in the national pecking order, so think of him as a very capable understudy rather than the man between the posts.

players.name: R. Goss
players.note: A 31-year-old keeper who finally found a regular home and became a fan favourite at his Bloemfontein club after years as a squad option. Coach Hugo Broos rates his attitude and work ethic, but here he's third in line and most likely to spend the tournament watching and training.

players.name: R. Williams
players.note: The captain and undisputed number one, a 33-year-old who became a national hero by saving four penalties in a shootout at the 2023 Africa Cup of Nations. He plays for Mamelodi Sundowns, was once ranked among the world's top ten keepers, and is the calm, vocal leader Broos builds the team around.

players.name: B. Cross
players.note: A 24-year-old Kaizer Chiefs left-back and the squad's biggest surprise pick, called up uncapped largely as cover after first-choice Modiba's fitness worries. He spent his teens in the youth setups at Schalke and Newcastle before coming home, and he can fill in across the back line if needed.

players.name: S. Kabini
players.note: A 21-year-old left-back who has built a name for himself in Norway with Molde after moving up through South African football. He'll compete with the more experienced Modiba for minutes on the left, so expect him to feature mainly as backup unless injuries open a door.

players.name: O. Makhanya
players.note: A 21-year-old centre-back who has impressed in Major League Soccer with Philadelphia Union, anchoring one of the meanest defences in the league. Still very new to the senior national side, he's one for the future who could grab a real opportunity if the World Cup goes well.

players.name: M. Mbokazi
players.note: At 20, the youngest player in the squad and one of its brightest stories, a centre-back nicknamed TLB who broke through fearlessly and already won a man-of-the-match award in a Soweto derby. Composed beyond his years, he's pushing hard to start despite his age.

players.name: A. Modiba
players.note: The first-choice left-back, a 30-year-old Sundowns mainstay nicknamed Postman who gets forward constantly and chipped in with goals all season. A late-season hamstring injury briefly threatened his place, but he made the squad and should start once fully fit.

players.name: K. Mudau
players.note: The first-choice right-back, a 30-year-old known as Sailor who has been a fixture in Sundowns' run of league titles and is rated among the best in his position on the continent. Reliable and tireless, he's one of the quiet certainties in the starting eleven.

players.name: K. Ndamane
players.note: A 21-year-old defender who earned his first senior call-up in 2025 and quickly became part of the picture, now on the books at champions Sundowns. He's young squad depth at centre-back here, in the camp to learn from the established names and grab any chance he gets.

players.name: I. Okon
players.note: A 21-year-old centre-back playing in Germany with Hannover 96 who chose South Africa despite his Nigerian heritage and interest from the Super Eagles. Broos clearly trusts him, picking him for the World Cup even after he missed AFCON, so he's genuine competition for a defensive spot.

players.name: N. Sibisi
players.note: The 30-year-old Orlando Pirates captain who led from the back as his club won the league, and a centre-back Broos has publicly backed against his critics. Experienced and composed, he's firmly in the mix to start at the heart of the defence.

players.name: T. Matuludi
players.note: A 26-year-old right-back from Polokwane City who has been a regular face in Broos' squads and quietly drawn interest from the country's biggest clubs. With Mudau ahead of him at right-back, he's most likely backup, but he's dependable cover.

players.name: J. Adams
players.note: A 24-year-old box-to-box midfielder for Sundowns who fought his way back into the national setup after a year in the wilderness, rediscovering his best form in the second half of the season. He gives Broos energy and legs in the middle as a rotation option.

players.name: T. Mbatha
players.note: A 25-year-old defensive midfielder for Orlando Pirates who has a knack for the dramatic, scoring on his international debut and again soon after. He sits in front of the back four breaking up play, and is one of the options to do the unglamorous work in central midfield.

players.name: T. Mokoena
players.note: The Guardian's pick as South Africa's player to watch, and the midfield engine for both Sundowns and the national team at 28. He scored in his club's CAF Champions League final win and brings goals, range of passing and set-piece danger, making him central to how Bafana play.

players.name: S. Sithole
players.note: A 26-year-old central midfielder known as Yaya who plies his trade in Portugal's top flight with Tondela, even through a tough relegation scrap. One of the squad's Europe-based players, he offers experience of week-in, week-out football abroad as a midfield option.

players.name: T. Zwane
players.note: At 36, the elder statesman of the squad and a Sundowns legend whose clever passing has shaped a decade of dominance. He's coming back from a long injury layoff, so Broos has been honest that he may not be ready for 90 minutes, but his guile off the bench could unlock a tight game.

players.name: O. Appollis
players.note: A 24-year-old left winger whose career nearly stalled amid rejections before he turned into one of the most exciting attackers in the country, shining in his first season at Orlando Pirates. Direct and full of tricks, he's a likely starter and a real threat to take defenders on.

players.name: L. Foster
players.note: The main striker, a 25-year-old at Premier League side Burnley who lit up AFCON earlier this year with goals and assists in every match South Africa scored. Strong, quick and good with his back to goal, he carries the team's main hope of finding the net at the World Cup.

players.name: E. Makgopa
players.note: A 25-year-old hard-running Orlando Pirates striker whom Broos has loyally backed even when club minutes dried up. He offers a willing, physical alternative up front, and is the kind of forward Broos likes to bring on to chase a game late.

players.name: T. Maseko
players.note: A 22-year-old winger on loan in Cyprus with AEL Limassol, where a run of regular games restored the confidence and sharpness Broos wants from him. His pace and directness make him a useful impact option off the bench in Group A.

players.name: R. Mofokeng
players.note: At 21, the wonderkid everyone in South African football is talking about, an Orlando Pirates playmaker who racked up goals and assists and was named league player of the month. Wearing the number 10, he's the creative spark Broos hopes can light up the tournament.

players.name: T. Moremi
players.note: A 25-year-old winger who earned a move to Orlando Pirates after standing out at AmaZulu and quickly became one of their key attacking threats. He gives Broos width and another option on the flanks, competing for game time in a crowded forward line.

players.name: I. Rayners
players.note: A 30-year-old Sundowns striker recalled for the World Cup after missing AFCON, with Broos valuing him as a different kind of forward to his other strikers. He had a productive scoring season for his club and gives the attack an extra tactical option.

players.name: K. Sebelebele
players.note: A 23-year-old Orlando Pirates winger who missed out on AFCON but worked his way into the World Cup squad, described as an explosive presence down the right. He's a high-energy option from the bench who can stretch tiring defences late in games.

players.name: Jo Hyeon-Woo
players.note: The Ulsan keeper who became a national hero in 2018 for a string of saves that helped sink Germany, and at 34 he is locked in a genuine fight with Kim Seung-Gyu for the starting gloves here. Quick off his line and brave in one-on-ones, he is the home-based option in a goalkeeping department where neither man is guaranteed.

players.name: Kim Seung-Gyu
players.note: The most-capped goalkeeper in this squad, with more than 80 appearances and a fourth World Cup now in front of him at age 35. He has spent recent years sharpening his footwork in Japan with FC Tokyo, and his case for the number one shirt rests almost entirely on that mountain of big-game experience.

players.name: Song Bum-Keun
players.note: The third goalkeeper, here mostly to train and push the two veterans ahead of him rather than to play. A towering shot-stopper for his club, he was a standout at youth level, named best keeper as South Korea won the 2020 AFC U-23 title, but with only a handful of senior caps he is the long-term project in this group.

players.name: Cho Wi-Je
players.note: A genuine fairytale call-up: in second-tier football at the start of the year, he then earned a move to the domestic champions and impressed enough that a late injury to another defender handed him a World Cup ticket. At 24 he is squad depth at the back rather than a guaranteed starter, but simply being here caps a remarkable twelve months.

players.name: Kim Min-Jae
players.note: The defensive anchor and one of the best centre-backs in the world, a ball-playing stopper who reads danger early and is just as comfortable starting attacks as snuffing them out. His Bayern Munich move made him the most expensive Asian player ever, and after a Serie A title with Napoli and Bundesliga honours in Germany, everything at the back is built around him.

players.name: Kim Moon-Hwan
players.note: An experienced wing-back who was the undisputed right-sided defender at the 2022 World Cup and is back for a second tournament at 30. He earns his place with relentless running up and down the flank, though he is competing with younger legs for the starting role this time around.

players.name: Kim Tae-Hyeon
players.note: A left-footed centre-back plying his trade in Japan, and one of the leading candidates to partner Kim Min-Jae in the heart of defence. At 25 he offers genuine pace and a wide covering range to mop up the space behind the line, exactly the profile this back line needs against quick forwards.

players.name: Lee Han-Beom
players.note: A 23-year-old centre-back who timed his run to the squad perfectly, heading home the winner in the Danish Cup final with Midtjylland just as the World Cup picture was being finalised. Comfortable on the ball and still on the rise in European football, he gives the back line a useful younger option.

players.name: Park Jin-Seop
players.note: A versatile defender who can slot in at centre-back or drop into defensive midfield, which is exactly why he is useful as cover at 30. His tactical flexibility makes him a candidate to step in alongside or in place of Kim Min-Jae, and he is comfortable stepping into midfield to help build play from deep.

players.name: Lee Tae-Seok
players.note: The likely starting left wing-back at just 23, having nailed down the role with a productive season at Austria Vienna that brought goals as well as assists. Pacy and attack-minded down the left, he is one of the younger players the manager is trusting with a regular job in this tournament.

players.name: Seol Young-Woo
players.note: A right wing-back who became the first South Korean to join Red Star Belgrade and immediately helped them to a Serbian league and cup double. A converted winger, he loves to push high and overlap, and he can cover either flank, which makes him a strong bet to start on the right of the back line.

players.name: J. Castrop
players.note: A Düsseldorf-born midfielder who came up through Germany's youth ranks before switching allegiance through his Korean mother, becoming the first foreign-born, mixed-heritage player ever picked for a South Korea World Cup squad. Aggressive and combative in the engine room at Borussia Mönchengladbach, he is a fresh option for the manager at 22.

players.name: Lee Gi-Hyuk
players.note: The bolt-from-the-blue pick of this squad, a 25-year-old from the K League who was the surprise name on the final list. His real value is flexibility: he can play centre-back, in midfield or at full-back, and is prized for his composure in build-up, so think of him as a do-everything reserve rather than a guaranteed starter.

players.name: Bae Jun-Ho
players.note: A 22-year-old attacking midfielder and one to watch, named Stoke City's player of the year in his debut season in English football. A regular starter in the Championship since, he carries the ball with flair from the left or through the middle, even if the goals and assists have not always followed; expect him as a creative option off the bench or in rotation.

players.name: Eom Ji-Sung
players.note: A right-footed winger who tends to operate from the left, plying his trade in the English Championship with Swansea. At 23 he is a wide attacking option rather than a nailed-on starter, offering pace and directness in the wider midfield areas if the manager wants to change the picture.

players.name: Hwang In-Beom
players.note: Normally the metronome at the base of midfield, the man who dictates tempo and breaks up opposition moves, but he arrives under a cloud of fitness after an injury-wrecked season at Feyenoord. If he is right, he is a key starter; if not, his minutes will need careful managing through the group stage.

players.name: Kim Jin-Gyu
players.note: A holding midfielder from the domestic champions whose stock has risen with Hwang In-Beom's fitness in doubt, putting him in line to do the unglamorous running in front of the defence. His job is to cover ground and ease the physical load on those around him, a useful insurance policy in the middle of the park.

players.name: Lee Dong-Gyeong
players.note: A left-footed attacking midfielder coming off a standout K League campaign, when he racked up double figures in both goals and assists on his way to the league's MVP award. That form earned him his spot, and he gives the manager a creative, goal-threatening option from the middle or the left.

players.name: Lee Jae-Sung
players.note: One of the squad's wise heads at 33, an attacking midfielder who has become a fan favourite over several seasons in the Bundesliga with Mainz for his clever, intelligent play. He has drifted in and out of the starting line-up for his country lately, but his tournament savvy and tactical brain make him a valuable presence whether he starts or comes on.

players.name: Lee Kang-In
players.note: The squad's in-form creator, fresh from winning back-to-back Champions League titles with Paris Saint-Germain and becoming the first Asian player to lift the trophy twice. A wonderfully gifted attacking midfielder who picks locks with his passing and dribbling, he is the man expected to supply the chances behind the front line.

players.name: Paik Seung-Ho
players.note: A central midfielder tipped to partner the deeper holder in the engine room, bringing tempo control and tidy distribution. He was central to Birmingham City's rise, earning a place in the League One team of the year as they stormed to the title, and then holding his own back in the Championship; a likely starter who keeps things ticking.

players.name: Yang Hyun-Jun
players.note: A 23-year-old winger who turned a Celtic bit-part role into a regular starting spot, chipping in seven league goals as the club swept the Scottish honours. Direct and quick down the flank, he gives the manager extra width and energy in attack as a rotation option rather than a certain starter.

players.name: Hwang Hee-Chan
players.note: Listed as a midfielder but really a forward, a powerful runner who hurts teams in behind with his pace and direct dribbling. His Wolves side endured a grim relegation from the Premier League, but his quality on the counter makes him an important attacking weapon, especially with Son alongside him.

players.name: Cho Gue-Sung
players.note: The big target striker who became a household name with a two-goal cameo against Ghana at the 2022 World Cup, and his selection here caps a comeback from a long-term knee problem that once threatened his career. A natural central finisher with real physical presence, he gives the side a different look as a backup to the first-choice number nine.

players.name: Oh Hyeon-Gyu
players.note: A 24-year-old striker who finally landed the number 18 shirt he had long coveted, and arrives in good scoring form after a productive run of league goals. Mobile and willing to run the channels, he is one of the younger forwards competing for minutes off the bench behind the established names.

players.name: Son Heung-Min
players.note: The captain, the talisman and the whole project's emotional centre, playing in his fourth World Cup at 33 after a glittering decade in the Premier League. Now with LAFC, he has reinvented himself as much a creator as a finisher, and South Korea's hopes of escaping the group lean heavily on his left foot and big-game nerve.

players.name: Joan García
players.note: Barcelona paid his release clause from neighbours Espanyol in 2025, and he repaid them by walking straight into the team and helping win the league. The kind of summer signing that makes the move look obvious in hindsight.

players.name: David Raya
players.note: Arsenal's number one, prized less for spectacular saves than for being calm with the ball at his feet, which is exactly how Spain like their keepers to play. Here he is one of three good ones competing for the gloves.

players.name: Unai Simón
players.note: Spain's go-to keeper through their Euro 2024 win, the steady hand behind a young squad. A one-club man at Athletic Club, where he has spent his whole career in the Basque country.

players.name: Pau Cubarsí Paredes
players.note: An 18-year-old centre-back who already looks unbothered playing for Barcelona, reading the game like someone twice his age. His coach Hansi Flick calls him the defensive answer to Lamine Yamal, which tells you the hype is real.

players.name: Marc Cucurella
players.note: The Chelsea left-back with the unmistakable curly mop, who set up Spain's winner in the Euro 2024 final. Tireless up and down the flank, and impossible to miss in a crowd.

players.name: Eric García
players.note: A Barcelona academy defender comfortable wherever the team needs him, from centre-back to full-back. The sort of reliable utility player every tournament squad quietly depends on.

players.name: Álex Grimaldo
players.note: A left-back who is really an attacker in disguise, with a free-kick and a cross good enough to rack up goals and assists in Germany. Spent years at Benfica before reinventing himself at Bayer Leverkusen.

players.name: Aymeric Laporte
players.note: The senior centre-back who organises Spain's defence, born in France but capped by the country he chose. Now back home at Athletic Club, the team he came through as a teenager.

players.name: Marcos Llorente
players.note: Atletico's Swiss-army-knife, equally happy at right-back, in midfield or charging forward, which is exactly why Simeone never lets him go. After missing Euro 2024, this is his long-awaited shot at a World Cup.

players.name: Pedro Porro
players.note: Tottenham's attacking right-back, more interested in whipping in crosses than sitting back defending. Pace and a delivery that makes him dangerous the moment he gets forward.

players.name: Marc Pubill
players.note: A right-back who earned his big move to Atletico after impressing at smaller Almeria, and now finds himself on a World Cup squad. An Olympic gold medallist with Spain in Paris, so he knows what a tournament high feels like.

players.name: Gavi
players.note: The Barcelona midfielder who plays every minute like a tackle is owed to him, all snarl and energy. His place here is a feel-good story after a long climb back from a serious knee injury.

players.name: Mikel Merino
players.note: A tall, two-footed midfielder at Arsenal who is surprisingly handy in the air at both ends, and has even filled in up front in a pinch. The kind of player a manager loves because he can do a bit of everything.

players.name: Pedri
players.note: The midfielder who runs the tempo for both Barcelona and Spain, gliding past challenges and rarely giving the ball away. Still only 23, yet he plays with the calm of someone who has seen it all.

players.name: Rodri
players.note: The captain and 2024 Ballon d'Or winner, the metronome who sits in front of the defence and makes everything tick. He lost most of last season to a knee injury, so a World Cup back at full strength is a story in itself.

players.name: Fabián Ruiz
players.note: A languid, left-footed midfielder at Paris Saint-Germain who makes the hard things look effortless. Easy to overlook next to the bigger names, but Spain rarely play well without him.

players.name: Martín Zubimendi
players.note: The holding midfielder Arsenal paid big money for in 2025, having once turned down a move to Liverpool to stay loyal to his hometown Real Sociedad. He does the unglamorous shielding work that lets the flair players sparkle.

players.name: Álex Baena
players.note: A creative left-footer who racked up more assists than anyone else in Spain before Atletico signed him in 2025. The man you want on the ball when a defence needs unpicking.

players.name: Dani Olmo
players.note: A clever forward who drifts between the lines, learning his trade in Croatia at Dinamo Zagreb before coming home to Barcelona. A regular scorer in Spain's biggest moments, including at Euro 2024.

players.name: Borja Iglesias
players.note: A proper penalty-box striker nicknamed Panda, back in the squad at 32 after rediscovering his scoring touch at Celta Vigo. The elder statesman among Spain's forwards and a feel-good recall.

players.name: Lamine Yamal
players.note: The 18-year-old Barcelona winger already treated as a global star, who curled in a jaw-dropping goal against France on Spain's way to the Euro 2024 title. Give him the right boot and a sliver of space and he can decide a match on his own.

players.name: Víctor Muñoz
players.note: A 22-year-old who scored on his Spain debut against Serbia, despite never being picked at any youth level first. A breakout season at Osasuna turned him from unknown into World Cup squad member in a matter of months.

players.name: Mikel Oyarzabal
players.note: The Real Sociedad forward who came off the bench to score Spain's winner against England in the Euro 2024 final, the night he became a national hero. Hard-working and dependable rather than flashy, exactly the man you want with the game on the line.

players.name: Yeremy Pino
players.note: A direct, two-footed winger who won the Europa League as a teenager at Villarreal before moving to Crystal Palace in 2025. Quick and fearless, the type to take on a full-back the moment he gets the ball.

players.name: Ferran Torres
players.note: A Barcelona forward who can play across the front line and has quietly become one of Spain's most reliable finishers. Often the man who pops up with a goal when the famous names are being marked out of the game.

players.name: Nico Williams
players.note: A blistering Athletic Club winger who shone at Euro 2024, and stayed loyal to his Basque club despite plenty of bigger offers. Brother of Ghana striker Inaki, and a one-on-one nightmare for any defender.

players.name: V. Johansson
players.note: A goalkeeper who was Stoke City's near ever-present in the Championship until he dislocated his shoulder in late December, and was statistically among the division's best shot-stoppers before the injury. He is one of three keepers Potter brought, all jostling for a starting role that isn't nailed down.

players.name: K. Nordfeldt
players.note: At 36, the elder statesman of the squad and the most experienced keeper here, now back home with AIK in the Swedish top flight. After years on the international fringes he started both nervy playoff matches that sent Sweden to the World Cup, so don't be surprised to see him between the posts.

players.name: J. Widell Zetterström
players.note: A towering keeper, around 6ft 6in, who has been Derby County's first choice in the Championship and even picked up a monthly player-of-the-month nomination this season. He wears the number 1 shirt here, but the keeper pecking order is genuinely open.

players.name: H. Ekdal
players.note: A centre-back on Burnley's books who spent part of the past season out on loan in the Netherlands to get regular minutes. He is squad depth in a defence built around Lindelof and Hien, the kind of steady senior option Potter can call on if injuries bite.

players.name: G. Gudmundsson
players.note: Sweden's first-choice left-back, who featured in every qualifying match and had a solid debut Premier League season after joining Leeds from Lille. Energetic going forward, he chipped in his first goal and assist for Leeds in an FA Cup run this spring.

players.name: I. Hien
players.note: A quick, composed centre-back at Italy's Atalanta and one of the pillars of Sweden's defence, likely starting in a back three. He has Champions League experience at club level, though a thigh injury did keep him out of the decisive playoff against Poland.

players.name: G. Lagerbielke
players.note: A central defender who rebuilt his career in Portugal with Braga after a stop-start spell at Celtic, and has chipped in with goals from the back. He scored in the playoff final win over Poland, so he arrives knowing he can produce on the big night.

players.name: V. Lindelöf
players.note: Sweden's captain and most-capped player, a calm, reliable centre-back who spent eight years at Manchester United before moving to Aston Villa. He is the anchor of the defence and the leader Potter leans on, with well over 70 international appearances behind him.

players.name: C. Starfelt
players.note: A no-nonsense centre-back playing regularly for Celta Vigo in Spain, with a season's worth of La Liga and European minutes in his legs. He is firmly in the mix to start alongside Lindelof and Hien if Potter goes with a back three.

players.name: H. Johansson
players.note: An attacking full-back who was part of the Mjallby side that pulled off a fairy tale, winning the club's first ever Swedish league title. That breakthrough campaign earned him a national-team call-up; here he is squad depth on the flank rather than a guaranteed starter.

players.name: E. Smith
players.note: A versatile defender who can also sit in front of the back line as a holding midfielder, playing his club football for St. Pauli in Germany's top flight. He is a relatively new face for Sweden, providing experienced cover across the spine of the team.

players.name: E. Stroud
players.note: A left-sided defender who was named the Swedish league's defender of the year as little Mjallby stunned everyone to win the title. The recognition fast-tracked his first call-ups; this is a big leap up in level, and he is here mainly to add depth and learn.

players.name: D. Svensson
players.note: A young left-back who earned a permanent move to Borussia Dortmund after impressing on loan, and he has racked up real Bundesliga minutes this season. Comfortable pushing forward, he gives Sweden a genuine alternative option down the left.

players.name: A. Bernhardsson
players.note: An attack-minded wide player by trade, now at Holstein Kiel in Germany after coming through with Elfsborg. He is a squad option who offers something different on the flank, more about energy and forward runs than defensive solidity.

players.name: Y. Ayari
players.note: A young, ball-winning central midfielder who broke through at Brighton with a full Premier League season under his belt. Combative and tidy in possession, he is part of a new generation Sweden is building its midfield around for the years ahead.

players.name: L. Bergvall
players.note: One of the brightest young midfielders in Europe and the baby of the squad, already a regular for Tottenham despite his age. He featured in both playoff wins that sent Sweden to the finals, and a tournament like this is the perfect stage for his graceful, press-resistant passing.

players.name: B. Nygren
players.note: An attacking midfielder who had a standout season at Celtic, scoring freely in Scotland and chipping in goals and assists in Europe. He set up two of Sweden's goals on the road to qualification and arrives as one of the squad's in-form creators.

players.name: J. Karlström
players.note: A holding midfielder who captains Italian side Udinese, the kind of disciplined screen who lets the flair players ahead of him take risks. A serial winner of domestic trophies earlier in his career, he brings calm and structure to the centre of the pitch.

players.name: K. Sema
players.note: A hard-running left winger who can also drop in at wing-back, now plying his trade in Cyprus after a long stint at Watford. He won a league title with Pafos and played a part in their first Champions League win, and he even bagged a hat-trick in a Sweden friendly last summer.

players.name: M. Svanberg
players.note: A box-to-box midfielder who has been a regular for Wolfsburg in the Bundesliga and has chipped in with goals this season. Experienced and well-rounded, he offers Potter a dependable senior option in the engine room.

players.name: B. Zeneli
players.note: A young midfielder who broke through with Elfsborg, including European nights, before earning a move abroad in early 2026. He only switched his international allegiance to Sweden recently, so the World Cup is a rapid rise; expect him as squad depth here.

players.name: T. Ali
players.note: A quick, tricky left winger known for his close control and dribbling, the standout creative force at Swedish champions Malmo. A late bloomer at international level, he is one of the squad's more unpredictable attacking options off the bench.

players.name: A. Elanga
players.note: A blisteringly fast right winger who earned a big-money move to Newcastle, the player Sweden look to for running in behind and stretching defences. His debut Premier League season was light on goals but heavy on threat, and his pace makes him a constant counter-attacking weapon.

players.name: V. Gyökeres
players.note: A powerful, relentless centre-forward who racked up astonishing numbers at Sporting before joining Arsenal and topping 20 goals in his debut league season. He was Sweden's playoff hero, scoring four times across the two ties including a hat-trick, and arrives as one of the tournament's most feared finishers.

players.name: A. Isak
players.note: Sweden's marquee striker and The Guardian's pick as their star player, an elegant, lethal finisher who joined Liverpool in a British-record deal. The puzzle for Potter is how to fit Isak and Gyokeres in the same team; together they give Sweden as fearsome a forward line as anyone at the World Cup.

players.name: G. Nilsson
players.note: A tall, old-school target man at Club Brugge, standing nearly 1.96m and a real menace in the air. With Isak and Gyokeres ahead of him, he is a different kind of option off the bench, the man to throw on when Sweden need a focal point and crosses into the box.

players.name: M. Keller
players.note: At 23, Keller is the youngest of Switzerland's three keepers and travels as a backup. He's the regular number one at Young Boys, one of the bigger clubs in Swiss football, so the tournament is about gaining experience behind the established names rather than expecting minutes.

players.name: G. Kobel
players.note: Kobel is Switzerland's number one, having inherited the gloves from the long-serving Yann Sommer in 2024. A commanding presence at Borussia Dortmund, he kept a league-best tally of clean sheets in 2025-26, and that shot-stopping is exactly what the Swiss will lean on in tight knockout games.

players.name: Y. Mvogo
players.note: Mvogo is the experienced third keeper, a 31-year-old who has bounced around Europe with PSV, RB Leipzig and now Lorient in France. He's been a reliable presence in goal at club level, but in this squad he sits behind Kobel and is here mostly for his calm, senior head in the goalkeeping group.

players.name: M. Akanji
players.note: Akanji is the rock at the heart of the Swiss defence and one of their genuine stars. After three trophy-laden years under Pep Guardiola at Manchester City, the 30-year-old became a regular starter at Inter, where his composure on the ball and ability to play out from the back make him the defender everything is built around.

players.name: A. Amenda
players.note: Amenda is a towering 22-year-old centre-back, listed at around 1.94m, who moved from Young Boys to Eintracht Frankfurt and has been linked with bigger clubs across Italy and England. He's squad depth here, learning behind the senior defenders, but his size and physical presence mark him as one for Switzerland's future.

players.name: E. Cömert
players.note: Cömert is a centre-back who has been at Valencia in Spain since 2022, with a recent loan spell at Valladolid for regular minutes. He's been part of the Swiss setup through three major tournaments, so while he's competing for a starting spot here, his familiarity with the squad makes him a dependable defensive option.

players.name: N. Elvedi
players.note: Elvedi has been a fixture at Borussia Mönchengladbach for a decade and is one of the most experienced centre-backs in the Bundesliga. Calm and consistent, the 29-year-old is a likely starter alongside Akanji, giving the Swiss back line a settled, well-drilled core.

players.name: L. Jaquez
players.note: Jaquez is a 22-year-old centre-back who earned a move from Lucerne to VfB Stuttgart, though injuries have slowed his first season in Germany. He's one of the youngest defenders in the squad and travels as depth, here to develop behind the senior players rather than to start.

players.name: M. Muheim
players.note: Muheim is an attack-minded left-back who helped Hamburg win promotion back to the Bundesliga in 2025 and has carried that form into the top flight with a steady run of assists. A relatively late bloomer for the national team, the 27-year-old competes with veteran Ricardo Rodríguez for the left-back berth.

players.name: R. Rodríguez
players.note: Rodríguez is the grand old man of the defence, a left-back with well over 130 caps and a record-holder for tournament appearances with Switzerland. Now 33 and playing at Real Betis after years in Italy and Germany, his experience, set-piece delivery and ability to slot in at centre-back make him invaluable even if his starting days are numbered.

players.name: S. Widmer
players.note: Widmer is the first-choice right-back and a leader at club level, captaining Mainz in the Bundesliga. He started all three group games at Euro 2024, so expect the reliable, hard-running full-back to hold down the right side of Switzerland's defence again here.

players.name: M. Aebischer
players.note: Aebischer is a versatile central midfielder who dropped down to Pisa on loan from Bologna in search of regular minutes after struggling for game time. The 28-year-old is squad depth in a crowded Swiss midfield, valued for his passing range and ability to cover several roles when called upon.

players.name: R. Freuler
players.note: Freuler is a tireless central midfielder who has been a mainstay for club and country for nearly a decade, now plying his trade at Bologna in Serie A. At 33 he's a ball-winner with a tidy passing range, the kind of dependable engine-room presence who helps the Swiss control games.

players.name: A. Jashari
players.note: Jashari is one of Switzerland's most exciting young midfielders, a 23-year-old who earned a big-money move to AC Milan after winning Player of the Year honours in Belgium with Club Brugge. A broken leg wrecked much of his first Milan season, so the World Cup is a chance to show the form that made him so coveted.

players.name: D. Sow
players.note: Sow is a defensive midfielder who has rediscovered his goal touch at Sevilla, chipping in with a useful handful of strikes in La Liga this season. The 28-year-old offers the Swiss a physical, box-to-box option in the middle and gives Yakin a different profile alongside the deeper-lying holders.

players.name: G. Xhaka
players.note: Xhaka is the captain and the heartbeat of this team, a deep-lying playmaker dictating tempo from in front of the defence. After captaining Bayer Leverkusen to a league-and-cup double, he took the surprising step of joining promoted Sunderland, where he wears the armband too. This is his fourth straight World Cup, and Switzerland goes as far as he drives them.

players.name: D. Zakaria
players.note: Zakaria is a powerful, athletic midfielder who captains Monaco and partners Xhaka in the Swiss engine room. He chips in with goals and drives forward with the ball, though an adductor injury disrupted his club season, so his sharpness coming into the tournament is one to watch.

players.name: C. Fassnacht
players.note: Fassnacht is a right winger who returned home to Young Boys after a spell at Norwich City, and that move helped revive his international career after more than two years away from the squad. At 32, he's a useful attacking option off the bench, bringing directness and goal threat from wide areas.

players.name: C. Itten
players.note: Itten is a target-man striker who has been banging in goals for Fortuna Düsseldorf in Germany's second tier, where his aerial strength and finishing make him a real handful. He's a squad option here for late-game situations when Switzerland needs a focal point up top to chase a result.

players.name: F. Rieder
players.note: Rieder is a creative attacking midfielder whose career got back on track in Germany after a tricky spell in France, winning the German Cup before joining Augsburg. At 23 he offers Switzerland passing and vision from the middle, a tidy option to unlock defences when games get stubborn.

players.name: R. Vargas
players.note: Vargas is a direct, quick winger who left a six-year stint at Augsburg to take on a new challenge at Sevilla. The 27-year-old likes to cut inside and shoot, and his pace gives Switzerland a way to stretch tiring defences, making him a strong candidate to start or change games out wide.

players.name: Z. Amdouni
players.note: Amdouni is a flexible forward who can lead the line or play just behind, and he showed his quality on loan at Benfica with goals against Champions League heavyweights. The 25-year-old gives Switzerland a mobile, technical attacking option, competing for minutes in a forward line with several strong choices.

players.name: B. Embolo
players.note: Embolo is Switzerland's main centre-forward, a strong, mobile striker who scored at the last World Cup and racked up goals over three seasons at Monaco before moving to Rennes. At 28 he combines power with link-up play, and the Swiss will look to him as their most reliable source of goals up front.

players.name: J. Manzambi
players.note: Manzambi is the breakout name, a 20-year-old from Geneva who was named the revelation of the 2025-26 Europa League after starring in Freiburg's run to the final. An energetic, box-to-box talent who already has a goal for the senior side, he is one of the youngest in the squad and an exciting wildcard going into the tournament.

players.name: N. Okafor
players.note: Okafor is a quick, versatile forward who won a Serie A title on loan with Napoli before joining Leeds in a big-money move to the Premier League. The 25-year-old can play across the front line, and his pace and finishing, including a memorable brace at Old Trafford, give Switzerland a dangerous attacking option.

players.name: D. Ndoye
players.note: Ndoye is one of Switzerland's brightest attackers, a winger who scored the goal that won Bologna their first Coppa Italia in 51 years before a big move to Nottingham Forest. At 25 his pace, dribbling and end product make him a key creative threat, and he is the kind of player who can decide a knockout tie on his own.

players.name: S. Ben Hsan
players.note: A 29-year-old keeper for Etoile du Sahel in the Tunisian league, here as a backup option behind the established names. He moved to Etoile in 2025 and is likelier to watch from the bench than to play.

players.name: C. Abdelmouhib
players.note: A 24-year-old who was the first-choice keeper as Club Africain won the Tunisian league title, which is a strong year for someone his age. He wears the number 1 shirt here but is competing with a more capped goalkeeper for the actual starting spot.

players.name: A. Dahmen
players.note: Tunisia's expected number one despite wearing 16, with around 37 caps and a steady home-league season at his boyhood club CS Sfaxien. Calm and well-drilled, he is the keeper Lamouchi trusts to anchor the defence.

players.name: A. Abdi
players.note: A 32-year-old left-back at Ligue 1 side Nice and one of Tunisia's more experienced full-backs. He pushes forward to support attacks, so expect him overlapping down the left when Tunisia have the ball.

players.name: A. Arous
players.note: A tall, 21-year-old centre-back who broke through this season at Turkish club Kasimpasa and earned his first Tunisia caps in early 2026. A breakout year has drawn interest from bigger clubs, and this tournament is his chance to keep rising.

players.name: A. Ben Hmida
players.note: A left-back from Esperance de Tunis, the biggest club in the domestic league, providing depth and cover on the left side. At 30 he brings plenty of experience even if he is not nailed-on to start.

players.name: D. Bronn
players.note: A vastly experienced centre-back, now at Swiss side Servette, who famously scored against Belgium at the 2018 World Cup. With more than 40 caps he is a calming, senior presence in the back line.

players.name: R. Chikhaoui
players.note: A 21-year-old defender from US Monastir who only recently earned his first senior cap, included here mostly to develop and add depth. Tall and still raw, he is one for the future rather than the starting eleven.

players.name: M. Neffati
players.note: A 21-year-old defender plying his trade in Sweden with IFK Norrkoping, one of the squad's younger and less-established names. He is here to gain tournament experience rather than to feature heavily.

players.name: O. Rekik
players.note: A 24-year-old centre-back, Dutch-born and a former Arsenal academy product, now settled at Slovenian club Maribor. After years of loans he has found regular football, which is what brought him into the Tunisia squad.

players.name: M. Talbi
players.note: A near-ever-present centre-back for Ligue 1 club Lorient and the cornerstone of Tunisia's defence. Tall and strong in the air, he wins the majority of his aerial duels, exactly what you want against the bigger forwards in Group F.

players.name: Y. Valery
players.note: Tunisia's likely starting right-back, a France-born defender who came up through Southampton before settling in English football. He brings the energy to get up and down the right flank throughout a game.

players.name: M. Ben Ouanes
players.note: A 31-year-old full-back who has been a regular at Turkish club Kasimpasa for several years. Versatile enough to cover either flank, he offers reliable, experienced cover off the bench.

players.name: K. Ayari
players.note: A 20-year-old talent on the books at Paris Saint-Germain, where he has been working with the academy and reserve setup. Calling him up is a bet on his potential, so he is here to learn more than to start.

players.name: Ismaël Gharbi
players.note: A creative midfielder who grew up in PSG's academy alongside the likes of Messi and Mbappe, now on loan at Bundesliga side Augsburg. He only switched his international allegiance to Tunisia in 2025 and gives the side a touch of flair in possession.

players.name: R. Khedira
players.note: A 31-year-old holding midfielder for Bundesliga club Union Berlin and the younger brother of former Germany star Sami Khedira. He only switched to Tunisia in 2026 but is expected to slot straight into the starting midfield as a screen in front of the defence.

players.name: H. Mejbri
players.note: Tunisia's number 10 and the team's main spark, a combative former Manchester United youngster now playing his football at Burnley. The Guardian's pick as the squad's standout, he is the player most likely to make something happen in the final third.

players.name: E. Skhiri
players.note: The captain and Tunisia's most-capped player, a tireless box-to-box midfielder at Bundesliga club Eintracht Frankfurt. He has been a first-choice starter for over a decade and is the engine the whole team is built around.

players.name: A. Ben Slimane
players.note: A 24-year-old, Denmark-born midfielder at Norwich whose strong end to the season earned him this call-up after a long injury layoff earlier in the campaign. He adds physicality and depth to the engine room.

players.name: H. Mahmoud
players.note: A 25-year-old midfielder at Swiss club Lugano, one of the squad's lesser-known names brought in to add options in the middle of the park. He is more likely to feature in rotation than to be a guaranteed starter.

players.name: S. Tounekti
