players.note: A direct, 23-year-old winger who earned a multi-million-pound move to Celtic in 2025 after impressing in Sweden. Primarily a left winger who can switch sides, he gives Tunisia genuine pace and one-on-one threat out wide.

players.name: E. Achouri
players.note: Tunisia's main wide attacking threat, a left winger at FC Copenhagen with regular Champions League minutes under his belt. He chips in with goals and assists and brings real European pedigree to the front line.

players.name: F. Chaouat
players.note: A 29-year-old striker in red-hot domestic form, leading the Tunisian league scoring charts for Club Africain including a derby hat-trick this season. After years abroad he is the in-form home-based forward Tunisia hope can finish chances at the tournament.

players.name: R. Elloumi
players.note: At 18 the youngest member of the squad, a forward who became the first Vancouver Whitecaps academy graduate to score on his home MLS debut. He committed to Tunisia in late 2025 and is a thrilling prospect along for the experience.

players.name: H. Mastouri
players.note: A 28-year-old striker wearing the number 9, now playing in the Russian top flight with Dinamo Makhachkala after a late-blooming international rise. He is a squad forward option rather than a guaranteed starter up top.

players.name: E. Saad
players.note: A German-born left winger who made his name winning promotion with St Pauli and now plays in the German second tier with Hannover 96. He offers an extra wide attacking option and the kind of direct running that stretches defences.

players.name: A. Bayindir
players.note: Bayindir spent the season as a backup at Manchester United and goes into the tournament as Turkiye's likely second-choice keeper. He brings top-flight experience even if regular minutes have been hard to come by at club level.

players.name: U. Çakir
players.note: Cakir is expected to be Turkiye's number one between the posts, having become the country's most expensive transfer when Galatasaray signed him. He was the regular keeper during the run to the Euro 2024 quarter-finals, so he arrives as the settled choice.

players.name: M. Günok
players.note: At 36, Gunok is the elder statesman of the goalkeeping group and a likely back-up here, but he is the man who pulled off that astonishing last-gasp save against Austria to send Turkiye into the Euro 2024 quarter-finals. His experience and calm are worth having on the bench.

players.name: S. Akaydin
players.note: Akaydin is a centre-back who plays his club football at Rizespor and offers squad depth at the back. He scored against the Netherlands in Turkiye's Euro 2024 quarter-final, so he has form for popping up with a goal on the big stage.

players.name: A. Bardakci
players.note: Bardakci is a left-footed centre-back who has been a steady presence in Galatasaray's title-winning defence. He gives Turkiye a calm, ball-playing option in the middle of the back line.

players.name: Z. Çelik
players.note: Celik is a right-back who has clocked up well over 100 games for Roma in Serie A and is Turkiye's experienced option on that flank. He defends solidly and can shuffle inside to centre-back when needed.

players.name: M. Demiral
players.note: Demiral is the leader of Turkiye's defence, a physical centre-back who now plays in Saudi Arabia for Al-Ahli after spells with Juventus and Atalanta. He scored both goals against Austria at Euro 2024 and is dangerous from set pieces at either end.

players.name: E. Elmali
players.note: Elmali is an attacking left-back who chipped in with goals from defence during Galatasaray's title campaign. He competes for the left-back slot and offers an outlet getting forward down that side.

players.name: O. Kabak
players.note: Kabak is a centre-back who rebuilt his career at Hoffenheim after a frustrating spell on the sidelines, working his way back into the Bundesliga side and the national team. He even adds the odd goal, having found the net a few times in the German top flight this season.

players.name: F. Kadioglu
players.note: Kadioglu is a versatile full-back who was voted Brighton's player of the season after shaking off an earlier injury, and he played every minute of Turkiye's run to the Euro 2024 last eight. Dutch-born, he chose Turkiye and is now a first-choice down the left.

players.name: M. Müldür
players.note: Muldur is a right-back at Fenerbahce, born and raised in Vienna before choosing Turkiye. His thumping volley against Georgia was voted the goal of Euro 2024, so he is a full-back who can produce a moment out of nothing.

players.name: Ç. Söyüncü
players.note: Soyuncu is an experienced centre-back who made his name in the Premier League with Leicester before returning home to Fenerbahce. With more than 50 caps, he is a senior figure competing for a starting spot alongside Demiral.

players.name: H. Çalhanoglu
players.note: Calhanoglu is the captain and the heartbeat of this team, a deep-lying midfielder at Inter who controls the tempo, takes the set pieces and rarely misses from the penalty spot. With more than 100 caps, he is the most experienced player in the squad and the one who pulls the strings.

players.name: K. Ayhan
players.note: Ayhan is a useful utility man for Galatasaray who can fill in at centre-back or sit in midfield, which makes him handy depth for Montella. Germany-born, he has been a regular squad member for years and gives the coach tactical flexibility.

players.name: O. Kokçu
players.note: Kokcu is a technical central midfielder who captains Besiktas, the club he supported as a boy, after turning down bigger offers to join them. Dutch-born and developed at Feyenoord, he passes well and arrives late into the box, giving Turkiye creativity in the middle.

players.name: S. Özcan
players.note: Ozcan is a defensive midfielder at Borussia Dortmund, the kind of player who shields the back four and keeps things simple. Germany-born, he scored his first international goal against Spain in qualifying, a memorable moment in an otherwise low-key role.

players.name: I. Yüksek
players.note: Yuksek is a powerful, hard-running central midfielder at Fenerbahce who does the unglamorous work of breaking up play and carrying the ball forward. He scored in a derby win over Besiktas this season and offers energy in the engine room.

players.name: C. Uzun
players.note: Uzun is a 20-year-old attacking talent who has caught the eye at Eintracht Frankfurt, chipping in with goals and assists in the Bundesliga and Champions League. Germany-born, he chose Turkiye and is one of the bright young pieces of this golden generation.

players.name: O. Aydin
players.note: Aydin is a direct, pacey winger at Fenerbahce who made a splash early on by scoring twice within minutes of an early start for the club. He is a squad option out wide, the type to change a game off the bench with his running.

players.name: A. Güler
players.note: Guler is the jewel of this side, a 20-year-old playmaker who finally broke through at Real Madrid this season as their creative number 10 under Xabi Alonso and was named the Champions League's breakthrough player. The Guardian's pick as Turkiye's star man, he is the one to watch with the ball at his feet.

players.name: Y. Akgün
players.note: Akgun is a Galatasaray academy product who plays as an attacking midfielder or right winger and has grown into a key man at the club. Quick and tricky, he gives Turkiye another option to unlock defences from wide areas.

players.name: K. Aktürkoglu
players.note: Akturkoglu is a direct left-sided winger who returned to Turkiye with Fenerbahce after a spell at Benfica and has been among the goals since. A regular for the national team, he stretches play and cuts inside to shoot, making him one of Montella's main attacking threats.

players.name: D. Gül
players.note: Gul is a 21-year-old centre-forward at Porto, born in Stockholm to a Turkish father and Swedish mother, who switched his allegiance to Turkiye and marked his debut by scoring against Spain in qualifying. He is a developing striking option rather than a guaranteed starter.

players.name: I. Kahveci
players.note: Kahveci is an experienced attacking midfielder with an eye for a spectacular goal, playing his football at Kasimpasa this season. At 30 he brings know-how and a long-range threat as a squad option in the final third.

players.name: K. Yildiz
players.note: Yildiz is a 20-year-old forward who wears Juventus's famous number 10 and was named Serie A's best under-23 player this season. Germany-born but committed to Turkiye, he scores and creates from the left and forms the spearhead of the attack alongside Guler.

players.name: B. Yilmaz
players.note: Baris Alper Yilmaz is a strong, quick wide forward who has been a key part of Galatasaray's run of league titles, weighing in with goals and a healthy number of assists this season. His physicality and pace make him a handful down either flank for Turkiye.

players.name: S. Mele
players.note: A 28-year-old goalkeeper who built his name in South American club football, Mele is here as one of the deeper options behind Bielsa's first-choice keeper. Expect him to spend the tournament training and on the bench rather than starting.

players.name: F. Muslera
players.note: At 39 the grand old man of the squad, Muslera was Uruguay's undisputed No. 1 at the last three World Cups before stepping back. He returns as a senior backup and dressing-room steadier, set to feature in his fifth World Cup, a feat very few players have ever managed.

players.name: S. Rochet
players.note: The 32-year-old who wears the No. 1 shirt and is Bielsa's expected starter in goal, sharpened by regular Brazilian top-flight football with Internacional. Calm with the ball at his feet, he is the man Uruguay will lean on to launch attacks from the back.

players.name: R. Araújo
players.note: Barcelona's centre-back and one of Uruguay's defensive cornerstones, the 26-year-old combines raw pace with the kind of last-ditch tackling that lets a back line sit higher. Watch for whether he shakes off a minor pre-tournament muscle knock, because Uruguay are a far harder team to break down with him in it.

players.name: S. Bueno
players.note: A 27-year-old centre-back who has logged his heaviest workload yet in English football with Wolves, making him a credible squad option in central defence. He is more likely to provide cover and rotation than to be guaranteed a starting spot.

players.name: S. Cáceres
players.note: A 26-year-old centre-back who has spent years anchoring the defence at Club America in Mexico, earning most of his caps during the recent World Cup qualifying run. He offers reliable depth in the heart of Bielsa's back line.

players.name: J. Giménez
players.note: Uruguay's captain and a centre-back hardened by years of Atletico Madrid's no-nonsense defending, the 30-year-old leads the back line and reads danger before it arrives. He sets the tone for a side that still treats its own goal as something close to sacred.

players.name: M. Olivera
players.note: A 28-year-old left-back who has won Serie A titles with Napoli, comfortable defending one-on-one and overlapping down the flank. He is in the mix to start at left-back, where his big-match experience in Italy gives Bielsa a steady option.

players.name: G. Varela
players.note: A 32-year-old right-back who came through Manchester United's ranks as a teenager and has since found his level as a regular for Flamengo in Brazil. An experienced full-back, he offers Uruguay cover and competition on the right side of defence.

players.name: M. Viña
players.note: A 28-year-old left-back whose career was interrupted by a serious knee injury in 2024 that needed major surgery, before he fought his way back to fitness through 2025. Reaching this squad at all is a comeback story, and he provides experienced depth at left-back.

players.name: R. Bentancur
players.note: Tottenham's midfield metronome and, at 28, heading into his third World Cup with more than 70 caps to his name. He breaks up play and then keeps the ball moving, the unshowy hub that lets the flashier names around him take risks.

players.name: E. Martínez
players.note: A 26-year-old defensive midfielder who anchored a Palmeiras side that chased the Brazilian title, doing the quiet shielding work in front of the back four. He gives Bielsa another holding option if Uruguay want extra protection in midfield.

players.name: J. Sanabria
players.note: A versatile 25-year-old who operates down the left, equally able to defend as a full-back or push on as a wide midfielder after years of regular football in Mexico's top flight. That flexibility is exactly why Bielsa values him as squad cover.

players.name: M. Ugarte
players.note: At 24 the youngest of Uruguay's key midfielders, a ball-winning specialist at Manchester United whose whole game is snapping into tackles and cutting out passes. If Uruguay want to suffocate a stronger opponent, he is the player who makes that possible.

players.name: F. Valverde
players.note: Uruguay's standout name and the engine of the team, a Real Madrid midfielder who covers absurd amounts of ground and strikes the ball ferociously from distance, including his first career hat-trick against Manchester City this season. At 27 and in his prime, he is the player opponents must plan around.

players.name: R. Zalazar
players.note: A 26-year-old attacking midfielder who had a breakout scoring season at Braga in Portugal, racking up goals from the No. 10 role and earning a big-money move on the back of it. He gives Bielsa creativity and a goal threat off the bench.

players.name: G. de Arrascaeta
players.note: Uruguay's chief playmaker and, at 31, the reigning South American Footballer of the Year after a glittering season at Flamengo. He carries a calf injury into the tournament, so the question is less whether he can unlock defences and more about when in the competition he will be fit to do it.

players.name: N. de la Cruz
players.note: A 28-year-old midfielder who plays alongside de Arrascaeta at Flamengo, so the two arrive with a built-in understanding. Left-footed and inventive, he can drift between the lines and may become more important if his club teammate's fitness wavers.

players.name: M. Araújo
players.note: A 25-year-old left-sided player at Sporting in Portugal who can fill in at left-back or bomb forward as a winger, with a Champions League goal against Manchester City already on his CV. That two-way profile makes him a useful tactical wildcard down the left.

players.name: A. Canobbio
players.note: A 27-year-old winger who has been among Fluminense's sharper attackers this season, chipping in goals from wide and carrying the ball directly at defenders. He gives Bielsa fresh legs and width to change a game from the bench.

players.name: R. Aguirre
players.note: A 31-year-old striker who earned his Uruguay call-up off a strong run of form in Mexican football and marked his international debut by scoring a winner in a qualifier against Colombia. He is a backup centre-forward here, the kind of physical presence to throw on late when chasing a goal.

players.name: J. Piquerez
players.note: Despite being grouped with the attackers, the 27-year-old is really an attack-minded left-back for Palmeiras who loves getting forward. Watch for his recovery from an ankle injury picked up on Uruguay duty, because fit and firing he is a genuine starting option down the left.

players.name: D. Núñez
players.note: Uruguay's spearhead, a 26-year-old striker all raw pace, power and chaos who terrifies defenders even when his finishing runs hot and cold. After a former spell in the Premier League with Liverpool and a move to Saudi club football, the World Cup is his stage to lead the line and turn half-chances into goals.

players.name: F. Pellistri
players.note: A 24-year-old winger, once a Manchester United prospect, who is now getting regular minutes at Panathinaikos in Greece. Quick and direct on the right, he is squad depth out wide and a useful change-of-pace option off the bench.

players.name: B. Rodríguez
players.note: A 25-year-old winger who finally became an undisputed starter at Club America this season, repaying the trust with a healthy haul of goals and assists. Direct and tricky, he is pushing to be more than just a squad option in Uruguay's wide areas.

players.name: F. Viñas
players.note: A 27-year-old centre-forward who hit a steady run of goals for Oviedo in Spain's top flight this season, which is what earned him a place. He is a backup striker option, the sort of penalty-box poacher Bielsa can call on to chase a goal late.

players.name: C. Brady
players.note: The youngest of the three keepers and the first homegrown player Chicago Fire have ever sent to a World Cup. He's here mostly to learn from the older two, but at 21 the future net is probably his.

players.name: M. Freese
players.note: He wrote a college research paper on penalty kicks, then put it to use by saving three in a Gold Cup shootout against Costa Rica. Those saves turned him from backup into the man most likely to start in goal at a home World Cup.

players.name: M. Turner
players.note: He played every minute of the 2022 World Cup in goal, spent a few years in England, then came home to New England to rebuild his form. This time he arrives as the experienced head rather than the guaranteed starter.

players.name: S. Dest
players.note: An attacking full-back who came up through Barcelona's academy before settling in the Netherlands with PSV. He defends like he'd rather be galloping forward, which is both his charm and his risk.

players.name: A. Freeman
players.note: The youngest man in the squad and the son of Super Bowl-winning receiver Antonio Freeman, so the athletic genes were never in doubt. A flying right-back who climbed every rung of Orlando's academy before forcing his way into the picture.

players.name: M. McKenzie
players.note: A calm, ball-playing centre-back from Delaware who has quietly made himself a regular in France's top flight with Toulouse. The kind of defender you only notice when he's missing.

players.name: T. Ream
players.note: At 38 he's comfortably the oldest player in the squad and wears the captain's armband, the steady veteran voice marshalling a young back line. He left the Premier League to come home to Charlotte but never gave up his spot for the U.S.

players.name: C. Richards
players.note: He anchored Crystal Palace's defence as they beat Manchester City to win their first major trophy, the 2025 FA Cup, then was named U.S. Soccer's Player of the Year. The Alabama-born centre-back has gone from promising prospect to the squad's most reliable defender.

players.name: A. Robinson
players.note: A left-back at Fulham who is genuinely one of the quickest defenders in the Premier League, forever sprinting back to clean up trouble. His overlapping runs are a big part of how the U.S. attacks down that flank.

players.name: M. Robinson
players.note: A powerful, recovery-fast centre-back at FC Cincinnati who came back from a torn Achilles to keep his national-team place. Between him and Tim Ream, this defensive pairing has racked up well over 100 caps.

players.name: J. Scally
players.note: A New York-raised full-back who moved to Germany as a teenager and has been a Bundesliga regular at Mönchengladbach ever since. Comfortable down either flank, which makes him a useful spare part to have on the bench.

players.name: A. Trusty
players.note: A Pennsylvania-born centre-back who just won the Scottish league title with Celtic and is heading to his first World Cup. A late bloomer who keeps quietly answering every question asked of him.

players.name: M. Arfsten
players.note: A wing-back at Columbus Crew who brings pace and a willingness to get forward and create. One of the home-grown MLS picks Pochettino trusts to stretch a defence down the left.

players.name: S. Berhalter
players.note: His father Gregg used to coach this team, so playing at the World Cup makes them only the second father-son pair to represent the U.S. there. He earned the call on his own merit after a breakout year setting up goals for Vancouver.

players.name: W. McKennie
players.note: The all-action engine of the midfield, a Texan who has spent years at Juventus and will play almost any role he's handed, from box-crashing runner to emergency full-back. Often described as the heart of this team, and he plays like it.

players.name: G. Reyna
players.note: Son of former U.S. captain Claudio Reyna and blessed with a left foot that can unlock any defence, when his body cooperates. A run of injuries stalled his Dortmund career, so a fresh start at Mönchengladbach was meant to get him back to the World Cup, and it did.

players.name: C. Roldan
players.note: A tireless, do-the-dirty-work midfielder who has spent his whole career at Seattle and just made the league's best eleven. He's the only player here who was an active MLS man at both the 2022 World Cup and this one.

players.name: M. Tillman
players.note: A smooth attacking midfielder who earned a club-record move to Bayer Leverkusen after starring in the Netherlands. He was the U.S.'s standout at the 2025 Gold Cup, and on his day he glides past people like the game is in slow motion.

players.name: T. Adams
players.note: The team's main holding midfielder, the one who breaks up attacks and tidies up before anyone realises there was danger. He's the only natural ball-winner of his type in the squad, so a lot rests on him staying fit after a strong season at Bournemouth.

players.name: T. Weah
players.note: Son of George Weah, the only African ever to win the Ballon d'Or and later president of Liberia, so the surname carries weight. Tim is a quick, hard-running wide forward at Marseille, and he was one of just three Americans to score at the 2022 World Cup.

players.name: A. Zendejas
players.note: A tricky winger who stars for Club America in Mexico and could have played for Mexico himself before committing to the U.S. He'd been out of the picture for a while, but a hot end to the Liga MX season earned him a late ticket onto the plane.

players.name: B. Aaronson
players.note: A high-energy attacking midfielder at Leeds whose game is built on pressing and pestering opponents into mistakes. Nicknamed the Medford Messi back home in New Jersey, a tag he carries with a grin rather than any real pressure.

players.name: F. Balogun
players.note: Born in New York, raised in London and an Arsenal academy product, he chose the U.S. over England and France. After a 19-goal season for Monaco, including a long late-season scoring run, he looks like the centre-forward this team has been waiting for.

players.name: R. Pepi
players.note: A poacher's poacher who scored 19 goals to lead PSV to another Dutch title, despite missing a chunk of the season injured. He once briefly switched allegiance toward Mexico before settling firmly with the U.S., and now he's the lively alternative to Balogun up front.

players.name: C. Pulisic
players.note: The face of American soccer, nicknamed Captain America, and the most-capped, most relied-upon player in the squad. He keeps rewriting U.S. record books while starring for AC Milan, and if anyone is going to win a knockout game on his own, it's him.

players.name: H. Wright
players.note: A big, physical forward who scored 17 goals to help fire Coventry to promotion to the Premier League. He took a long road through Turkey and the lower leagues to get here, and he was one of only three Americans to score at the last World Cup.

players.name: B. Ergashev
players.note: Neftchi Fergana's keeper is here as a backup option, with only a handful of caps to his name. At 1.92m he's a big presence in the box, but at this tournament he'll most likely be watching from the bench while the senior keeper plays.

players.name: A. Nematov
players.note: A young goalkeeper from Nasaf who has already won a best-keeper award at U23 level and played at the Paris Olympics. He's one of the most valued players in Uzbekistan's domestic league, but on this squad he sits behind the established number one and is more about the future than starting now.

players.name: U. Yusupov
players.note: Uzbekistan's first-choice goalkeeper, the 34-year-old plays his club football in Iran for Foolad and racked up a dozen clean sheets last season. With more than 40 caps, he's the steady, experienced hand expected to start in goal at the country's debut World Cup.

players.name: K. Alijonov
players.note: Pakhtakor's right-back is a regular for the national team and a serial trophy-winner at club level, having collected a stack of Uzbek league and cup titles. Reliable and experienced, he's a strong candidate to start down the right side of the defence.

players.name: R. Ashurmatov
players.note: A centre-back who has built his career across Russia, South Korea and now Iran with Esteghlal, he won an Asian U23 title with Uzbekistan back in 2018. Expect him to be in the conversation for a starting spot in the middle of the back line.

players.name: U. Eshmurodov
players.note: An experienced centre-back at Nasaf, the 33-year-old offers height and steadiness rather than flash. He's squad depth at this World Cup, the kind of seasoned defender a coach is glad to have on the bench if injuries or suspensions bite.

players.name: B. Karimov
players.note: At 18, this Surkhon right-back is one of the youngest players in the whole tournament, earning his place after a breakout domestic season. A leg fracture in the spring clouded his build-up, so realistically he's here to learn and soak up the experience rather than start.

players.name: A. Khusanov
players.note: The crown jewel of this squad: the first Uzbek to play in the Premier League, he joined Manchester City in early 2025 and has already won the League Cup and FA Cup. Quick and composed for a defender just 21, he anchors the back line and is the player most opponents will have circled.

players.name: S. Nasrullayev
players.note: A left-back who came through at Nasaf and helped them win a run of domestic cups. He's been part of the national-team picture for a few years and gives the squad a useful option on the left, though he may have to settle for a backup role here.

players.name: F. Sayfiev
players.note: At 34, this left-back is one of the squad's elder statesmen, with more than 60 caps and a move to Neftchi in 2025. Left-footed and versatile across the back line, he brings experience and tactical know-how whether he starts or comes off the bench.

players.name: J. Urozov
players.note: A young left-back at Dinamo Samarqand who only made his senior international debut in early 2026. He's squad depth at this tournament, one of the developing defenders Cannavaro is blooding for the years ahead rather than relying on now.

players.name: A. Abdullaev
players.note: A defender who can also screen midfield, he has bounced between Uzbek clubs and the UAE, now turning out for Dibba. With a modest cap tally he's more of a depth option here, valued for his versatility across defence.

players.name: A. Ulmasaliev
players.note: A centre-back at Olmaliq (AGMK) who was part of the 2025 CAFA Nations Cup-winning squad. He provides cover in the middle of the defence and is likely to feature as backup rather than a guaranteed starter at this World Cup.

players.name: J. Masharipov
players.note: A creative left winger and one of the team's most capped attacking players, he plays his club football in Iran. The cloud over him is fitness: a serious knee injury kept him out for much of the season, so how sharp he is could decide whether he's a starter or an impact option.

players.name: A. Ganiyev
players.note: A defensive-minded midfielder now playing in the UAE with Al Bataeh, he won league titles early in his career at Nasaf and later collected silverware in Dubai. On this squad he's a depth option in central midfield rather than a nailed-on starter.

players.name: J. Iskanderov
players.note: An experienced midfielder at Neftchi who is one of the squad's senior figures. At 32 he brings calm and game-management in the middle of the park, and is exactly the kind of steady head a team leans on at a first World Cup.

players.name: O. Hamrobekov
players.note: A central midfielder who has played for Bunyodkor and abroad, with a good chunk of caps and a few international goals. He's competing for minutes in a crowded midfield and is likely to be used as a rotation or impact option here.

players.name: A. Mozgovoy
players.note: An attacking midfielder of mixed Uzbek-Russian heritage who has come through clubs including Nasaf, he offers craft in the final third. He's squad depth at this tournament, a creative option to bring on rather than an automatic starter.

players.name: O. Shukurov
players.note: One of the team's leaders and a regular starter in central midfield, the Baniyas man does the unglamorous work: breaking up play, shielding the defence and keeping the ball moving. With more than 70 caps, he's a likely fixture in the engine room.

players.name: A. Fayzullaev
players.note: Uzbekistan's brightest young creator, an attacking midfielder who was the breakout star of the 2024 Asian Cup before a club-record move to Istanbul Basaksehir. At 22 he's the imagination of this team, the player expected to unlock defences and the one neutrals should watch.

players.name: S. Esanov
players.note: A young central midfielder who only joined Bukhara in early 2026, he's among the least experienced names in the squad. Realistically he's here for the experience and squad balance rather than to start, a prospect getting an early taste of the big stage.

players.name: O. Orunov
players.note: A pacey left winger now at Persepolis in Iran, known for his dribbling and his eye for goal from wide areas after a prolific spell in the Uzbek league. He gives the attack a direct, run-at-defenders option, whether from the start or off the bench.

players.name: D. Khamdamov
players.note: A right winger and former Asian young-player-of-the-year who has been a Pakhtakor mainstay. Tricky and direct, he's a genuine attacking weapon for Uzbekistan and pushes hard for a place in the front line, even if competition for those spots is fierce.

players.name: A. Amonov
players.note: A centre-forward who has played across the Uzbek league, the UAE and Iran, now back at Bunyodkor. He's a backup striking option behind the established names up front, the sort of forward brought on to chase a game late.

players.name: I. Sergeev
players.note: A veteran striker with more than 80 caps who once topped the Uzbek league scoring charts and finished as top scorer of an Asian U19 tournament as a teenager. Now at Persepolis, the 32-year-old is the experienced foil and backup to the captain in attack.

players.name: E. Shomurodov
players.note: The captain, all-time leading scorer and emotional heart of the team, he led Uzbekistan to its first-ever World Cup. After spells with Genoa and Roma in Italy, he plundered goals on loan at Basaksehir, and as the focal point of the attack he'll carry the country's hopes up front.
